known.title: Canonical two-colour recognition and its relative filler scopes
known.text: Over a characteristic-zero field on the affine line, an actual pointed coalgebra action on the two-idempotent factorizing system gives the rooted branch homotopies and a colour-diagonal projector at every arity. The rooted linear-diagram comparison retains the ordered collision maps and kills the primary unmixed two-vacuum class; the uniform-source secondary class \(\ell\rho^{\prime}\) remains. The constructed simultaneous pure-wall insertions for \(P(M,M^{\prime})\star D\), with arbitrary differential modules, connected factorizing \(D\) and canonical all-vacuum pointing, give underlying coefficient nullity at every arity except for the canonical all-vacuum \(P\)/no-\(D\) component fixed by the pointing. A separate arity-four argument kills the common mixed-source winding for arbitrary unbounded singleton objects. If the normalized singleton is constant and has an actual global propagating insertion with its prescribed vacuum-first cut comparison, the mixed-source binary relative filler exists with the fixed singleton path, one designated ordered cut and both collision branches. The exterior actor \(\Lambda(\xi)\), \(|\xi|=1\), has a discrete \(k^2\) torsor of final binary fillers. Full recognition is established for every coherent coassociative pointing on the native Chevalley actor of an arbitrary unbounded genuine-unit dg chiral algebra, with all ordered higher cells and parameter spaces retained. The exact radical projection extends this to every pointing in the stated module-radical family. Actual split inactive-summand excision and constant nonunital unitization give further complete domains. The displayed \(k^2\) filler torsor and nonzero secondary belong to their specified different recipients. For three disjoint nonempty wrong-colour blocks, fix the root and two marks. The discrepancy of the action on this word has a primitive with the prescribed pointing. For two differently coloured singletons with output of the second colour, a supplied coherent cocommutative structure on the actor also compares the prescribed primitives at both endpoints away from the old collision. The general root and cut refinements and recognition for arbitrary coassociative actors remain open.

known.title: Surjective base change and the tame cocycle subcategory
known.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), retain the nonzero-level rank-one Heisenberg boundary, the exterior actor \(B=\Lambda(\epsilon)\) with \(|\epsilon|=1\) and \(d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0\), ordinary algebraic tensors and localization at state quasi-isomorphisms. For a surjective base arrow \(a:d\to d^{\prime}\) in the specified Heisenberg action comparison, let \(G_d^a\) be the full subcategory where the dg vertex ideal generated by \(h(\ker a)\) is acyclic. Quotienting by that ideal proves \[N G_{d^{\prime}}\simeq N G_d^a,\] preserving both cocycle legs, all refinements and every admissible target link. A base section retracts the full transition and makes it injective on components and all based homotopy groups. The displayed split object and specified pullbacks are tame. The remaining inclusion \(N G_d^a\to N G_d\) is still undecided, including higher homotopy even if every component meets the tame subcategory. Actual mapping paths and finite matching pullbacks show that objectwise incoming tame coverage is sufficient for the full split nerve comparison, without a global selecting functor. That coverage must include the constructed matching-limit roofs and remains unproved. Every arbitrary base arrow factors through a surjective one with the other factor inducing a nerve homotopy equivalence, so the remaining base-transition problem reduces to surjective arrows. Relative free/PBW exactness is one possible method; the ideal-valued monotonicity test only excludes outgoing arrows to tame objects. The full nilpotent inclusion and strict-coslice comparison remain open. The genuine comparison \(q_B\), including its unit homotopy, is established for a single degree-one exterior generator on the nonzero-level rank-one boundary.

known.title: The derived mapping space out of any finite exterior source
known.text: Let \(A=\Lambda(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r)\) have degree-one generators and zero differential and translation. For every finite \(r\ge1\) and arbitrary unbounded ordinary algebraic dg vertex target, the derived mapping space has two coordinates for each nonempty subset \(I\) of the generators. Their degrees are \(2-|I|\) and \(1-|I|\). For a singleton the equations say that its first coordinate \(a_i\) is closed and its second \(s_i\) obeys \(ds_i=Ta_i\). For larger subsets the differential sums the signed zero-mode actions of the smaller coordinates over complementary blocks, with the largest index in the second block. The resulting \(2(2^r-1)\) coordinates and their simplicial differential forms retain the homotopies. The comparison with marked geometric action roofs also has to account for the independent boundary tensor factor.

known.title: Components and loops of the genuine Heisenberg action space
known.text:
Let \(H=V_\kappa\) be the rank-one Heisenberg vertex algebra over \(\mathbb C\), with \(J_{(1)}J=\kappa\mathbf1\) and \(\kappa\ne0\). Let \(B=\Lambda(\epsilon)\) on one degree-one generator with \(d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0\). An action of \(B\) on \(H\) gives a map \(B\otimes H\to H\) with a specified path from its restriction on \(1\otimes H\) to the identity. Let \(F\) be the resulting homotopy fibre. The map \(q_B\) from the nerve of the original category of action roofs to \(F\) is a weak equivalence. The charge and constant term distinguish the components, each of which has scalar loops and vanishing higher homotopy:
\[
 F\simeq \mathbb C^2_{\rm disc}\times K(\mathbb C,1).
\]

To measure the two coordinates, lift \(\epsilon\otimes1\) to a closed state \(e\) on the source leg of a roof and choose \(u\) in its acyclic kernel with \(du=Te\). For right leg \(f\), the class of \(f(u)\) modulo translations is \((\operatorname{ch}/\kappa)[J]+\operatorname{ct}[\mathbf1]\). Convolution removes the realized action with the same pair. Scaling the exterior generator in the resulting zero-label action gives a polynomial family \(f_t\). On a common incoming resolution its tangent yields a derivation \(E\) with \(Ed=\partial_t f_t\). The map \(f_t+dt\,E\) is the path to the projection and keeps the unit comparison. On a based sphere, scaling two exterior copies extracts the quadratic coefficient of the whole polynomial tail. The constant term factors through the marked boundary. The linear term gives the additive scalar for a loop and vanishes in higher sphere degrees.
hypotheses: Use ordinary algebraic dg vertex superalgebras and ordinary tensors over \(\mathbb C\), localized at quasi-isomorphisms of the whole state complex. Retain the surjective actor resolution \(P\to B\), the admissible boundary quasi-isomorphism \(H\to W\), the map to the commutant in \(W\), and every boundary arrow under \(H\).

The boundary has a bounded-below direct-sum energy grading preserved by the inclusion and differential, with the vertex energy law and locally nilpotent current zero mode. The actor resolution may be unbounded. The unit homotopy is part of the target. Comparisons for other actors, arbitrary base transitions and independently defined physical boundary actions require their own maps.

known.title: Finite-colour exterior actions on the rank-one Heisenberg algebra
known.text:
Take three degree-one exterior generators on a rank-one vacuum Heisenberg algebra \(H=V_\kappa\), \(\kappa\ne0\). On each axis a genuine action records a charge and a constant. Specifying these six numbers and the unit paths still leaves three mixed pair coefficients. For two copies of a colour \(v\), the raw mixed coefficient is \(m(v,v)=\lambda(v)^2/(2\kappa)\), where \(\lambda\) is its charge. Thus at \(\kappa=2,\lambda(v)=3\) it is \(9/4\). Subtracting \(\lambda(u)\lambda(v)/(2\kappa)\) from \(m(u,v)\) gives the alternating form \(\omega(u,v)\).

For a finite-dimensional space \(V\) of degree-one colours, write \(F(V)\) for the homotopy fibre over \(1_H\) of restriction \(\operatorname{Map}(\Lambda V\otimes H,H)\to\operatorname{Map}(H,H)\). An action includes its path to the unit on the \(H\) factor. The two unary functionals and \(\omega\) give all components, naturally under linear substitutions. The vacuum coefficient on the degree-one colour states detects the loops. Together these maps give \[F(V)\simeq\big(V^*\oplus V^*\oplus(\Lambda^2V)^*\big)_{\rm disc}\times K(V^*,1).\] For \(r=\dim V\) and a chosen basis, the fibre over prescribed axis actions with their paths is \(\mathbb C^{\binom r2}_{\rm disc}\). Fixing the mixed coefficients as well leaves a weakly contractible fibre on those compatible data. Restrictions to the coordinate planes recover the whole space when the identifications on each shared axis are coherently matched. [The finite-colour theorem and proof](#ch07-theorem-finite-colour-exterior-actions). The [one-colour calculation](#ch07-genuine-heisenberg-fibre) constructs the marked unit path on the original roofs.
hypotheses: Use ordinary unital algebraic differential graded vertex superalgebras over \(\mathbb C\), localized at quasi-isomorphisms of their whole state complexes. In \(\Lambda V\) the differential and translation are zero.
Keep the actual Heisenberg spectator \(H\), with \(J_{(1)}J=\kappa\mathbf1\), in both legs defining the action.

questions.title: Fusion on a common completed module domain

question.title: Fusion on a common completed module domain
question.text: For affine modules, compare all independently completed fusion iterates on one intrinsic composable category while retaining both vacua, the spectator and all normal jets. Three- and four-pole regular evaluations exist on the common factorized intersections, and finite total spectator cohomology gives the stated three-pole comparison. For ordered Heisenberg completed inputs, extend beyond the finite-diagonal and retained-leg domains, with third-level strictness, the separate leg actions, chamber transport and both module units. Analytic Virasoro sewing requires an independently continuous receiving operation after collision.

questions.why: For a trivial first input and an infinite horizontal spectator with independent vectors \(u_n\), the joint series \(\sum_{n\ge0}p^nu_n\) belongs to \(U((p))\) and has no finite spectator span in \(\mathbb C((p))\otimes U\). A stronger tensor theorem must handle this discrepancy and also carry the occupied unit past the next fusion.

known.title: A spectator bound for independently fused affine modules
known.text: Resolve the pair and spectator independently. On their three-pole coefficient intersection the radial comparison shuffles the two bars. The pair-first comparison augments the outer binary bar and both input bars, then applies the inner tensorator to the rational pair head at outer length zero. [The two maps in the three-pole evaluation](#ch08-theorem-three-pole-evaluation). For each fixed outer exponent the inner Laurent series may use only a finite-dimensional subspace of the spectator, which can vary with the outer exponent. For a constant input \(T_{12}\otimes_{\mathbb C}M_3\), suppose the spectator cohomology \(H^\bullet(M_3)\) has finite total dimension. The coefficientwise inclusion from the completed pair tensored with \(M_3\) into the joint inner complex is then a quasi-isomorphism. To recover the original binary recipient, the [radial comparison](#atlas-c-horizontal-full-three-pole-native-finite-total) uses the coherent smooth affine–right-line realization, the full tensor–Hom unit, the restricted cofree model with common-cutoff actions, the functorial derived ideal triangle of bimodules and the bounded-below positive-current torsion theorem. On four leaves there is a full regular-current evaluation on the common factorized domain for \((12)(34)\). General independently completed iterates and changes of tree still require their own comparison. After deleting the third normalized vacuum, the anchored binary complex \(E\) has already been completed in \(p=w^{-1}\) and is defined over \(F=\mathbb C((p))\). In the outer variable \(s=w/z\), the [scalar comparison](#s-third-vacuum-anchored-affine-fusion) \(F((s))\otimes_F E\to E((s))\) is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when each \(H^i(E)\) is finite-dimensional over \(F\).

known.title: Deleting the third vacuum on the original anchored tests
known.text: Place the three marked positions at \((z+w,z,0)\) over the separated nested field \(F=\mathbb C((p))\), \(L=F((s))\), where \(w=p^{-1}\) and \(z=(sp)^{-1}\). Delete the normalized vacuum in slot three. On any original smooth test at infinity, translate the variable by \(v=u-z\). A positive current \(xv^{-r}\) acts through \(\sum_{h\ge0}\binom{r+h-1}{h}z^h xu^{-r-h}\), a finite sum on each smooth vector. This carries the surviving pair at \((z+w,z)\) to the anchored pair \((w,0)\) and intertwines the current differential and the central residue. At fixed polynomial arity, proper arity and test degree the lower outer Laurent bound is imposed on each finite test stage. An unbounded test can require different bounds at different stages. On the separate binary module \(E=S_w(T)\), the scalar extension \(L\otimes_F E\to E((s))\) is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when every individual \(H^i(E)\) has finite dimension over \(F\). This degreewise condition permits infinitely many nonzero cohomological degrees. With two inflated regular horizontal modules the series \(\sum_{n\ge0}s^n(H^n\otimes1)\), for a Cartan generator \(H\), detects the cone. The separated calculation at invertible \(w\) leaves the integral collision jet and the full cone for independently composed protected iterates as further problems.

questions.title: A common nonrational coefficient category

question.title: A common nonrational coefficient category
question.text: Construct a common positioned coefficient category for rational, multiplicative, elliptic and monodromic fields, with genuine mixed tensors, supported cuts, units, finite normal derivatives and full-turn holonomy. The marked balanced KZ–Gaussian subsystem and the selected elliptic formal theory already carry their indicated operations. For the scalar-corrected sixth elliptic field \(Y_6^\ddagger\), the conjugated moment actions and formal descent hold on its transported regular lattice. Identify independently selected lattices and construct the analytic specialization, mixed operations and recognition functor on the enlarged category.

questions.why: Actual mixed coefficient objects, generated supported operations, the marked KZ instance and the selected all-order elliptic fields are available. The remaining category must have its own genuine mixed tensors and native operation spaces, with field, moment and global comparison maps on their exact domains.

questions.title: Quantum operations with the required higher source terms

question.title: Quantum operations with the required higher source terms
question.text: For the selected elliptic source, compare the all-order realization of the scalar-corrected sixth field with an independently fixed seventh field or exchange. Identify its transported regular lattice with the proposed independently chosen geometric coefficient lattice. Keep the period signs, both moment actions and normals through this comparison. The separate Hamiltonian higher-operad problem asks for a continuous comparison and inverse with all the essential higher classical source terms, including the terms that enter at arity four.

questions.why: The sextic change of frame transports a known formal theory, including its moment actions and regular lattices. A seventh coefficient prescribed independently of that change can distinguish the two constructions.

questions.title: The full supported gravitational stress operation

question.title: The full supported gravitational stress operation
question.text: Complete the actual stress/marked-normal/heat comparison on the stress-cohomology complement and all required singular faces, with the independently prescribed targets and full coupled correction quotient. Retain the full finite \(e,h,f,b,c\) source, its ordinary and first-normal operations through bare order one, exact higher source contacts, the terms from precomposition with the source homotopy, fixed-frame unary relative normalization and finite moving-common-height preparations. The required independent-height partial collisions, marked endpoints and full action/insertion/source Hom equation must hold on one declared common domain.

questions.why: Exact source nilpotence, projected identities and unary correction provide determining inputs but do not identify the full stress complement, singular operations or permitted coupled correction class. The common-height chart and each normal/heat domain keep their own limits.

questions.title: The relative cubic map in free elliptic reduction

question.title: The relative cubic map in free elliptic reduction
question.text: Construct the full relative cubic homotopy on the original six-field current recipient with its lower maps and marking prisms held fixed. Finite current words act on the specified seed currents and their differential envelope. Insert the unit and \(s\) rows and the finite old-\(U\), selected-field and root jets in their original order. The paired-prefix moments retain their scale ratios, and polynomial collars compose on the prescribed domain. The projected polynomial-homotopy term vanishes on the graph-source image. Evaluate the original compact restricted square \(\gamma=Aj_qj_r-Ej_r\), construct the actual old-cylinder \(J_N\) on its unsupported homotopy-output rows, and retain the full coefficient and source differential. The \(q\)-first to lifted root-first prism and one old incidence edge are computed at zero old jet and fixed new anchor. Evaluate the other incidences and the eight-term compact marking with the original lower maps. [The lifted root-first prism and its old incidence edge](#s-elliptic-root-first-prism). Verify the original attachment without replacing any old endpoint or lower map.

questions.why: Finite domains and projected current values have advanced, but the original compact exit and old-source cylinder still determine the fixed relative attachment. Zero trace or zero projected polynomial term does not replace those maps or certify a correction-invariant obstruction.

known.title: A first normal jet distinguishes two six-field retractions
known.text:
Take the old contact \((12)\) in normal \(U\), keep \((34)\) as spectator and take \((56)\) in \(V\). Write \(\nu_j=d(-s_{V,j})\) for the closed reflected descendant. Let \(c_V,c_x,c_q\) be the normalized point currents in the indicated normals, and put \(D_j=c_Vc_x\,\partial_{q_j}c_q\) with the original fibre factors in their labelled order. On this row the two contractions taking \(q\) first each give \(D_j/2\). Keeping \(y=v+\lambda V\) and \(x=w\) fixed in the root-first retraction instead gives \(\lambda D_j/2\). The source-boundary prism from \(q\) first to that retraction therefore gives \((1-\lambda)D_j/2\). The two retractions fix different complementary coordinates during the first contraction.

Pair with a compact test equal to \(q_j\) near the normal origin. Differentiating the point current gives the first moment \(-(1-\lambda)/2\) times the retained coefficient. It is \(-1/2\) at \(\lambda=0\) and vanishes at \(\lambda=1\). A constant test misses both. On the first old assignment edge keep the new anchor fixed. Translation between the old anchors acts on graph moments by the finite expansion of \(\exp(\pm U\cdot\nabla_{x_{12}})\). At zero old jet, \(U_i c_U=0\) for each component of the old normal, so only the constant term acts on the old point current \(c_U\). The two incidence contributions cancel with their deletion signs.

The normal-section exchanges also fill their signed cube separately in each of eight labelled terms. The compact evaluation must still compare those terms on their actual supported sections, using the independent compact maps, both harmonic components and the prescribed lower maps. [The compact evaluations and their common domain](#ch09-compact-comparison-and-prescribed-lower-homotopies).
hypotheses: Use the original six-field history over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^4)\), at zero old \(U\)-jet on the finite generated cochain domain. Keep the supported top densities, closed harmonic colour pairing, both occupied vacua, the length-zero central bar section, all determinant and suspension signs and the same fixed new anchor on the old edge.

questions.title: Global arithmetic positivity and its field trace

question.title: Global arithmetic positivity and its field trace
question.text: Prove positivity of the complete Weil form on arbitrary compact support intervals, or construct a negative test for that complete functional. For support length at most \(31/10\), the lower bound uses 1,152 modes in each parity and controls the coupling to their complement. Separately compare the existing integral ordered collision and normal/Frobenius systems with an independently defined native chiral source on common trace domains, preserving both endpoint actions, nonconsecutive collisions and every prime-power contribution. A positive geometric realization must give the prescribed full Gram identity on those same domains.

questions.why: Fixed-window positivity, the full geometric trace, proper-ideal bar operations and integral normal/Frobenius maps are established at their declared scopes. The remaining all-vector signed estimates and native operation/trace comparisons have distinct requirements.

rows.name: Heisenberg, free fields and lattice vertex algebras
rows.summary: At nonzero level a charged Gaussian half-space ray realizes the full polynomial Fock module on rotation-finite endpoint cohomology. With the Cauchy regulator, outgoing subtraction and framing carried along, ordinary ray collisions give the charged interchange and its descendants. Two level-one preparations can be compared with the independent harmonic disk. A derived endpoint functor with nonsplit charge extensions, the deepest attachment of the full supported spacetime coefficient and a three-dimensional cap still require additional data. Ordinary lattice categories and section-valued genus averages have their separate hypotheses.

object.note: Polynomial finite-pole free fields; ordinary lattice vertex algebras

dual.note: Degreewise curved free-field dual; lattice dual still open

modules.note: Smooth free-field modules with all marked collisions

fusion.note: Polynomial Fock and finite ordinary lattice categories

bulk.note: Nonzero-level rank-one Gaussian model and its bracket

lines.note: Ordinary charged collision intertwiners with finite descendants. Increasing-height graph winding has inverse phase to positive endpoint continuation on the unchanged orientations.

states.note: Independent level-one harmonic disk with a mixed two-mode probe or a neutral ray-pair source. Strongly rational holomorphic lattice averages have their separate rank and commutant hypotheses.

dictionary.note: At numerical nonzero level the regular kernels, marked current modes and regulated ordinary charged rays agree across the Gaussian field change. The two-dimensional disk has an independent normalization.

statements.title: A free field with two independent parameters
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\kappa,\lambda\in\mathbb C\) and give \(V=\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), \(Tx_r=rx_{r+1}\), the Wick contraction \(P(u)=\kappa u^{-2}+\lambda u^{-1}\). Its exchange satisfies \(S(u)(x_1\otimes x_1)=x_1\otimes x_1-2\lambda u^{-1}1\otimes1\), and its ordinary unital geometric point modules with all marked collisions are exactly the smooth modules with \([J_m,J_n]=(\kappa m\delta_{m+n,0}+\lambda\varepsilon(m)\delta_{m+n,-1})1\), where \(\varepsilon(m)=1\) for \(m\ge0\) and \(-1\) otherwise. The curved dual has zero differential and curvature \(\sum_{r\ge1}(\kappa r e_r+\lambda e_{r-1})e_{-r}\) on exterior cochains completed by finite negative-mode cutoffs separately in each exterior degree, with finite positive-mode support at each cutoff. For any two contractions of this form, the primitive field map \(V_{P+Q}\to V_P\otimes V_Q\) preserves fields and exchange and adds the contraction parameters; it is not a fixed-level fusion coproduct.

statements.title: Fock modules and rational coinvariants
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), consider Heisenberg modules with \([a_m,a_n]=m\kappa\delta_{m+n,0}\), each positive mode locally nilpotent, and sufficiently high positive modes annihilating each vector. The assignment \(E\mapsto\mathcal F(E)=E[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), with \(a_{-m}=x_m\), \(a_m=m\kappa\partial_{x_m}\) and \(a_0=A_E\), is an exact equivalence from \(\mathbb C[a_0]\)-modules, and negative-current coinvariants recover \(E\). At finitely many distinct complex points, the derived coinvariants of the algebraic tensor product of these Fock modules under rational currents vanishing at infinity are \(\bigotimes_iE_i\) in degree zero. For finite-dimensional \(E_i\), their coinvariant connection is \(d+\kappa^{-1}\sum_{i<j}A_iA_j\,d\log(p_i-p_j)\); on scalar-charge dual fibres the positive half-exchange is \(e^{\pi i\alpha\beta/\kappa}\) followed by the flip, with normalized associator equal to one.

statements.title: Grading changes the derived endomorphisms
statements.text: For the algebraic Heisenberg mode algebra \(A_\kappa\) over \(\mathbb C\), with \(\kappa\ne0\), put \(\mathfrak n_-=\bigoplus_{m\ge1}\mathbb Ca_{-m}\), \(W=A_\kappa\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n_-)}\mathbb C\) and \(R=\mathbb C[a_0]\). With \(\deg a_n=n\), internally graded derived Hom, summed over internal degrees but retaining full products within each homogeneous component, gives a formal endomorphism dg algebra with value \(R\). In the ordinary unbounded derived category of all algebraic \(A_\kappa\)-modules, \(\operatorname{Ext}^0(W,W)=R\), \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(W,W)=(\prod_{m\ge1}V_m)/(\bigoplus_{m\ge1}V_m)\), where \(V_m=a_mR[a_m,a_{m+1},\ldots]\), and every other degree vanishes. For every polynomial Fock module \(\mathcal F(E)\), full \(\operatorname{RHom}(W,\mathcal F(E))\) vanishes, whereas derived negative-current coinvariants equal \(E[0]\).

statements.title: The Gaussian bulk and its boundary current
statements.text: On \(\mathbb C\times\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), take the Gaussian abelian Chern–Simons observable complex over \(\mathbb C\), with numerical \(k=\hbar\kappa\ne0\), pairing \(-\kappa(2\pi i)^{-1}\int\alpha\wedge\beta\), and boundary condition \(j^*\alpha\in dz\wedge\Omega_c^\bullet\). Its carrier is the direct sum over field number of completed projective bornological symmetric powers, realized by compact smooth kernels satisfying that boundary condition in every variable. The rotation-finite boundary cohomology is the universal rank-one Heisenberg vertex algebra \(V_k\), while interior cohomology is an exterior algebra on one degree-one class. With orientation \(dx\wedge dy\wedge dt\), the outward-oriented sphere operation and the generator \(\xi\) normalized by \(\iota_{J_0}\xi=1\), the bulk bracket is \(\{\xi,\xi\}=2\pi i/k\), and the corresponding finite-jet vacuum cohomology has algebraic secondary pairing \(1/k\).

statements.title: Vacuum extensions detect the Heisenberg level
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), restrict the polynomial Heisenberg Fock construction to finite-dimensional \(\mathbb C[t]\)-modules with nilpotent \(t\), where \(a_0=t\), and transport the product by \(\mathcal F(M)\star\mathcal F(N)=\mathcal F(M\otimes N)\). Prescribe the conformal-block connection \(d-(T_M\otimes T_N/\kappa)\,dz/z\) on these chosen coefficient spaces, with the ordinary associator; the positive half-exchange is \(\operatorname{flip}\exp(\pi iT_M\otimes T_N/\kappa)\). On the marked vacuum extension \(J=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), with its inclusion and quotient maps \(i:\mathbb C\to J\), \(p:J\to\mathbb C\), normalized by \(i(1)=t\), \(p(1)=1\), \(p(t)=0\), and \(n=ip\), positive pure braid is \(1+(2\pi i/\kappa)n\otimes n\). A complex-linear exact strong braided equivalence preserving this exact marked extension and its unit identification between levels \(\kappa,\kappa'\ne0\) therefore requires \(\kappa=\kappa'\), although the ambient associative algebra \(\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathbb C[t]}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)\simeq\Lambda(\epsilon)\), \(|\epsilon|=1\), is unchanged.

statements.title: A comparison preserving the vacuum and its operations
statements.text: At nonzero Heisenberg level, identify the negative-current coinvariants and the degreewise completed curved cochain transform on a common localized category. The comparison must carry the marked vacuum, rational collisions and logarithmic transport. For two unit charges at level three, positive continuation of the incoming position in the normalized collision coefficient gives \(e^{2\pi i/3}\). On a graph oriented by increasing normal coordinate the unsubtracted mutual contraction is \(-k^{-1}\int d\log(z_1-z_2)\), giving \(e^{-2\pi i/3}\) for the positive full turn with fixed endpoint positions. Any functor using that latter path as the same oriented Fock transport must account for the inversion. The independently prescribed extension to nonsplit marked modules and its bulk action remain open.

statements.title: Siegel–Weil for the hyperbolic genus
statements.text: Let \(V\) be a strongly rational holomorphic vertex operator algebra over \(\mathbb C\), with its conformal vector, algebraic graded direct-sum states, a chosen Cartan subalgebra of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), and associated positive-definite even lattice of rank \(r\ge3\). Write \(c=c(V)\), let \(\mathcal H(V)\) be its hyperbolic genus, let \(G_W\) be the finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphisms of \(W\) on its associated lattice, and put \(m(V)=\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}|G_W|^{-1}\). For \(r>4\) and \(\tau\) in the upper half-plane, \[\frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_W(\tau)}{|G_W|}=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\infty\backslash\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)}\varepsilon(\gamma)^c\frac{\operatorname{ch}_C(\gamma\tau)}{\eta(\gamma\tau)^r},\qquad \Gamma_\infty=\{\pm T^n:n\in\mathbb Z\}.\] Here \(\eta\) is the Dedekind eta function and \(\varepsilon\) its standard multiplier, with metaplectic lifts when required; the sum is absolutely and locally uniformly convergent. At \(r=3,4\), multiply each summand by \(\operatorname{Im}(\gamma\tau)^t\), continue meromorphically from \(\operatorname{Re}t>1-r/4\), and evaluate at \(t=0\): the standard section specified by the real Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions is regular there and has the same value, with the metaplectic convention at rank three. The proof uses the positive nonvacuum commutant weights supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang’s 2026 preprint; assuming those weights are strictly positive is an explicit alternative hypothesis. For this holomorphic class this establishes, in the absolutely convergent range \(r>4\), the character identity of Möller–Rayhaun, arXiv:2408.07117 (2024), Conjecture 5.7; at \(r=3,4\) the identity holds for the specified continuation. The arithmetic Siegel–Weil theorems are known inputs.
statements.antecedents: Möller–Rayhaun (2024), arXiv:2408.07117, Conjecture 5.7, Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.11; van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 4.2; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), arXiv:2611.12417, Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3; Opitz (2018), Theorem 3.7.2; Kudla (2001, preprint), arXiv:math/0110236, Theorem 4.1(i) and Proposition 4.22.

statements.title: Characters, discriminant gluings and genus mass
statements.text: For a strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra \(V\) with a chosen Cartan of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), positive-definite even associated lattice \(L\) of rank \(r\ge3\), and positive nonvacuum \(C\)-module weights as supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang (2026), put \(D=L^*/L\), let \(K\subset O(D)\) be the image of \(\operatorname{Aut}(C)\) on its simple modules under the opposite-discriminant identification, and set \(m_L=\sum_{[M]\in\operatorname{gen}(L)}|O(M)|^{-1}\). Every discriminant isometry \(\phi:D_M\to D\) gives the holomorphic extension \(W_{M,\phi}=\bigoplus_{a\in D_M}C_{\phi(a)}\otimes V_{M+a}\), on algebraic ordinary states, and the isomorphism classes over \(M\) are \(K\backslash\operatorname{Iso}(D_M,D)/O(M)\). For characters on the upper half-plane, let \(G_W\) be the full finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphisms on the associated lattice, and set \(m(V)=\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}|G_W|^{-1}\) over the hyperbolic genus. Then \[m(V)=\frac{|O(D)|}{|K|}m_L,\qquad \frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_W}{|G_W|}=\eta^{-r}f^T\Theta_{\mathrm{av}},\qquad \Theta_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{1}{m_L|O(D)|}\sum_{[M]}\frac{1}{|O(M)|}\sum_{\sigma\in O(D)}\sigma\theta_M,\] where \(f=(\operatorname{ch}_{C_a})_{a\in D}\) and \(\theta_M\) is the vector of lattice-coset theta series. The mass formula itself is known from Moriwaki and Möller–Rayhaun; the character contraction retains the entire discriminant symmetrization and the kernels of the lattice actions.
statements.antecedents: Moriwaki (2021, revised preprint), Theorem 4.16; Möller–Rayhaun (2024), Theorem 4.7, Corollary 4.11, Proposition 4.15 and Corollary 4.16; van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 4.2; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3.

statements.title: The hyperbolic average on marked curves in every genus
statements.text: Let \(V\), of central charge \(c=c(V)\), be strongly rational and holomorphic over \(\mathbb C\), with a chosen Cartan of \(V_1\), strongly rational Heisenberg commutant \(C\), associated positive-definite even lattice \(L\) of rank \(r\ge3\), and positive nonvacuum commutant weights supplied by Dong–Sun–Wang (2026), or assumed explicitly. For each \(g\ge1\), use ordinary algebraic modules, restricted duals, invariant forms with vacuum norm one, and a marked sphere with \(g\) disjoint paired handle sewings and an extra vacuum insertion. If \(B_g\) is the rank-one Heisenberg vacuum sewing series with constant term one, \(C_g\) the commutant vector built from its own creation and evaluation intertwiners, \(f_{C,g}=B_g^{-(c-r)}C_g\), and \(\Phi_{W,g}=B_g^{-c}Z_{W,g}\), then \[\frac{1}{m(V)}\sum_{[W]\in\mathcal H(V)}\frac{\Phi_{W,g}}{|G_W|}=f_{C,g}^T\Theta_{\mathrm{av}}^{(g)}=\kappa_{r,g}^{-1}f_{C,g}^TE_{D,g}(\Omega,0),\qquad \kappa_{r,g}=\begin{cases}1&r>g+1,\\2&r\le g+1.\end{cases}\] Here \(m(V)=\sum|G_W|^{-1}\) uses full effective lattice stabilizers, \(D=L^*/L\), and \(\Theta_{\mathrm{av}}^{(g)}\) is the mass-normalized lattice-genus theta vector symmetrized by one \(O(D)\)-element acting simultaneously on all handles. The Eisenstein vector uses the standard Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions, parameter \(s=(r-g-1)/2+2t\), and continuation from \(r/2+2\operatorname{Re}t>g+1\); its value at zero is regular. Equality is coefficientwise in the finitely many plumbing parameters, locally analytic on disjoint-disc sewing domains, and continues as an equality of sections on marked smooth curves, compatibly with the actual geometric changes of coordinates, factorization and pinching, using the same VOA, lattice and gluing label on every component before averaging products. The commutant factor is defined on curve charts; only the theta factor is defined on full Siegel space. The arithmetic equality, including its factor, is known from Kudla at even rank and Li’s metaplectic theorem at odd rank.
statements.antecedents: Kudla, Some extensions of the Siegel–Weil formula (1992), Theorem I.2; Li (2023, revised preprint), arXiv:2110.07457, Theorem 2.2.9 and Remark 2.2.12; Damiolini–Gibney–Tarasca (2019, preprint), Theorem 8.5.1; Gui (2023, revised preprint), Theorem 13.1; Tuite–Welby (2023, preprint), equations (99)–(104), (114)–(115), (133) and §7.2; Carpi–Codogni (2026, preprint), Theorems 7.3–7.4 and Proposition 7.6; Dong–Sun–Wang (2026, preprint), Theorem 3 and Corollary 5.3.

statements.title: A separating covariance in rank sixteen
statements.text: For the positive-definite even unimodular rank-sixteen genus \(\{E_8\oplus E_8,D_{16}^{+}\}\), let \(p=286/691\), \(q=405/691\) be the normalized inverse-orthogonal-group weights and write \(A_g=p\theta_{E_8\oplus E_8}^{(g)}+q\theta_{D_{16}^{+}}^{(g)}\), \(\Delta_g=\theta_{E_8\oplus E_8}^{(g)}-\theta_{D_{16}^{+}}^{(g)}\). On a block diagonal in Siegel space, \[A_{g+h}\big|_{g+h\to g,h}-A_gA_h=pq\Delta_g\Delta_h.\] The \(4+4\) restriction has nonzero coefficient \(3085190905724928000/477481\), detected by the ordered \(D_4\) Gram coefficients \(7257600\) and \(2096640\). For actual lattice-VOA curve amplitudes, with the same vacuum plumbing factor removed and a common determinant-line trivialization, the corresponding \(5+5\) separating coefficient is \(759006325862823886848000/477481\). The sewn average uses the same lattice label on both components. With the same marking, the two independent averages agree with it exactly when their covariance vanishes. For the one-class genus of \(E_8\) this holds at the \(1+1\) cut.
statements.antecedents: Gaberdiel–Volpato (2009), equations (2.15)–(2.17), §3.1, equation (3.5) and §4; Carpi–Codogni (2026, preprint), Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5. The covariance identity is elementary.

statements.title: The masses of the rank-four genus with weight-one algebra of type C
statements.text: For the strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra of central charge \(24\) whose weight-one Lie algebra is of type \(C_4\) at affine level \(10\), the associated lattice is \(\sqrt{10}D_4\). Its lattice-genus mass is \(1/1152\), and its hyperbolic-VOA-genus mass, using full effective Cartan-preserving lattice groups, is \(1/384\): \(|O(D_4)|=1152\), \(|W(C_4)|=384\), and the discriminant index is three.
statements.antecedents: Betsumiya–Lam–Shimakura (2022, preprint), §5.10, Propositions 5.28–5.29; Möller–Rayhaun (2024), Table 2. Orthogonal and Weyl group orders are standard.

statements.title: The rank-four character
statements.text: For the strongly rational holomorphic complex vertex operator algebra of central charge \(24\) with weight-one Lie algebra of type \(C_4\) at level \(10\), strongly rational Cartan Heisenberg commutant and associated lattice \(\sqrt{10}D_4\), the normalized hyperbolic-genus character average is \[j(\tau)-708=q^{-1}+36+196884q+21493760q^2+\cdots,\qquad q=e^{2\pi i\tau}.\] The genus has a single holomorphic isomorphism class.
statements.antecedents: van Ekeren–Möller–Scheithauer (2015, preprint), Theorem 8.1; Betsumiya–Lam–Shimakura (2022, preprint), Proposition 5.29; the standard central-charge-24 modular-character argument; Kudla (2001, preprint), Theorem 4.1(i).

statements.title: A coefficient-native category of charged endpoints
statements.text: For the Gaussian charged-endpoint construction, a chosen propagator defines a bounded dg product \(B_P\) on the compact smooth native carrier. The finite-free singleton coefficient category has all bounded \(B_P\)-linear maps, strict composition and units, balanced tensor and finite charged duals satisfying both triangles. Collar and moment functors are quasi-equivalences at this singleton scope. A specified continuous product bar contracts by a conjugated Euler homotopy, and smooth position families carry the actual differential-form correction. Separately, ordinary tensor descends in the split module-homotopy category, the polynomial tower has all-arity units on every dg \(E\)-module, and polynomial Wick maps have transported-operator corrections on the stated large-separation Laurent domain. These are coefficient and module-homotopy comparisons: the charged graded-free kernel remains non-\(K\)-flat in the ordinary derived category. Two compact sources of charges \(q,-q\) in one ball give a concrete failure of the naive all-position map to one energy-completed multipole point. Other recipients remain possible. The point-derived local-cohomology coring and the all-charge hybrid diagonal coring use different diagonal constructions. The polynomial/pro factorizing marked-category system carries the actual native cut actor, its higher cut and collision coherences, and both occupied-vacuum placements on the full ordered atlas. The common completed collision/separation carrier, supported lattice, nonsplit geometric left endpoint, invariant geometric balanced coring and physical sewing retain their stronger comparison requirements.

statements.title: Point-derived duality and the separate all-charge coring
statements.text: For the specified exterior-point and polynomial oscillator coefficient algebras, the genuine ordinary derived adjunction has kernel \(R\Gamma_{(t)}B\), \(B=k[t]\), with an explicit Čech counit, coproduct, idempotence and triangle identities. Its image is the \(t\)-power-supported derived sector. A separate hybrid coefficient enhancement admits every algebraic unbounded charged complex and all graded module-linear maps, with the diagonal Koszul coring and balanced triangles. The charged graded-free kernel remains non-K-flat over the exterior algebra; its ordinary and derived tensors are different. The full oscillator algebra has an actual derived unit roof. The product-bar homotopy has total-count bounds on the stated polynomial, fixed-field native and oscillator-energy domains; an arbitrary completion mixing infinitely many counts in one coefficient needs a further estimate. Finite independent point tensors retain these constructions. Collision-chart gluing, the geometric transverse actor and its balanced coring remain separate.

statements.title: Finite separated Wick maps and chosen primitive transport
statements.text: On the reduced exterior algebra over the fully separated configuration space, the explicit strictly unital \(A_\infty\) automorphism has arity at most the number of positions, a finite inverse, and finite insertions for arbitrary commuting charge matrices, including Jordan blocks, with all coefficient morphisms. A prescribed comparison is matched only under the stated relative, normalized-bar and complete universal formal Maurer–Cartan class hypotheses; this does not produce every numerical or supported relative homotopy. Absolute spectral identities use rational-kernel jet substitutions before expansion into one common Laurent domain. The strict Wick representative has no continuous extension from the full normal Taylor energy product to the specified finite-pole target. Other representatives and completions are not excluded. A chosen interior primitive difference gives bounded conjugations of the coefficient actions, full morphism composition and finite duals; specified additive choices compose strictly. Boundary restrictions, arbitrary-choice independence and physical sewing remain open.

statements.title: Two states distinguished by a mixed disk measurement
statements.text:
Put two quanta in harmonic one or a single quantum in harmonic two of a level-one boundary current. With \(p_j\) the creation variable, both \(p_1^2\) and \(p_2\) have squared norm two. A compact interior test strictly above the collar that contracts with \(p_m\) by \(\delta_{jm}\) acts by \(\partial_{p_j}\) on the annular polynomials. Use disjoint ordered slabs for the two first-mode tests. The resulting operator \(O=2p_1^2\partial_{p_2}+p_2\partial_{p_1}^2\) sends \(p_2\) to \(2p_1^2\) and \(p_1^2\) to \(2p_2\). The unit states \((p_1^2\pm p_2)/2\) therefore have sharp outcomes \(\pm2\). On the independently normalized harmonic disk fix the zero mode and write \(Z_j\) for the circular Gaussian coordinate of variance \(j\). In the two preparations the real symbol \(2\operatorname{Re}(Z_1^2\bar Z_2)\) has means \(\pm2\), although the one-mode marginals agree. A one-sided real collar contributes \(q^2\) to the unnormalized pairings. The slab operators act on the stated cochains. [Joint law and field operation](#ch11-relative-phase)

To compare all harmonics, form \(\Phi_r=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{i,j\ge1}r^{2(i+j)}Z_iZ_j\overline{Z_{i+j}}\) on a circle of radius \(0<r<1\). Compressing this real statistic to the holomorphic states gives the radially damped cubic operator \(W_r\). In the two preparations above its means are \(\pm r^4\). More generally, for a state supported on finitely many oscillator grades the mean tends to the expectation of \(W\). For a density operator prepared by a fixed two-sided real collar \(0<q<1\), it tends to the trace of \(W\) in that normalized state. The unscaled readings escape every bounded interval in probability under each fixed disk law absolutely continuous with respect to the vacuum. [The mean theorem](#ch11-theorem-the-cubic-observable-on-the-disk) and [the boundary fluctuations](#ch11-proposition-boundary-fluctuations-of-the-cubic-disk-observable).

rows.name: Affine Kac–Moody algebras at irrational shifted level
rows.summary: For any finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra at nonrational shifted level, the ordinary unit of affine induction is invertible on every unbounded source under the specified smooth right action, affine-free lifts, common Taylor cutoffs and tensor–Hom adjunction. A smooth vector killed by \(t^N\mathfrak g[t]\) reads a positive current modulo \(t^N\). At \(N=2\) only the linear term acts. Lifts can lower the mode index. To obtain output in the truncated resolution \(P_N\), the first negative-mode lift uses input in \(P_{N+1}\). For every finite diagram choose one source order large enough for all its composites, with compatible maps when that order increases. [How the smooth action reads a Taylor cutoff](#ch06-affine-currents-and-the-algebra-acting-on-their-resolution). The image of induction is generated by the regular-top module and its graded shifts. The sharp positive-ideal tensor exponent over the horizontal enveloping algebra is one more than the number of positive roots. The horizontal restricted-current comparison for unbounded binary inputs has its own smooth output tests with jointly locally nilpotent positive-current cohomology. At these nonrational shifted levels it remains open whether the regular top generates every smooth complex with jointly torsion cohomology. Independent physical fusion also requires its own comparison.

statements.title: The raw-level curved point dual
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra with invariant form \(B\) normalized by long-root square two, and let \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\notin\mathbb Q\). For the universal affine algebra at raw level \(k\), the curved point dual is \((C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g((z))),d_{\mathrm{CE}},+\eta_k)\), where \(\eta_k(xz^m,yz^n)=kmB(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0}\) and \(d\alpha(x,y)=-\alpha([x,y])\). Complete separately in each exterior degree by finite subsets of \(z^{-1}\mathfrak g[z^{-1}]\), allowing finite \(\mathfrak g[[z]]\)-dual support separately for each such subset, with no product over exterior degrees. This is the point dual for the universal envelope, rather than a formula for simple quotients or an identification with the affine vertex algebra at the complementary level.

statements.title: KZ fusion with an explicit collision comparison
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), long-root square two and \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\notin\mathbb Q\), induce \(\mathbb V^k(E)\) from finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\)-modules \(E\), with positive currents acting trivially on the top. Their fixed-level product is \(\mathbb V^k(E)\odot\mathbb V^k(F)=\mathbb V^k(E\otimes F)\), with energy completion \(\prod_hX_{[h]}\), associator \(\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}(-\Omega_{12}/\kappa,-\Omega_{23}/\kappa)\), and upper-half-plane vertex braiding \(\operatorname{flip}\,e^{\pi i\Omega/\kappa}\), where \(\Omega\) is the Casimir tensor of \(B\). The rational-current Chevalley–Eilenberg collision map from distinct points to the completed one-point product is a quasi-isomorphism on modules with a finite Weyl filtration and finite-dimensional tops. The comparison extends to bounded-above complexes in that exact category by completing each term before direct-sum totalization; the completed target need not itself have finite support.

statements.title: An affine endomorphism obstruction
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), use algebraic Laurent-polynomial \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) modes at any raw level \(k\), with \([e,f]=h\), \((e,f)=1\) and \((h,h)=2\), and put \(W_k=A_k\otimes_{U(z^{-1}\mathfrak{sl}_2[z^{-1}])}\mathbb C\). In full algebraic Chevalley–Eilenberg cochains computing ordinary \(\operatorname{RHom}_{A_k}(W_k,W_k)\), the degree-one cochain sending \(f_{-1}\) to the induced vacuum and every other negative basis mode to zero represents a nonzero class at every \(k\). Consequently this endomorphism dg algebra cannot be quasi-isomorphic to \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)^{\mathrm{op}}\) concentrated in degree zero, including at irrational shifted level. This assertion uses algebraic modes and full Hom; it does not replace the coinvariant construction of the KZ connection.

statements.title: A commutative noncritical vacuum model
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), with long roots of square two, and any \(k\ne-h^\vee\), let \(V^k(\mathfrak g)\) be the universal vacuum and use continuous finite-jet cochains. The inclusion \(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g[[z]];\mathbb C)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g[[z]];V^k(\mathfrak g))\) is a dg vertex quasi-isomorphism with commutative source, and vacuum self-Ext in discrete smooth modules is \(H^\bullet(\mathfrak g;\mathbb C)\). It supplies a commutative \(E_3\)-model; uniqueness among all \(E_3\)-structures with this cohomology holds for \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) but fails for general simple \(\mathfrak g\), already for \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\).

statements.title: The nonabelian physical comparison
statements.text: For complex simple \(\mathfrak g\) at noncritical level, construct the boundary-module functor from an independently defined Chern–Simons theory and compare its supported insertions with affine rational-current collision maps. The comparison must preserve the universal vacuum, level normalization, horizontal transport and mixed bulk/boundary operations. Extend the algebraic collision comparison beyond finite Weyl filtrations only after identifying a module category and completion on which all iterated products are defined.

statements.title: Vacuum composition at every invariant level
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra, \(B\) an invariant symmetric form, and \(s\in\mathbb C\). Put \(\ell=-sB-\operatorname{Kill}_{\mathfrak g}/2\). The affine vacuum cochain algebra \(A_s\) has a filtered multiplicative comparison \(A_s\simeq R\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{wt}}_{U_\ell}(V_\ell)^{\mathrm{op}}\). Here internal map weights are summed, while Hom within each weight retains its required products. A finite-quotient bar model uses shifted operator order, bounds zero-mode bar length at each cutoff, and has polynomial zero-mode outputs. An independently defined diagonal map gives the compatible square. A filtered chain contraction supplies a strictly unital augmented \(A_\infty\) quasi-inverse and a homotopy of the dual square. Ordinary composition has complementary level \(-\ell-\operatorname{Kill}_{\mathfrak g}\). The theorem includes degenerate forms, raw level zero, and the critical form. The full regular contragredient, same-level ordinary-composition and native collision comparisons remain separate.

statements.title: The ambient contragredient vacuum and a finite-energy obstruction
statements.text: With the same affine data, take the full algebraic dual separately in each energy component of a graded-projective vacuum resolution. Its direct sum over energies is a graded-injective resolution of the contragredient vacuum. Signed transposition gives \(\operatorname{rev}_E A_s\simeq R\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{wt}}_{U_\ell}(D V_\ell)\) in ordinary composition order, where \(\operatorname{rev}_E\) reverses internal map weights. The transpose subalgebra consists of maps continuous for the degreewise weak topology. For nonzero semisimple \(\mathfrak g\), the natural inclusion of lower-bounded modules with finite-dimensional energy spaces into all graded modules misses the horizontal \(H^3(\mathfrak g;\mathbb C)\) self-extension classes. Thus this inclusion is not derived fully faithful. The full regular module has infinite-dimensional energy-zero space and requires a different comparison.

statements.title: Intrinsic vacuum marks and the modular BRST correction
statements.text: For every finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra, retain smoothness and joint nilpotence of the positive-current action. Under the specified generic line-action inputs, the intrinsic category has the bounded-below equivalence and smooth full-faithfulness comparison, including the actual vacuum and augmentation marks, homogeneous endomorphisms and heart kernel. Intermediate energy spaces may be infinite-dimensional. With \(\delta(x)=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x)\), the differential \(Q_\delta=Q+c_0(\delta)\) gives the corrected semiregular coreflector for ordinary smooth modules and bounded-below direct-sum complexes. The unmodified functor carries the negative-character twist. The diagonal comparison is the enhanced counit/augmentation comparison on the intrinsic image. Arbitrary unbounded totals, coefficientwise BRST-to-diagonal maps, the full regular contragredient and native collision comparisons remain separate.

rows.name: Affine algebras at rational level
rows.summary: Noncritical universal affine collision products are identified with vertex tensor products using the required resonance lattices. At positive integral level, the derived product of finite sums of integrable simples at distinct points retains an additional loop-space factor. Broader simple-quotient duality and physical or quantum-group comparisons remain separate from these universal-category results.

statements.title: Noncritical rational fusion and resonance
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra with long-root square two, \(k\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\ne0\). On finitely generated smooth universal-affine modules locally finite under \(\mathfrak g[[z]]\), with their Sugawara grading-restricted generalized module structure, the rational-current fusion product represents the Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang \(P(z)\)-intertwining maps for \(z\ne0\). For finite-dimensional Weyl tops, its associator and braiding are obtained by reducing the KZ operators on formal fusion lattices over \(\mathbb C[[\varepsilon]]\) at \(\kappa+\varepsilon\); direct evaluation is valid when constituent conformal weights have no nonzero integral differences in each pairwise and triple top tensor product. Resonant lattices can be nonstandard, so an unqualified substitution into a generic KZ matrix is insufficient.

statements.title: The loop-space factor in positive-integral derived fusion
Curved duals of simple rational quotients
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) and a simple admissible or negative-rational affine quotient \(L_k(\mathfrak g)\) over \(\mathbb C\), construct a complete curved dual incorporating the full null-field ideal and prove an equivalence with an explicitly defined category of discrete smooth \(L_k(\mathfrak g)\)-modules. The comparison must retain the simple vacuum and its collision products; the universal Tate-Lie cochain dual alone does not impose those null relations.

statements.title: The root-of-unity fibre comparison
statements.text: For the represented affine collision product at positive integral level over \(\mathbb C\), compare the long bimodule fibre over \(\mathbb C^I\), where \(I\) indexes integrable simple modules, and its weak Hopf reconstruction with a precisely specified root-of-unity quantum-group category or its semisimplification. The comparison must identify the parameter, associator, braiding and quotient maps. Admissible and negative-rational simple quotients require separate choices of category and recipient; an ordinary strong monoidal fibre to vector spaces is not assumed.

statements.title: A telescope invisible to zero-mode base change
statements.text: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) at raw level \(-3\), write \(B=Y_1\), \(H=U(\mathfrak{sl}_2[t^{-1}])\), \(R=U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\), and use the coherent native affine adjunction. Form the algebraic telescope \(L\) of the singular-vector maps between horizontal-Verma-induced \(B\)-modules with their assigned energy shifts. Then \(R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L=0\), while \(H\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L\ne0\) and the affine realization \(\Phi L\ne0\). Its actual unit \(L\to\Psi\Phi L\) is invertible. Indeed the cone defining this telescope has a cochain representative bounded below by \(-1\). In the cofree model its realized terms are injective for smooth positive currents and their invariant subcomplex recovers that representative. Classifying the unit for all unbounded objects at raw \(-3\) remains open. At raw \(-h^\vee\) and \(-2h^\vee\) in every simple type, and for \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) at the integers \(\ell\le-4\), different nonzero telescopes have zero realization under the native hypotheses.

rows.name: Affine algebras at critical level
rows.summary: The universal critical algebra remains curved on the dual side, and its smooth vacuum self-extensions contain differential forms on opers. Algebraic induction remains an equivalence after its exact detected localization. Under the coherent native-action, tensor–\(\operatorname{Hom}\) and common-lower-energy actual-unit/full-faithfulness hypotheses, a nonzero ordinary critical telescope has zero smooth realization, so the ordinary global unit fails. Presentable categorical self-duality survives, but the compact category has no right Serre functor; collision fusion and lines over opers remain open. In the separate four-colour theory at \(K=-2\), the full algebraic state cohomology is free over \(R_3\) on the classical critical state cohomology. Its translation-compatible state frame depends on choices.

statements.title: Criticality does not remove curvature
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\mathfrak g\ne0\) be finite-dimensional and simple, with invariant form \(B\) normalized by long-root square two, and take its universal untwisted affine algebra at \(k=-h^\vee\), without a degree derivation. Its curved point dual is \((C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g((z))),d_{\mathrm{CE}},\eta_{-h^\vee})\), where \(\eta_k(xz^m,yz^n)=kmB(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0}\); completion is separately by finite negative-mode subsets in each exterior degree, with finite positive support for each subset and no product over exterior degrees. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), normalized by \(B(h,h)=2\), the commuting pair \(hz,hz^{-1}\) has curvature \(-4\), so this cocycle is not exact. The vanishing shifted level \(k+h^\vee=0\) therefore supplies no uncurving of this model.

statements.title: Self-duality without a compact Serre functor
statements.text: For a nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), use discrete smooth modules of its untwisted affine algebra at \(k=-h^\vee\), without a degree derivation. Let \(\mathcal C\) be the idempotent-complete thick dg subcategory of the ordinary derived category generated by algebraic inductions from finite-dimensional smooth representations of central inverse images of compact open Lie subalgebras, and let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)\). There is no functor \(S:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\) with natural complex-linear isomorphisms \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)^*\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,SA)\), where Hom means degree-zero derived Hom and the star is the full algebraic dual. Nevertheless \(\mathcal S^\vee\simeq\mathcal S\) as presentable dg categories under the semi-infinite pairing.

statements.title: Critical vacuum self-extensions
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), normalized by long-root square two, let \(V^{-h^\vee}\) be the universal affine vacuum in the category of discrete smooth fixed-level modules. Writing \(Z=\mathcal O(\operatorname{Op}_{{}^LG}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[[z]]))\) for its regular-disc oper centre, one has \(\operatorname{Ext}^\bullet(V^{-h^\vee},V^{-h^\vee})\cong\Omega_Z^\bullet\otimes H^\bullet(\mathfrak g;\mathbb C)\); the constant-\(\mathfrak g\)-relative version omits the last factor. The differential from first-order variation of the level acts as \(d_{\mathrm{dR}}\otimes1\).
statements.cite: Edward Frenkel and Constantin Teleman, Self-extensions of Verma modules and differential forms on opers (2006), Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.6.

statements.title: Critical collision over opers
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) and universal affine modules at \(k=-h^\vee\), construct collision fusion and a category of lines over the regular-disc oper centre, with coherent associativity, units and the compatible action of the critical central currents. The construction must recover separated-point Gaudin operators without dividing by \(k+h^\vee\), and specify how it behaves under specialization of the oper.

statements.title: The critical translation cone retains kernel and cokernel data
statements.text:
For the two-term translation object \(z_{\rm top}=\operatorname{fib}(T:Z\to Z)\), its cohomology fits into \(0\to\operatorname{coker}(T:H^{n-1}Z\to H^{n-1}Z)\to H^n(z_{\rm top})\to\ker(T:H^nZ\to H^nZ)\to0\). At critical level it cannot simply be identified with the oper-form cohomology of the input \(Z\).

Scope: This is the formal consequence of the stated translation-cone definition. It does not identify an actual universal critical action space, construct its \(E_2\) structure, or transfer a bracket.

rows.name: Virasoro algebras, finite categories and continuous series
rows.summary: Universal curved Virasoro duality and supported induction have their stated representation categories. At each complex charge, logarithmic Ward fusion is represented on the lower-bounded \(C_1\)-cofinite generalized modules. The finite-base ribbon reconstruction concerns its specified finite category. For analytic positive sewing, fixed words obey tree comparisons on their prescribed domains. Two independently prepared composites admit a positive and a diagonal vacuum readout on explicit stronger graph domains. On the original completed binary image a nonzero outer primary readout can still be nonclosable. An intrinsic domain closed under every admitted fusion and sewing, an independent partner measure and a physical cap require further data.
