statements.title: The universal curved Virasoro dual
statements.text: For the universal Virasoro algebra over \(\mathbb C\) at any \(c\in\mathbb C\), use \(\mathfrak w=\mathbb C((z))\partial_z\), positive polarization \(P=\prod_{n\ge-1}\mathbb CL_n\), and negative modes \(D=\bigoplus_{n\le-2}\mathbb CL_n\). Its point dual is the curved continuous Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra \((B_c,d,\Omega_c)\), where \(d\alpha(x,y)=-\alpha([x,y])\) and \(\Omega_c(L_m,L_n)=c(m^3-m)\delta_{m+n,0}/12\). In degree \(q\), \(B_c\) is a product over finite negative-mode subsets of size at most \(q\), with finite positive-dual support separately in every factor; there is no product over exterior degrees. This computation is for the universal envelope and does not supply the curved dual of a simple quotient.

statements.title: A charge-independent universal vacuum model
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for every complex \(c\), let \(\mathrm{Vir}_c\) be the universal vacuum and \(W_1=\prod_{m\ge-1}\mathbb CL_m\) the formal regular-vector-field algebra. On continuous finite-jet cochains, the inclusion \(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(W_1;\mathbb C)\hookrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(W_1;\mathrm{Vir}_c)\) is a central, commutative dg vertex quasi-isomorphism. Universal vacuum self-Ext in discrete smooth modules is \(\Lambda(\omega_3)\), \(|\omega_3|=3\), and this supplies a strictly unital commutative \(E_3\)-model whose Browder bracket vanishes. Identifying this model with geometric mixed bulk/boundary operations is a separate open comparison.

statements.title: Minimal models and a finite weak Hopf algebra
statements.text: For coprime integers \(2\le p<q\), put \(c_{p,q}=1-6(p-q)^2/(pq)\), and take finite direct sums of ordinary simple modules of the simple Virasoro vertex algebra \(L(c_{p,q},0)\) over \(\mathbb C\). The output constructed from full rational Ward invariants at distinct points agrees with the vertex \(P(z)\)-tensor product, with common continuation paths and the simple vacuum as unit. If \(I\) indexes the simple modules, the exact faithful long bimodule fibre \(F(M)=\bigoplus_{i,j\in I}\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,M\boxtimes L_j)\) takes values in \(\mathbb C^I\)-bimodules and reconstructs a finite weak Hopf algebra whose finite module category has the same ribbon structure. Its tensor unit projector is \(\Delta(1)\), and its scalar counit need not be a character; this statement concerns the finite simple-quotient category, not all modules of rational central charge.

statements.title: The degenerate field algebra generated by two doublets
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), fix \(b\ne0\), \(t=b^2\notin\mathbb Q\), and \(c=13+6(t+t^{-1})\). Let \(\mathcal C\) be the finite-length, lower-bounded, \(C_1\)-cofinite Virasoro vertex tensor category, with simple modules \(L_{r,s}\), \(r,s\ge1\), of weights \(((t+1)^2-(rt+s)^2)/(4t)\), and fix its parity-corrected two-row quantum-group fibre \(\omega\) and coherent tensorator. The algebraic sum \[A_\omega=\bigoplus_{r,s\ge1}L_{r,s}\otimes\omega(L_{r,s})^*\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)\] has unital, translation-covariant associative intertwining fields on universal covers of ordered configuration spaces. Each finite input has finitely many output sectors; only the weights within each sector are completed, with restricted output duals and finite-dimensional sums below every real-part weight bound. The known finite-input vertex-tensor convergence theorem applies on chosen branches, including nonreal \(t\). The right action of \(U_{e^{-\pi it}}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\otimes U_{e^{-\pi i/t}}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\) on multiplicity duals preserves the fields, and its invariant fields are exactly the Virasoro vacuum algebra. Over that algebra, the highest-state doublets of \(L_{2,1}\) and \(L_{1,2}\), their descendants and iterated field coefficients generate every multiplicity space. Exchange is the constant dual inverse of the parity-corrected fibre braid; the mixed fundamental full turn is the known value \(-1\). The fields have noninteger powers; for positive real irrational \(t\), the algebraic sector sum is not globally lower-bounded.
statements.antecedents: Creutzig et al. (2020, preprint), Theorem 3.1.4, Proposition 4.2.4 and Theorems 5.2.2, 5.2.5; Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang VII (2011, preprint), Theorem 11.8(2); Koshida (2022, preprint), Theorems 5.7, 5.10, 5.11; Etingof–Gelaki–Nikshych–Ostrik (2015), Theorem 5.4.1 and Examples 7.9.10–11; Huang–Kong (2003, preprint), Proposition 2.7 and Theorem 4.3; Cremmer–Gervais–Roussel (1993), §§3, 5, especially equations (5.7)–(5.12).

statements.title: Singular sewing requires full radical descent
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), take \(b\ne0\), \(b^2\notin\mathbb Q\), \(c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2\), and \(h_{r,s}=((b+b^{-1})^2-(rb+s/b)^2)/4\), with \(r,s\ge1\). For fixed external weights and two coefficient-one three-point Ward forms, if both forms annihilate the entire radical of \(M(c,h_{r,s})\), the Verma block limit as the intermediate weight tends to \(h_{r,s}\) exists coefficient by coefficient and equals sewing through the simple quotient. At each descendant level every positive Smith exponent of the Gram family is one; this is the transversality that makes the conclusion follow from descent. At \(c=1\), intermediate weight \(1/4\) and four fixed external weights \(1/16\), both forms descend at every level but the level-two Verma limit exceeds the quotient coefficient by \(1/768\), so the irrational theorem cannot be specialized without an additional condition.

statements.title: Formal Beltrami sources and Ward insertions
statements.text: For the universal Virasoro vacuum over \(\mathbb C\) at any \(c\), let \(\mu\) be a formal series with zero constant term in finitely many commuting parameters, with smooth compactly supported coefficients on a planar sphere chart. With \(\bar\partial(z-w)^{-1}=\pi\delta^2(z-w)\), source coupling \(-\pi^{-1}\int\mu T\,d^2z\), and \(f_\mu\) normalized by \(\bar\partial f_\mu=\mu f_\mu'\), \(f_\mu=z+O(z^{-1})\), the normalized vacuum functional \(Z_c=e^{W_c}\) satisfies \(-\pi\delta W_c/\delta\mu=(c/12)\operatorname{Sch}(f_\mu)\) and \(W_c[0]=0\). Nested annular mode insertions with zero/one cutoff plateaux recover the ordered vacuum matrix coefficients, and the punctured-flow identity determines the contact terms for overlapping cutoffs; other plateau values require weighted residues. These are identities of continuous formal source coefficients, with no assertion of convergence in \(\mu\).

statements.title: Continuous fusion with arbitrary recipient inputs
statements.text: For real \(c>1\), construct an intrinsic admissible source assignment for arbitrary objects of the common continuous Ward recipient, and prove the corresponding represented fusion category with compatible repeated collisions and inverse domains. Fixed positive point-module inputs already have a representing recipient; full five-point interior sewing, entangled mixed Ward identities and coefficient-one vacuum units hold on their declared stages under \(H\) and the retained analytic hypotheses. The actual outer primary sewing does not extend to the whole common recipient, so its finer cluster-quotient source must be retained in the categorical construction. Preserve the separate geometric tree theorem at fixed \(c>25\).

statements.title: Completed principal sewing and the geometric tree sector
statements.text: For every real \(c>1\), compact-uniform three-leg estimates give exponentially weighted input maps, a nonempty two-successive-insertion domain with strict radius loss, and a local five-principal sewing germ. Internal momentum tails remain uncut. The stated four-point boundary-input hypothesis is retained where used. At each fixed \(c>25\), a separate geometric theorem supplies finite-tree local sewing and principal-marked sphere-tree Hilbert/channel comparison on Teichmüller space. It retains the Schwarzian and decoration lines and internal-momentum-dependent phases. The theorem for fixed positive inputs gives a common recipient representing the declared continuous rational Ward operations, and full five-point interior sewing holds under its stated \(H\) and analytic hypotheses. On the admitted finite-product recipient category, a complete dense intrinsic common input functor recovers the exact positive and vacuum source topologies. Actual collision still fails to preserve the recovered positive source; operation-compatible composite domains, units and repeated sewing remain separate.

statements.title: Five-point collar coherence with four completed inputs
statements.text: For real \(c>1\), positive principal momenta and the stated positive Shapovalov and four-point boundary-input hypothesis \(H\), five independently constructed sewing maps extend to all four completed inputs on one entire-energy Fréchet domain. They take values in a fixed regularized output space over the five collar strips. A finite input exponent may depend on a compact position set; the sufficient collar widths remain non-effective. The five flip identities hold on their overlaps, and the independent spectral-label pentagon gives collar coherence. The corresponding typed positive spectral category has natural bounded spectral morphisms and closed unitary associators, with inverses on the same output energy scales. Its mode domain has compact total-output spectrum and finite output level; intermediate spectra need not be compact. Full integer-mode Ward covariance includes the normally convergent negative-mode sum on strengthened inputs. External spectral measures remain multiplicities, and fusion retains its canonical output measure. The generating function has radius at least one; the stated removable singularity at \(c=25\) still refutes universal exact radius one. Separate results give full five-point interior sewing under \(H\) and the retained analytic hypotheses, point and meromorphic target recipients, full mixed rational Ward identities and coefficient-one units for every placement of one vacuum. Fixed positive point-module inputs have a common representing recipient for the declared operations. The intrinsic common input functor is constructed on the admitted finite-product recipient category with its exact elementary topologies. Each fixed word of \(d\ge3\) positive inputs has a nonzero output in the specified rooted vacuum channel. For two positive inputs the vacuum pairing is zero at unequal labels and is the paired two-point function at equal labels. General composite binary operations still need actual source stability, kernel annihilation, recipient-image continuity and the original units and reassociations.

statements.title: Four-point comparison on completed descendant inputs
statements.text: For real central charge in a compact subset of \((1,\infty)\) and positive principal momenta, all-descendant middle-leg doubling gives a common completed four-point comparison under the stated boundary-input hypothesis. All three finite input legs lie in weighted Hilbert spaces with exponent \(t>T_K\), depending on the position compact. The spectator/output exponent remains \(s>\max(A_0/2,\log L/2)\). The construction is bounded in the prescribed direct-integral Hilbert and Bochner \(L^1\) targets and retains the actual channel branches. Its atomless decomposable operator is not globally Hilbert–Schmidt. A separate five-point theorem admits four entire-energy inputs across the full ordered interior under \(H\) and the retained analytic hypotheses. Mixed completed vacuum sewings have their coefficient-one unit triangles, and fixed positive inputs have a representing Ward recipient. Arbitrary recipient sources, repeated collisions and all-arity interior sewing retain their further requirements.

statements.title: Conditional extremal and Parseval comparisons
statements.text: For \(k>1\) and \(0<t<1\), let \(w\) be a positive continuous translation-periodic weight on the upper half-plane with \(0<a\le w(\tau)y^{2-k}\operatorname{ht}(\tau)^{k-3/2}\le A<\infty\), where \(y=\operatorname{Im}\tau\) and \(\operatorname{ht}\) is modular height. Its \(t\)-quasiperiodic holomorphic fibre has an extremal orthogonal basis. Complete block reciprocity is equivalent to identifying the blocks with that basis and their prescribed norms. Under a faithful holomorphic block realization with bounded evaluations, an absolutely convergent monomial Gram identity gives isometric comparison of the polynomial closures. Density in the coefficient space and density in the full Bergman space are distinct requirements. A one-sided kernel inequality yields equality when the exact total traces agree. Global modular dimension formulas additionally require full covariance and the fixed cocycle. These criteria do not prove the physical nonlinear Gram identity, either density condition, positivity or cusp control; numerical trace agreement does not discharge an exact identity.

statements.title: Completed vacuum placements and the resolved nested norm
statements.text: Under the same real \(c>1\) analytic and boundary-input hypotheses, a rapid completed vacuum module \(V_\nu\) acts on finite exponential principal-input stages on the stated strict annuli. Its two placements are \(Y(\omega,z)\) and \(e^{zL_{-1}}Y(\omega,-z)\), with the prescribed translation margins; the vacuum vector has coefficient one. Actual Ward compatibility extends to completed inputs with all principal spectra retained. Separately, for fixed positive external labels the resolved three-input vector retains its intermediate multiplicity label and satisfies \(\|V\|^2=2^{-1/2}N\); the vector \(2^{1/4}V\) has norm squared \(N\). The proof sums the outer vacuum series after the finite Ward operations and then continues the resulting holomorphic pairing. It does not flatten both raw vacuum series into one unrestricted absolute double series or compute the norm after integrating out multiplicity. Coefficient-one unit triangles hold for all four mixed vacuum placements on their specified rapid or strengthened endpoint stages. This does not replace the rapid vacuum source by an arbitrary exponential source or make every common-recipient output an input to another sewing.

statements.title: The reflected Virasoro category and its actual marks
statements.text: For every complex charge \(c\), the specified line dg algebra \(Y_c\) acts coherently on the resolution and weight-pro carrier of \(W_{26-c}\). The actual right-action map preserves differential and opposite composition. It gives the declared cohomologically bounded-below enhanced equivalence, including the full subcategory of bounded-below smooth Virasoro complexes of charge \(26-c\) whose cohomology is jointly nilpotent under the positive subalgebra \(\mathfrak n_2\); no lower internal-energy bound is imposed. The inverse, unit and counit are explicit. The regular module maps to \(W\), the universal-vacuum mark to \(V_{26-c}\), and the augmentation to the restricted contragredient \(D_\sigma V_{26-c}\). The internal weight completion and derived bimodule comparison are essential; this is not a strict full action on the degree-zero module alone. The full unbounded reflected null class is classified by the line charge: ordinary acyclics occur away from the stated coprime minimal-series values, and actual acyclic telescopes retain reflected classes at those values. Native supported induction has a separately computed kernel and continuous separated tensorator. The relation between its weak class and ordinary equivalences, the remaining collision comparisons and physical realization retain their own targets.

statements.title: Augmentation Ext at nonsimple reflected charges
statements.text: For every complex \(c\), the ordinary derived endomorphism algebra of the reflected augmentation is formal and quasi-isomorphic to \(\Lambda(\eta_3)\), with \(|\eta_3|=3\). For the normalized map \(q:V_{26-c}\to D_\sigma V_{26-c}\), both actual maps \[R\operatorname{End}(V)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}(V,D_\sigma V)\longleftarrow R\operatorname{End}(D_\sigma V)\] are quasi-isomorphisms. A homotopy-commuting-square construction turns them into a unital dg-algebra roof in ordinary composition order. At nonsimple charges, \(q\) remains noninvertible and its cone is nonzero, even though \(R\operatorname{Hom}(V,\operatorname{Cone}q)=0\) and \(R\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Cone}q,D_\sigma V)=0\). These two vanishing tests do not establish conservativity or identify the full unbounded null class. The universal vacuum, its contragredient and its simple quotient remain distinct.

statements.title: A bare exterior \(E_3\) algebra has no coupling parameter
statements.text:
A strictly unital \(E_3\)-algebra over \(\mathbb C\) with cohomology \(\Lambda(x_3)\), \(|x_3|=3\), is unique up to equivalence at the level of its bare \(E_3\) structure. That structure alone therefore supplies no varying coupling scalar. A filtration, mixed action, retained translation or central-charge class, marked comparison, or braided category is additional data.

Scope: This is single-generator exterior rigidity. It is not a rigidity theorem for arbitrary simple affine cohomology, and uniqueness does not construct an enhancement on a separately prescribed object. Rank-one coefficient Koszul comparisons retain their specified unipotent sector and separate charge grading; no full all-charge braided equivalence follows from bare formality.
hypotheses: This is single-generator exterior rigidity. It is not a rigidity theorem for arbitrary simple affine cohomology, and uniqueness does not construct an enhancement on a separately prescribed object.
Rank-one coefficient Koszul comparisons retain their specified unipotent sector and separate charge grading; no full all-charge braided equivalence follows from bare formality.

rows.name: \(W\)-algebras and quantum Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction
rows.summary: Universal principal \(W\)-algebras have finite vacuum-extension models. For the universal principal \(W_4\) vacuum at \(\tau=k+4=\pm3/2,\pm2/3\), the local torsion summands have length one and the full twelve-dimensional graded Yoneda algebra is determined. The degree-seven generator kills all of degree eight. At \(\tau=-3/2\) the four-input native operation gives \(\gamma=0\). The associative vacuum endomorphism dg algebra is formal there and, by reciprocal equivalence and complementary duality, at all four of these fibres. The full vacuum Ext algebras at the other ten candidate levels remain open. For regular \(W_3\) a curved bar recognizes all weak modules, while a nonzero weak module can be invisible to every vacuum Ext group. On the full unpolarized \(W_3\) bar, smooth coinduction kills a graded-free object that survives the product-closed quotient generated by totalizations of componentwise exact short triples. A global polarized equivalence, a reduction-compatible physical action and higher-rank states require further structure.

object.note: regular universal \(W_3\) mode algebra; higher and non-principal comparisons open

dual.note: complete algebraic bar dual of regular universal \(W_3\)

modules.note: All weak \(W_3\)-modules are recognized. The full product-generated exact-triple quotient fails to give an equivalence. Global polarized duality remains open.

fusion.note: finite sums of Weyl reductions, any nilpotent \(f\), type ADE, irrational level

bulk.note: Generic exterior vacuum Ext and associative formality. At \(W_4\) shifted levels \(\pm3/2,\pm2/3\) the graded Yoneda algebra is known, including \(\eta_7u=0\) for the additional class \(u\) of degree eight. The marked quartic vanishes at \(\tau=-3/2\). The enhanced vacuum equivalences give ordinary associative formality on these four fibres. Two-sided cocycles are explicit for \(v_-\) at \(-3/2\) and \(z_+\) at \(3/2\). The positive affine three-class has a rank-nine formula. Its nine native readings and the independently defined physical bulk comparison remain open.

lines.note: rigid Weyl-reduction categories, type ADE, irrational level; physical lines open

states.note: A bulk-prepared cap and global physical sewing in rank at least two require an independent state construction.

dictionary.note: independent bulk theory and normalized currents-to-observables map

statements.title: Finite vacuum models and exterior algebras
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra of rank \(r\), with exponents \(m_i\), and let \(V=W^k(\mathfrak g)\) be its universal principal \(W\)-algebra, retaining the universal generators at special levels. In the category \(\mathcal S_k\) of all weak modules, at every noncritical level \(k\ne-h^\vee\), absolute \(\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal S_k}(V,V)\) is computed by a bounded finite-dimensional conformal-weight-zero complex and has Euler characteristic zero. Outside a finite rational set of noncritical levels, it is \(\Lambda_{\mathbb C}(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r)\), with \(|\eta_i|=2m_i+1\), and the associative derived endomorphism algebra is \(A_\infty\)-formal, in particular for every \(k\notin\mathbb Q\). For \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) and \(\mathfrak{so}_5\), the exterior answer and formality hold at every noncritical level, respectively as \(\Lambda(\eta_3,\eta_5)\) and \(\Lambda(\eta_3,\eta_7)\); the \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) result includes \(k=-12/5,-4/3\), where \(c=-22/5\).
statements.antecedents: De Sole–Kac (2005); Bakalov–Kac–Voronov (1999); Raskin (2016); Dhillon (2019); Bouwknegt–McCarthy–Pilch (1996); Zhu (1994).

statements.title: Exceptional universal \(W_4\) self-extensions
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(V=W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_4)\) be universal, with \(\tau=k+4\in\{3/2,-3/2,2/3,-2/3\}\), and take absolute Ext in all weak modules. Its Poincaré polynomial is \(1+t^3+t^5+t^7+2t^8+t^9+t^{10}+t^{11}+2t^{12}+t^{15}\), so its total dimension is twelve. Nonzero generators of the degree-three, degree-five and degree-seven spaces satisfy \(\eta_3\eta_5\ne0\), \(\eta_3\eta_7\ne0\) and \(\eta_5\eta_7=0\); at \(\tau=\pm3/2\), the canonical Drinfeld–Sokolov map \(\Lambda(\theta_3,\theta_5,\theta_7)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}(V,V)\) has kernel \((\theta_5\theta_7)\). In the local shifted-level ring with parameter \(t=\tau-\tau_0\), there is one torsion summand \(R/(t)\) in degree nine and one in degree twelve. The two first Bocksteins \(H^8\to H^9\) and \(H^{11}\to H^{12}\) each have rank one. A first derivative on the null complements of the corresponding polynomial differentials is nonzero at each sign of \(3/2\). Reciprocal local-family isomorphisms carry this result to \(\pm2/3\). At \(3/2\), the degree-three class acts in six two-term strings, with starting degrees \(0,5,7,8,9,12\) and zero action on their partners. The Yoneda product is graded commutative. Let \(u\) be the additional degree-eight class, detected by the first Bockstein. At \(\tau=3/2\), rational cocycles of ghost spins at least \(23\) and \(27\) have product zero because the largest spin in the degree-fifteen target is \(49\). Together with \(\eta_7(\eta_3\eta_5)=0\), this gives \(\eta_7u=0\) in cohomology. Reciprocal and complementary duality carry this zero to the other exceptional fibres. At all four levels the graded Yoneda algebra is \(\Lambda(\eta_3)\otimes(\mathbb C\oplus I)\), with \(I^2=0\) and one generator of \(I\) in each of degrees \(5,7,8,9,12\). At shifted level \(-3/2\) the marked quartic \(\gamma\) vanishes. On all smooth weak coefficients the state modes identify the graded-opposite derived commutator, up to dg Lie quasi-isomorphism, with the weight-zero state Lie algebra. Its commutators land in the acyclic image of translation from weight \(-1\). In the marked minimal model the four-input Lie antisymmetrization gives \(6\gamma\,s(\eta_3 z)=0\) on a nonzero top class. The vacuum endomorphism dg algebra is formal there as an associative dg algebra. Reciprocal vertex-algebra equivalence and complementary duality transport ordinary associative formality to the other exceptional fibres. Every cohomology class at the original fibre has a two-sided derived Hochschild lift. The four fibres have central charge \(-7\) at positive \(\tau\) and \(253\) at negative \(\tau\). Among the other candidate levels, dimensions are known through degree five at \(\tau=\pm1\) and through degree four at \(\pm2,\pm1/2\). At \(\pm3,\pm1/3\) the generic dimensions give lower bounds. The full ten fibres remain open. [Vacuum self-extensions of principal \(W\)-algebras, §8](#ref-ch12-cq8).
statements.antecedents: Raskin (2016); Dhillon (2019); Drinfeld–Gaitsgory (2011); Boonstra (1994); De Sole–Kac (2005); Braverman–Gaitsgory (1996).

statements.title: A curved bar construction for all weak \(W_3\)-modules
statements.text: For every \(c\in\mathbb C\), let \(V_c\) be the regular universal \(W_3\)-algebra, let \(A_c\) be the closure of its finite mode operations for pointwise convergence on discrete cyclic weak modules, and set \(e(a)=\pi_0(a\mathbf1)\), \(E=\ker e\), where \(\pi_0\) projects onto the vacuum-weight line. The curved bar algebra \(\widehat B=\prod_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E^{\otimes n},\mathbb C)\), with algebraic tensors, the topology annihilating finite-dimensional finite-length tensor spaces, graded-opposite bar multiplication and curvature \(h(a,b)=e(ab)\), has free contramodules \(B[[M]]^r=\prod_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E^{\otimes n},M^{r-n})\); twisting gives a dg adjunction \(K\dashv F\) for possibly unbounded smooth complexes, with \(F(Q)^r=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(A_c,Q^r_{\mathrm{disc}})\). Curved contramodules free on degree-zero generators \(M\), with every recovered orbit map \(a\mapsto e(a)m+(Dm)(a-e(a)1)\) continuous into discrete \(M\), form an abelian category exactly equivalent to all weak \(V_c\)-modules. For ordinary weak modules, bar cochains continuous successively in the mode inputs, with each intermediate Hom space treated as discrete, compute derived Hom and Yoneda composition.
statements.antecedents: Beilinson (2007); De Sole–Kac (2005); Al-Ali–Linshaw (2016); Positselski (2009); Clarke–Crossley–Whitehouse (2006); Bousfield (2003); Damiolini–Gibney–Tarasca (2019).

statements.title: Braided quantum Hamiltonian reduction
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a simple complex Lie algebra of type \(A,D\) or \(E\), let \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and let \(f\in\mathfrak g\) be any nilpotent element. Quantum Hamiltonian reduction \(H_f^0\) is a braided tensor equivalence between the category of finite direct sums of affine Weyl modules \(\mathbb V^k_\lambda\), induced from finite-dimensional simple \(\mathfrak g\)-modules of dominant integral highest weight \(\lambda\), and the category of finite direct sums of their reductions as \(W^k(\mathfrak g,f)\)-modules. The reduced category is rigid, with \(H_f^0(\mathbb V^k_{\lambda^*})\) dual to \(H_f^0(\mathbb V^k_\lambda)\), where \(\lambda^*\) labels the dual finite-dimensional representation.
statements.cite: Creutzig–Dhillon–Nakatsuka, [The Kazhdan–Lusztig category of W-algebras of simply-laced Lie algebras at irrational levels](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.04667) (2026), Theorems 1.1 and 5.2; §§2.1–2.2.

statements.title: Polarized nonlinear duality and the remaining vacuum cochains
statements.text: For universal principal \(W_3\) and \(W_4\) over \(\mathbb C\), construct a polarized completed curved dual, define the null classes on smooth complexes and contramodules, and prove that the twisting adjunction induces an equivalence after localization. The comparison must preserve the vacuum and intertwine quantum Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction; its extension to rational simple quotients remains a separate question. For the exceptional \(W_4\) vacuum the four associative fibre endomorphism algebras are formal. At \(k+4=3/2\), evaluate the nine native obstruction coefficients in the formula for the marked positive affine three-class. Construct a two-sided cochain for the additional degree-eight class in the original resolution and identify the normalization of separately specified affine reduction maps. Determine whether the separately defined reciprocal Drinfeld–Sokolov reductions identify their pinned affine maps, and construct a nullhomotopy of the degree-seven orbit operation on its geometric coefficient before integration.

statements.title: Irrational W₃ sector cohomology
statements.text: For \(K\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\) and dominant integral \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) weights \(\lambda,\mu,\lambda^{\prime},\mu^{\prime}\), use the explicit paired \(W_3\) BRST complex \(T_{\lambda,\mu}(K)\otimes T_{\lambda^{\prime},\mu^{\prime}}(-K)\), with \(c(K)=50-24K-24/K\) and \(c(-K)=100-c(K)\). Its cohomology vanishes unless \((\lambda^{\prime},\mu^{\prime})=(\lambda^*,\mu)\). On the partner, its cohomology is one-dimensional in each of degrees \(0,3,5,8\) and zero otherwise. The proof uses the nonzero primitive-cover transgression from the Jantzen connecting map and the unique on-shell coresolution column; the bottom differential is its transferred projection. This is a graded-vector-space theorem. It does not construct sector multiplication, a two-row vertex algebra, a braid-reversed equivalence, arbitrary-module derived \(\operatorname{Hom}\) or a rational-level extension.

statements.title: The canonical reduction map can vanish on a surviving class
statements.text: For universal principal \(W\)-algebras, the canonical Drinfeld–Sokolov map has its own exceptional parameters even when the target Ext ring is exterior. In type \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), with \(\tau=k+2\), its degree-three scalar is \(-\tfrac12(1-\tau^{-2})\), which vanishes at \(\tau=\pm1\) while the target class survives. The degree-five kernel in type \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) occurs at \(\tau=k+3=\pm2,\pm1/2\); the degree-seven kernel in type \(\mathfrak{so}_5\) occurs at \(k=-5,-1\). Equality of the target rings does not make this specified map invertible.

statements.title: Two-sided cocycles on the original exceptional vacuum complex
statements.text: For \(y=v_-\) in degree nine at \(k+4=-3/2\), or \(y=z_+\) in degree twelve at \(k+4=3/2\), all Hochschild arities are given on the natural endomorphisms of every smooth weak coefficient complex. The constant term is the state mode \(sO_y\), and the unary term is fixed on the differential \(Q\) and translation \(T=[Q,H_c]\). In the negative raw basis \(H_c\delta_2=1/\tau\), so the signed deletion coefficient is \(2/3\). The positive affine state \(a_+=h_{3,0}\) has a separate determinant formula using fixed-fibre formality. The \(31\times41\) matrix has rank nine. Three arity-two and six arity-three native evaluations suffice, with both diagonal minors of determinant \(+1\). Their nine scalar values remain unexpanded.

rows.name: Yangians, the Yang double and rational quantum vertex algebras
rows.summary: All-rank rational divided-state fields and the restricted RTT ghost vacuum have compatible exchanges on their prescribed carriers. At every rank \(N\ge2\) and every numerical level the determinant-one Cauchy presentation injects modulo \(\hbar^2\) into the local-vacuum-normalized all-arity modes. A two-point mode with a diagonal pole lies outside its image. The original lifts extend at every precision in every rank at level zero. At nonzero level they fail modulo \(\hbar^3\), where different rank-two lifts preserve the state actions and give a proper normalized embedding. The smooth point equivalence holds in the finite reduction-defined quotients and in their homotopy limit. Extending it to field actions and comparing fixed-level collision with a level-additive coproduct remain open. Ordered cuts of the level-zero chiral cotangent Yangian preserve every vertex product. For complex simple \(\mathfrak g\) its ordinary Zhu bialgebra is the dense polynomial cotangent Yangian at \(\hbar=1\). The ordinary RTT Yangian also defines an associative chiral algebra on words by multiplying adjacent states when their positions coincide.

object.note: Rational divided-state fields at all levels and in every rank \(N\ge2\). The normalized mode embedding is proper modulo \(\hbar^2\) in every such rank.

dual.note: \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\), \(n\ge2\): RTT ghost vacuum and product-completed curved dual

modules.note: Graded Koszul cochains and restricted smooth point duality at finite and formal precision. The unrestricted field comparison remains open.

fusion.note: Positive finite-type Yangian lattices, spectral coproduct and level addition. On the locus of opposite factorizations, separated highest-long-root Hecke sheets admit an exchange intertwining their level-zero cotangent currents.

bulk.note: graded lattice vacuum cohomology; smooth Ext and bulk operations open

lines.note: finite-type spectral line action and localized fundamental exchange

states.note: One-point vacuum blocks of the level-zero chiral cotangent Yangian on the sphere, with standard or mini-twistor coordinate action.

dictionary.note: universal twisting tensor; independent boundary–bulk comparison open

statements.title: The RTT ghost dual vacuum
statements.text: For the crossing-normalized RTT double of \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) over \(\mathbb C\), \(n\ge2\), with arbitrary central level \(K\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\) and no determinant-one quotient, use torsion-free weight-graded lattices complete separately in each weight, with finite-dimensional classical weight spaces vanishing below weight zero, and take the \(\hbar\)-adic completion for vertex operations. Its dual vacuum has odd generators \(c_{ij,s}\) of cohomological degree one and weight \(s-1\), with \(c(y)=\sum_{s\ge1}c_sy^{s-1}\), \(dc(y)=-c(y)^2\), \(Tc_s=sc_{s+1}\), and \[c_{ij}(y)c_{kl}(y')+c_{kl}(y')c_{ij}(y)=\frac{\hbar}{y-y'}\bigl(c_{kj}(y)-c_{kj}(y')\bigr)\bigl(c_{il}(y)-c_{il}(y')\bigr).\] Ordered exterior monomials give a topological basis, and the fields \(Y(a,z)b=(e^{zT}a)b\) have a unique unitary, translation-covariant exchange compatible with the differential, the Yang–Baxter equation and both hexagons. Its coefficient of \(\hbar^j\) on homogeneous inputs \(a,b\) has pole order at most \(j+\operatorname{wt}(a)+\operatorname{wt}(b)\).
statements.antecedents: Gui–Li–Zeng (2022); Li (2008); Gurevich (1990); Wambst (1993); Etingof–Kazhdan (2000); Jing–Kožić–Molev–Yang (2016).

statements.title: Monoidal Koszul cochains and spectral fusion
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for the normalized \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) Yangian with \(n\ge2\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\) and no determinant-one quotient, let \(M,N\) be torsion-free weightwise complete lattices whose classical weight spaces are finite-dimensional and vanish below weight zero. If \(B\) is the RTT ghost dual vacuum and \(K(M)\) denotes restricted graded Koszul cochains with coefficients in \(M\), the dressed left \(B\)-action and the coaction cup product give \(K(M)\widehat\otimes_BK(N)\simeq K(M\widehat\otimes N)\). With \(\sigma_zT^*(u)=T^*(u-z)\), the coproduct \(\Delta_z=(\sigma_z\otimes1)\Delta\) satisfies \((\Delta_x\otimes1)\Delta_y=(1\otimes\Delta_y)\Delta_{x+y}\) on the rational representatives before their Laurent expansions at separated spectral points. The central coproduct adds boundary levels, and the fundamental intertwiner \(1-\hbar P/(y-y')\) becomes invertible after spectral localization; at numerical \(\hbar\), this requires \(y-y'\ne0\) and \((y-y')^2\ne\hbar^2\).

statements.title: Noncritical graded vacuum cohomology
statements.text: Let \(V_K\) be the universal normalized RTT vacuum of \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) over \(\mathbb C\), \(n\ge2\), with \(K\ne-n\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\), no determinant-one quotient and scalar affine form \(\kappa_K(X,Y)=K(\operatorname{tr}(XY)-\operatorname{tr}(X)\operatorname{tr}(Y)/n)\). In the category of torsion-free weightwise complete graded lattices bounded below and of finite type, the one-vacuum Koszul complex is a dg \(\hbar\)-adic quantum vertex superalgebra whose cohomology is torsion-free and has topological basis \[\mathbb C[d_r:r\ge0]\otimes\Lambda(\lambda_s:s\ge2)\otimes H^*(\mathfrak{gl}_n;\mathbb C).\] Here \(\sum_{r\ge0}d_rv^r=(1-\operatorname{qdet}T(v))/\hbar\), \(\lambda_s=\operatorname{tr}c_s\), and \(H^*(\mathfrak{gl}_n)=\Lambda(\eta_1,\eta_3,\ldots,\eta_{2n-1})\), with \(\eta_1=\lambda_1\). The cohomology fields are regular and supercommutative, with \(Td_r=(r+1)d_{r+1}\) and \(T\lambda_s=s\lambda_{s+1}\).

statements.title: From point duality to smooth fields and collision products
statements.text: At fixed numerical level \(K\in\mathbb C\), take the normalized \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) RTT point double for \(n\ge2\), over \(R_N=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^N)\), \(N\ge1\). Twisting and coinduction are adjoint on termwise \(R_N\)-free smooth complexes and curved contramodules whose underlying graded objects are retracts of free contramodules on graded \(R_N\)-free modules. Their units and counits give an equivalence after killing, on reduction modulo \(\hbar\), complexes coacyclic on restriction to \(\mathfrak p=\mathfrak{gl}_n[[t]]\), and curved objects whose positive reductions are Becker-coacyclic. Here the positive reduction is the contratensor with \(C^\bullet_{\rm cont}(\mathfrak p)\). The functors, units and counits commute with every finite reduction. Over \(\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), complete topologically free smooth terms may have different mode cutoffs at each precision. The curved side is complete in each degree and graded-projective, with joint bounds on creation weight and precision in its summations. These point localizations form the homotopy limit of the finite ones. Mapping complexes use the derived inverse limit, which retains the \(\lim^1\) contribution. Extending this [point equivalence](#ch12-yang-double-at-a-point) to unrestricted modules, field and monoidal coefficient actions, and comparing fixed-level boundary collisions with the level-additive coproduct remain open.

statements.title: All-rank divided-state fields and their exact source scope
statements.text: The all-rank source proves that integral divided-state RTT fields agree with Etingof–Kazhdan fields for every \(N\ge2\) and every complex level \(K\), including the flat determinant-one quotient. It works at each finite \(\hbar\)-precision; the integral pairing has one divided input and its Laurent bound may depend on that precision. The level automorphism is translation by \(-K\hbar\), and the determinant-one classical fibre is \(V_K(\mathfrak{sl}_N)\) for the trace form. At critical level the two-current field has scalar coefficient \(-N\omega/(s^2-\hbar^2)\), \(s=z+u-v\), using the partial first-leg inverse. In the [forward centered annihilation calculation](#ch12-double-yangian-vacuum), the \(E_{12},E_{21}\) coefficient is \(-N/(x^2-N^2\hbar^2/4)\). Already at \(N=3\) its order-\(\hbar^2\) coefficient is \(-27/(4x^4)\), compared with \(-3/s^4\) in the scalar field factor. This source theorem does not identify completed module categories or establish a relation inside an intrinsic mode algebra.

statements.title: Point duality has algebraic, formal and smooth domains
statements.text: The uncompleted algebraic RTT double, with numerical parameters, direct-sum tensor algebras, finite mode relations and no determinant relation, has an acyclic curved twisting cochain. It identifies ordinary unbounded derived modules with the stated coderived curved comodules and contraderived curved contramodules. A separate nonzero-level \(\mathfrak{gl}_2\) theorem uses \(\hbar\)-adic completion and completed cobar, without a combined mode or bar-length completion. The classical smooth affine theorem uses its own polarized continuous dual and explicit coacyclic/Becker weak classes. The normalized RTT point double also has a [restricted smooth equivalence](#s-smooth-quantum-duality) at every finite precision and on its homotopy-coherent formal limit. This uses reduction-defined null classes and graded-projective curved coefficients. The comparison for unrestricted smooth fields and collisions remains open.

statements.title: A proper rank-two RTT embedding at divided precision two
statements.text: Let \(K\in\mathbb C\), including \(0,-2\). In the determinant-one rational double divide each RTT defect by \(\hbar^2\) and each determinant defect by \(\hbar\). In the all-arity mode algebra impose the exchange and residue relations with their spectators, then set the central local-vacuum mode \([z^{-1};1]\) equal to the empty algebra unit. The divided Cauchy lifts give an injective map \(D_K/\hbar^2D_K\hookrightarrow\overline M_2\). Both halves, the centered mixed relation and both descending column determinants hold. At classical degree two the pole component of \([(x-y)^{-1};e_{12},e_{21}]\) has coefficient \(1/(2(x-y))\), whereas products of current modes have Laurent-polynomial components there. This proves the image is proper. The embedding modulo \(\hbar^2\) holds in every rank. At the next precision the centered mixed residue for the prescribed lifts is \(K/[3yz(y-z)]\). At level zero they give proper embeddings before and after normalization at every precision. In rank two a correction vanishing at \(K=0\) gives a proper normalized embedding modulo \(\hbar^3\) at every level. Comparing the joint level-splitting coproduct with separately integrated modes requires retaining the cross-diagonal poles.

statements.title: Obstruction to retaining the same Cauchy generator images
hypotheses: Work in rank \(N\ge2\) with a numerical level \(K\) and the local-vacuum normalization of the all-arity mode algebra. Keep the prescribed Cauchy generator images and centered spectral shifts. Divide each quadratic exchange defect by \(\hbar^2\) before truncation.
statements.text: Modulo \(\hbar^3\) the creation, annihilation and mixed residues are respectively \(K/[3y^2z^2(y-z)]\), \(K/[3(y-z)]\) and \(K/[3yz(y-z)]\). Each is nonzero for a nonzero level \(K\). At \(K=-2,\ y=1,\ z=2\), the mixed coefficient is \(1/3\). A map at all orders with these generator images would survive reduction and contradict this value. At \(K=0\) the fixed lifts give proper injections at every precision before and after vacuum normalization. In rank two, changing the generator images also gives a proper normalized embedding modulo \(\hbar^3\) at nonzero level. [The residue and the changed lifts](#ch12-intrinsic-rtt-modes).

rows.name: Trigonometric and elliptic spectral parameters
rows.summary: Scalar multiplicative fields and the selected elliptic quantum fields exist on their specified formal carriers. The ordered quintic normalization realizes \(Y_{\le5},S_{\le6}\). The fixed zero sixth generating pair obstructs the next extension. For the scalar-corrected sixth field \(Y_6^\ddagger\), conjugation transports the two moment actions, formal fusion, normal maps and the regular lattices in every precision. Realizing an independently selected geometric lattice, a prescribed seventh field and numerical analytic sewing remains open.

statements.title: Scalar trigonometric fields
statements.text: Put \(P=\mathbb C[x_0,x_1,\ldots]\), \(Tx_r=x_{r+1}\), and \(V=P[[\hbar]]\), completed only in \(\hbar\). The Wick extension of the contraction \(\hbar/(e^u-1)\), with \(J=x_0\) and \(Y(J,u)J=(e^{uT}J)J+\hbar/(e^u-1)\), gives a quantum vertex algebra with field target \(P((u))[[\hbar]]\) and exchange target \((P\otimes P\otimes\mathbb C[q,q^{-1},(q-1)^{-1}])[[\hbar]]\), where \(q=e^u\). Locality is uniform in the spectator at each finite \(\hbar\)-precision, and the exchange satisfies unitarity, Yang–Baxter and both hexagons. There is no uniform pole bound for complete inputs: the exchange of \(\sum_{r\ge0}\hbar^rx_r\) with \(J\) has poles of unbounded order.

statements.title: A completion obstruction to an algebraic polar target
statements.text: Let \(k\) be a characteristic-zero field, \(R=k[[\hbar]]\), \(V\) a separated, \(\hbar\)-adically complete flat \(R\)-module, and \(T\) an \(R\)-linear endomorphism. Put \(W=V\otimes_R V\). If an \(R\)-linear map \(S:W\to W\otimes_R R[q,q^{-1},(q-1)^{-1}]\) satisfies \([T_1,S]=-q\partial_q S\), every output is regular at \(q=1\). The single covariance identity gives a sharp coefficient condition over commutative rings. Universal regularity for these maps holds exactly when the additive group of \(k\) is torsion-free. Indeed, write \(F_j=S((1-\hbar T)^{-j}a\otimes b)\). If \(F_{j+1}\) has a pole of order \(m>0\) with leading coefficient \(c\), then \(F_j=(1-\hbar T_1-\hbar q\partial_q)F_{j+1}\) has leading coefficient \(\hbar m c\) at order \(m+1\). Flatness preserves this injection over a torsion-free base. A pole of \(F_0\) would require a strictly decreasing infinite sequence of positive orders. Conversely, if \(pc=0\) for a nonzero \(c\in k\) and prime \(p\), take \(V=R\), \(T=0\) and \(S(1\otimes1)=c(q-1)^{-p}\). The Euler derivative vanishes and the pole remains. This test uses only linear covariance. A singular exchange over a characteristic-zero field needs a larger target, for example one allowing pole order to grow with precision.

statements.title: Meromorphic Yangian–quantum-loop comparison
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be complex semisimple, \(\hbar\notin\mathbb Q\), \(q=e^{\pi i\hbar}\), and \(|q|\ne1\). On finite-dimensional noncongruent Yangian modules, whose poles of each root current \(x_i^\pm(u)\) have no nonzero integral differences, the functor \(\Gamma\) to quantum-loop modules has coherent meromorphic tensorators for the deformed Drinfeld coproducts and preserves the braidings from the commutative parts \(R^0\) of the universal R-matrices. If \(\Pi\subset\mathbb C\) satisfies \((\Pi-\Pi)\cap\mathbb Z=\{0\}\) and \(\Pi\pm\hbar/2\subset\Pi\), then \(\Gamma\) restricts to an equivalence between the finite-dimensional module subcategories whose root-current, Cartan-current and inverse-Cartan-current poles lie respectively in \(\Pi\) and \(\exp(2\pi i\Pi)\). The comparison is meromorphic in the shift. A common admissible window for the shifted spectra gives the categorical comparison. At a shift where the tensorator and its inverse are regular, evaluation gives an isomorphism.
statements.cite: Gautam–Toledano Laredo, [Meromorphic tensor equivalence for Yangians and quantum loop algebras](https://arxiv.org/html/1403.5251v6), Publications Mathématiques de l’IHÉS 125 (2017), 267–337, §§2.5–2.6, 6.2–6.5.

statements.title: Elliptic fields with their global coefficients
statements.text: For a complex elliptic curve \(E\), extend scalar bar–cobar duality to matrix-valued meromorphic exchange kernels with a chosen period bundle, and construct compatible state fields and collision operations over \(E\). The construction must specify the allowed polar divisors, the translation action, the period holonomies and the tensor completion, and prove the exchange and associativity identities on those same carriers. Comparing with an elliptic quantum vertex algebra requires identifying its classical state space and its elliptic modulus throughout the deformation.

statements.title: Matrix trigonometric fields in the multiplicative ring
statements.text: Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic zero and \(N\ge2\). For \(M\ge1\) set \(A_M=k[[\hbar]]/(\hbar^M)\) and \(x=e^z\) near the identity of the multiplicative group. At precision \(M=2\) an off-diagonal matrix coefficient is \(\hbar/(x-1)\). It lies in \(\mathcal O_M=A_M[x,x^{-1},(x-1)^{-1}]\) and its expansion in \(z\) is not a Laurent polynomial. The scalar form and the coefficients of the exchange take values in \(\mathcal O_M\) at each precision. The field \(Y_\eta(a,z)b\) also contains the translated state \(e^{zT}a_1\) from the first factor of the coproduct of \(a\). The coaction gives the mixed pairing that is integral on divided states. Level-changing coproducts and cut residues commute with reduction in \(M\). In the inverse-limit scalar ring the pole bound may depend on \(M\).

statements.title: Binary Ward data do not determine a charged field family
statements.text: For the translated rational-current module with \(\kappa\lambda\nu\ne0\), one selected inserted primary admits the specified binary construction on every polynomial second input and for every current mode. Its free scalar and shift data can give either an ordinary Laurent example with trivial full turn or the normalized Kummer and Gaussian examples in their larger coefficient algebras. Translation and binary Ward commutators alone therefore do not force the Gaussian monodromy. Fields of arbitrary inserted descendants, vacuum normalization, coherent charge families and ternary collision identities remain separate constraints.

statements.title: Necessary conditions for full RTT recognition
statements.text: In characteristic zero, at nonzero deformation parameter and rank at least two, the fundamental tensor square in the specified full RTT category is absolutely simple and has only scalar endomorphisms. The constant RTT coefficient equation is an identity over arbitrary coefficient algebras; it does not force commutativity. Any compatible Laurent presentation through an exact faithful monoidal fibre must send the fundamental exchange to a polynomial matrix with polynomial inverse and determinant one. These are necessary conditions. A full noncommutative cocycle, additive translation frame and comparison on every finite comodule remain unconstructed.

statements.title: Cubic elliptic fields on all algebraic jet states
statements.text: For the fixed elliptic two-torsion kernel on the algebraic differential polynomial state space \(P=\operatorname{Sym}(\bigoplus_{m\ge0}\mathfrak{sl}_2^{(m)})\), the local/formal state-field map is constructed through \(\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^4)\). It retains the original midpoint second-order symbol and \(K=r_0^2/8-r_0^{\prime}/2\), together with the exact admitted normalized all-state cubic exchange. The four-factor and product-pole arguments give actual generating locality with a collision bound independent of spectator polynomial degree and jet orders, and reconstruction gives weak associativity on all polynomial states with independent jets and full outputs. Admitted exchange retains finite meromorphic state span per input, vacuum, shifts, period laws, unitarity and both cubic hexagons. Every admitted skew shift-covariant differential biderivation \(N\), including nonlinear or jet-valued generator outputs, is also realized by \(\delta S_3=N\), \(\delta Y_3=-M_zN/2\). The exact midpoint/endpoint gauge preserves the declared recipients. The whole admitted cubic family keeps that finite-precision scope. The selected scalar-corrected, ordered-state-normalized realization has all-order local formal fields on \(P[[\hbar]]\), agreeing with \(Y_0\) through \(Y_5\) and \(S_0\) through \(S_6\), and a chosen sixth field is separately constructed at precision \(\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^7)\). Generated supported coefficient operations and the precisely marked KZ instance also exist. The scalar-corrected full sixth field \(Y_6^\ddagger\) has an all-order realization. Conjugating the corresponding quintic operations by its sextic frame produces both moment actions and formal global descent on the pulled-back regular lattices. Independently selected coefficient lattices, a prescribed seventh field, a common native category and analytic specialization are further comparisons. The normalized zero homogeneous exchange correction does not solve the distinct quartic Yang–Baxter equation.

rows.name: Hall algebras and shuffle algebras
rows.summary: For the zero-potential one-loop quiver, the finite-root-jet cobar is quasi-isomorphic to its quadratic algebra over \(\mathbb Q[\hbar]\) in every charge. This computes the regular field on the algebraic charge sum. Dressed coproducts, polar fields at finite precision and specified inverse limits have their own domains. Critical Hall multiplication still requires a supported, orientation-compatible comparison on the whole flag before proper direct image, including the attachment of its two branches.

object.note: One-loop polynomial regular field in all charges. Finite-precision and adic polar fields on their specified coefficient spaces.

The zero-potential one-loop field specifies no such compact-state preparation. [The critical Hall comparison](#ch18-problem-189).

statements.title: Scalar bar–cobar duality and wheel defects
statements.text: Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic zero, \(G=\mathbb G_a\) or \(\mathbb G_m\), \(\varepsilon=\pm1\), and \(0\ne\gamma\in\mathcal O(G^2)\), with no nonunit factor depending on only one variable; write \(O_m=\mathcal O(G^m)\), \(\Lambda_m=O_m^{S_m}\), and let a superscript \(S_m,\varepsilon\) mean transformation by \(\varepsilon^{\ell(w)}\), with \(\ell(w)\) the Coxeter length. The coalgebra \(C_{\gamma,m}=(\prod_{i<j}\gamma(Z_i,Z_j))O_m^{S_m,\varepsilon}\), with consecutive-block coproducts, and the quadratic algebra \(B_\gamma=T_k(O_1)/(\gamma O_2^{S_2,\varepsilon})\), with generators in degree one, satisfy \(\Omega C_\gamma\simeq B_\gamma\) and \(C_\gamma\simeq\operatorname{Bar}B_\gamma\) in the category of sequences of \(\Lambda_m\)-modules. If also \(\gamma(Z_1,Z_2)\) and \(\gamma(Z_2,Z_1)\) are coprime, the map from \(B_{\gamma,m}\) to the big shuffle space \(O_m^{S_m,-\varepsilon}\), with unaveraged shuffle kernel \(\gamma(Z_j,Z_i)\) and permutation sign \((-\varepsilon)^{\ell(w)}\), has kernel \(H^0_{W_m}(B_{\gamma,m})\) and cokernel \(H^1_{W_m}(B_{\gamma,m})\), where \(W_m\subset\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda_m\) is the wheel locus. Its image is the shuffle subalgebra generated in weight one, so the map to that smaller algebra is surjective with the same torsion kernel and zero cokernel.
statements.antecedents: Bayer–Sturmfels (1998); Loday–Vallette (2012); Kunin–Lienkaemper–Rosen (2020); Dotsenko–Feigin–Reineke (2021); Dotsenko–Feigin–Kucharski–Reineke (2024); Neguţ (2022).

statements.title: When wheel defects appear
statements.text: Over a field \(k\) of characteristic zero, let \(\gamma\) be a unit times \(g(Z_1-Z_2)\) on \(\mathbb G_a\), or a unit times \(g(Z_1/Z_2)\) on \(\mathbb G_m\), where \(g\ne0\), \(g(0)\ne0\) in the multiplicative case, and \(\gamma(Z_1,Z_2)\) is coprime to its reverse; either exchange sign \(\varepsilon=\pm1\) is allowed. Over an algebraic closure, let \(r\) be the least length of a root sequence of \(g\), with repetitions allowed, whose sum is zero in the additive case or whose product is one in the multiplicative case; set \(r=\infty\) if there is none. Then \(r\ge3\), both wheel-supported defects of the quadratic-to-shuffle comparison vanish in weights \(m<r\), and both are nonzero in every weight \(m\ge r\). If \(r<\infty\), the weight-one-generated shuffle algebra is neither quadratic nor Koszul for its weight grading.

statements.title: One-loop Hall currents and their coproduct
statements.text: Over \(R=\mathbb Q[\eta]\), take the zero-potential one-loop Hall algebra \(B=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]^{S_n}\), with loop weight \(-\eta\), first input the subrepresentation, no rank shift and unaveraged shuffle kernel \((v+\eta)/v\). Its Cartan extension \(A=B\rtimes R[p_0,p_1,\ldots]\), where \(p_r\) acts on weight \(n\) by multiplication by \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^r\), is faithfully realized by rational creation and occupation currents over the family of all finite sets of algebraically independent sites. Cartan dressing gives a unital algebra map \(\Delta_z:A\to(A\otimes_RA)((z^{-1}))\), conjugate to separation of the sites, with \((\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta_z=\mathrm{id}\), \((1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta_z=e^{zT}\) and shifted coassociativity: for three blocks at \((x+z+w,y+w,t)\), compose rationally and then expand at \(w=\infty\), followed coefficientwise by \(z=\infty\). The comparison holds at \(\eta=0\) as well as at nonzero parameters, and joint faithfulness uses the whole family of finite site sets.
statements.antecedents: Kontsevich–Soibelman (2011); Tsymbaliuk (2021); Maillet–Sánchez de Santos (2000); Latyntsev (2021); Jindal–Kaubrys–Latyntsev (2026).

statements.title: The polar field and the oriented Hall operation
statements.text: For a geometric Hall or Hecke correspondence, compare its actual polar field with the oriented supported operation before proper flag forgetting. Work on a common two-input tensor and coefficient lattice with Cartan actions, moments, normal derivatives and both units. The one-loop zero-potential polynomial cobar preserves the regular operation on finite root jets in every charge. Matching that regular field leaves the singular part of the critical operation undetermined. At the charge-two node the nonzero cubic first lifts on the fourth cut. The strict chain map acts on a semifree resolution of the auxiliary jet with the closed odd generator retained. A geometric map must still identify the input on the flag giving that representative. [The cubic pole and its two cut tests](#atlas-c-co-05). At the first critical flag the incoming coefficient, both branches of the moment divisor and their intersection all participate in a single comparison.

statements.title: Actual Hall fields at finite precision and in the adic limit
statements.text: At each precision \(\mathbb Q[\eta]/(\eta^N)\), the one-loop construction has a free jet carrier, covariant fields, exchange and coassociative charge maps. Derivative pairing compares these with the Hall spectral coproduct and multiplication. The zero-potential cyclic three-loop quiver uses \(\mathbb Q[a,b,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^N)\), with \(h=a+b\), and permits arbitrary specialization of the loop weights. For a finite symmetric zero-potential quiver with an odd positive number of loops at every vertex, the coloured construction uses finite \(\epsilon\)-precision and the prescribed sign twist. Opposite arrows may carry independent weights. Transposing the exchange reverses the colour indices. For the shifted one-loop field on algebraic inputs of charges \(d,e\) and total jet order \(M\), the pole order is at most \(de+M\). Arbitrary adic inputs have values in \(\varprojlim_N W_N((z))\). At \(a=b=0\) the three-loop generator field already has a double pole for \(d=e=1,\ M=0\), even though its exchange is the identity.

statements.title: Polynomial one-loop cobar in every charge
statements.text: Put \(R=\mathbb Q[\hbar]\) and \(A_m=R[x_1,\dots,x_m]^{\mathfrak S_m}\) with shuffle factor \(\prod_{i,j}(1+\hbar/(x_i-x_j))\) between the two blocks. Let \(W_m\) be the dual of finite total root-jet support and \(S_R\) the quadratic algebra whose relations are the charge-two cobar boundaries. The augmented algebra map \(F_R:\Omega(W_R)\to S_R\) sends the charge-one jet \(J_i\) to \(i!a_i\) and every higher-charge generator to zero. It is a quasi-isomorphism over the polynomial ring on the algebraic sum of all charges. In charge \(m\), the ordered-partition bar contracts onto the top orientation. The deformed adjacent transpositions \(s_i+\hbar(1-s_i)/(x_i-x_{i+1})\) give the actual Hall merges. Each term in the contraction lowers root degree by at most \(\binom m2\), so its transpose increases support by at most that bound and preserves finite jets. The map preserves the moments, charge, translation, unit and regular operation \(Y(a,z)b=(e^{zT}a)b\). There is also a compatible inverse-limit comparison on the different recipient where support may grow with precision. The Cartan-relative bar retains the two Cartan actions and its ordered three-block identities.

statements.title: Scalar augmentation completion removes the charged part
statements.text: For the ordinary scalar augmentation ideal \(I\) in the Hall algebra with rank commutator, every positive Hall charge belongs to every \(I^k\). Its scalar augmentation completion is therefore exactly the completed Cartan. This obstruction concerns that scalar completion; it does not collapse the Cartan-relative charged bar or rule out the declared smooth and spectral recipients.
hypotheses: The ordinary scalar augmentation ideal in the Hall algebra with rank commutator.
Distinguish scalar augmentation from the Cartan-relative charged bar and its actual recipient.

rows.name: Celestial algebras of self-dual gauge theory
rows.summary: The tree two-tower current theory has graded algebraic duality and finite-on-input principal-parts operations. Its four-degree all-state quantum quotient has explicit ghosts and coupling modulo total translation. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2,\mathfrak{sl}_3\) the [nine-degree boundary quotient](#s-bb-celestial-d2-boundary-candidate) inherits the all-polynomial brackets and ordered basis through \(s^2\). Its ghost differential, coupling and module tensor remain open, as do full smooth quantum duality and physical sewing. For pure gauge theory with one anomaly-cancelling axion, the [cubic Ward identity with one closed current](#ch19-cubic-ward-identity) fixes a simple pole on the transverse polynomial plane in its stated sector. The scalar diagonal of the ordered collision fixes the first transvectant correction to the polynomial Hamiltonian bracket. Its [local Jacobi classification](#ch19-scalar-hamiltonian-bracket) leaves a formal parameter choice and gives a nonzero deformation class modulo constants. The ordered scalar product exists on the ramified coefficient ring. For the marked pure \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) four-tower presentation, all cubic generator identities and a free PBW basis hold over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^4)\). At fourth order the Ward identities hold at constant transverse output for all polynomial inputs and longitudinal descendants. The [total order-\(s^4\) double pole](#ch19-marked-sl2-cubic-closure) on \(e[x^2],f[y^2]\) has coefficients \(8/9\) and \(44/9\) on \(L_h^2\) and \(L_eL_f\) in units of \(\nu^2\). With the cubic brackets and ordered three-field residues fixed, the [quartic Ward identities on all polynomial jets](#ch19-quartic-current-outputs) give a free ordered vertex basis over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^5)\), with \(E[1]\) omitted. At [transverse degree one](#ch19-quartic-labelled-poles), the inputs \(J_e[x^3],J_f[y^2]\) give simple-pole coefficients \(26/3,-2/3\) when \(T\) acts on the first or the second field of \(L_e[x]L_f[1]\), respectively, in units of \(\nu^2\). The [open celestial comparison](#s-completed-and-quantum-celestial-duality) concerns the microscopic fields, the individual graph amplitudes, higher orders and a physical coproduct for two lines.
