statements.title: Tree-level graded duality
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with \(\epsilon\) even, so the second current tower is an abelian adjoint module. The universal level-zero current vertex algebra \(V(\mathfrak a)\) has polynomial ghost algebra \(B_{\mathrm{pol}}=C_*(\mathfrak a[t])^{\vee_{\mathrm{fib},t}}\), using the restricted dual in polynomial fibre degree and \(t\)-degree, with \(Qc^i=-\tfrac12f_{jk}{}^ic^jc^k\). There is a graded algebraic identification \(B_{\mathrm{pol}}\simeq(\operatorname{Bar}U(\mathfrak a[t]))^{\vee_{\mathrm{fib},t}}\); cobar recovers \(U(\mathfrak a[t])\), whose primitives and \(d/dt\) recover the current conformal algebra and then \(V(\mathfrak a)\). The coefficients are polynomial in ghosts and jets; full energy-homogeneous coefficient cochains and completed smooth duals have different carriers.

statements.title: A flat quantum quotient in four twistor degrees
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional and simple over \(\mathbb C\), normalize its invariant form \(K\) by long-root squared length two, and choose \(a,\ell\in\mathbb C\) satisfying \(2a\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{ad}}((\operatorname{ad}X)^4)=3\ell^2K(X,X)^2\) for every \(X\in\mathfrak g\). Over \(R=\mathbb C[s]/(s^3)\), with \(e_1=(1,0)\), \(e_2=(0,1)\), retain currents \(J[0],J[e_1],J[e_2],J[e_1+e_2],\widetilde J[0]\) and axions \(E[e_1],E[e_2],E[e_1+e_2],F[0]\), assign \(J[\alpha],E[\alpha]\) twistor degree \(\alpha\) and \(\widetilde J[\alpha],F[\alpha]\) degree \(\alpha+e_1+e_2\), and kill every state of total degree outside \(\{0,e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2\}\). This quotient admits an \(R\)-free one-loop vertex deformation with quadratic current coefficient \(s^2a\), linear coefficients \(-s^2h^\vee a/3\), \(-2s^2h^\vee a/3\), axion coupling \(s\ell\), and an explicit differential ghost vertex algebra, both free on their retained ordered derivative monomials. Their pairing \(I\) satisfies \(QI+\tfrac12I_{(0)}I=D_{\mathrm{tot}}H\) for an explicit \(H\), so \(Q+I_{(0)}\) squares to zero on the ghost algebra tensored with every ordinary untwisted module of this quotient; the coupling is Maurer–Cartan modulo total translation. At nonzero axion coupling the displayed state-level total derivative is nonzero; zero-mode square-zero does not imply the stronger state-level Maurer–Cartan equation.
statements.antecedents: Costello–Paquette (2022); Fernández–Paquette (2024); De Sole–Kac (2005); Gui–Li–Zeng (2022); Li (2016).

statements.title: Algebraic co-vacuum endomorphisms and the missing vacuum fibre
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional and simple, \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[u,v,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\) with \(\epsilon\) even, \(A=U(\mathfrak a[t,t^{-1}])\), \(\mathfrak p=\mathfrak a[t]\), and \(\mathfrak n=t^{-1}\mathfrak a[t^{-1}]\). Form the level-zero vacuum \(V=A\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}\mathbb C\) and co-vacuum \(W=A\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n)}\mathbb C\), inducing from the trivial modules, and compute derived Hom in all algebraic left \(A\)-modules with full algebraic cochains and product totalization. Then \(H^0\operatorname{REnd}_A(W)=U(\mathfrak a)^{\mathrm{op}}\), and \(\mathfrak a^*\) embeds as a split vector-space summand of \(H^1\operatorname{REnd}_A(W)\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{RHom}_A(W,V)=0\), whereas \(\mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(\mathfrak n)}V\simeq\mathbb C\).

statements.title: Divergence of the unrenormalized ghost pairing
statements.text: For the level-zero two-tower gauge current algebra \(\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with \(\mathfrak g\) finite-dimensional simple over \(\mathbb C\) and \(\epsilon\) even, use the vacuum polarization and normalize \(K\) by long-root squared length two. At total polynomial fibre-degree cutoff \(N\), the determinant cocycle on mode numbers \(m,-m\) of the constant currents is \(2h^\vee(N+1)(N+2)mK_{ab}\). It has no finite limit when \(mK_{ab}\ne0\), so this unrenormalized vacuum construction supplies no finite complementary-level ghost pairing.

statements.title: Completed and quantum celestial duality
statements.text:
For the two adjoint towers of a simple complex gauge Lie algebra, construct a completion and localization that compare smooth celestial modules with a curved or differential ghost dual, retaining the vacuum and all polynomial fibre degrees. Construct the ghost differential, coupling and module tensor for the [nine-degree boundary algebra](#s-bb-celestial-d2-boundary-candidate), and compare its collision operations with the local observables of an independently quantized self-dual gauge theory on twistor space. A finite-on-input principal-parts operator must be promoted to an algebra-valued operation on the chosen completed carrier before it can define the required coproduct and module tensor product.

For the four marked currents of pure \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) gauge theory with one axion, identify the renormalized microscopic defect fields whose collisions give the quartic brackets on every polynomial jet. The effective two-field pole specifies a sum. Separating the contributions from two open loops and from one loop with two axion vertices requires amplitudes for the individual graphs in the same normalization. Extending the [marked quartic algebra](#s-celestial-quartic-cartan-constraint) through order \(s^5\) or higher requires new brackets. A physical coproduct must also act on two independently prepared lines and reproduce the [mixed terms on independent backgrounds](#ch19-closed-current).

statements.title: The celestial boundary algebra on the nine transverse bidegrees
statements.text: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) or \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\), take the [four polynomial currents](#ch19-four-currents) over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^3)\), with axion coefficient \(\ell_0s\) and one-loop coefficient \(c_1=a_1s^2\). Give \(J[\alpha],E[\alpha]\) transverse bidegree \(\alpha\), and \(L[\alpha],F[\alpha]\) bidegree \(\alpha+(1,1)\). The axion field \(E[1]\) with constant transverse label is omitted. Both \(s\) and longitudinal translation have degree zero. The brackets preserve total bidegree. A normally ordered word of degree outside \(D_2=\{0,1,2\}^2\) therefore belongs to a vertex ideal, even when each letter has degree in \(D_2\). The quotient is free on the retained ordered words exactly at \(2a_1\gamma=3\ell_0^2\), with \(\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm ad}((\operatorname{ad}a)^4)=\gamma K(a,a)^2\) and \(\gamma=8,9\) for the two ranks, respectively. Indeed, for \(K(h,h)=2\), Jacobi on \(J_h[x],J_h[y],J_h[1]\) leaves \(2(2a_1\gamma-3\ell_0^2)s^2(T+\lambda+\mu)L_h[1]\). At equality the ordered polynomial brackets restrict to \(D_2\), and their ordered basis descends. The ghost differential, its coupling and the module tensor on this square remain open. In the [four-degree quotient](#s-a-flat-quantum-quotient-in-four-twistor-degrees) the coupling gives a square-zero differential on the ghost algebra tensored with each ordinary untwisted module. A tensor product between two such modules requires a separate construction.

statements.title: A cubic axion residue on the transverse polynomial plane
statements.text:
In the formal vacuum algebra of pure self-dual Yang–Mills theory with the anomaly-cancelling axion, take \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) and \(K(a,b)=\operatorname{tr}_3(ab)\). Let \(x,y\) be the transverse Taylor coordinates, normalized by \(\{x,y\}=1\). Insert the closed current \(E[x^2y]\) and the two positive-helicity currents \(J_{12}[x],J_{23}[y]\) in this order. The subscripts denote matrix units. The tree bracket of the two positive currents has colour \(E_{13}\) and label \(xy\). Take the positively oriented residue of \(E[x^2y](z)J_{13}[xy](w)\), dividing the contour integral by \(2\pi i\). In the resulting simple pole the coefficient of the two negative-helicity currents \(:L_{12}[1,0]L_{23}[0,0]:\) at cubic order is \(-s
u/9=+s^3/27\). Here \(s\) is the axion coupling and the one-loop coefficient is \(
u=-s^2/3\) in this normalization. The same normal product in the Jacobi residual computed from the lower brackets has the opposite coefficient.

For polynomial labels the Ward equation compares the Hamiltonian derivative on the two output slots of the ordered simplex integral with differentiation on each input. Their difference is a Hochschild coboundary. The normalized primitive vanishes on \(1,x,y\), and its recurrence respects interchange of the two coordinates because a Hamiltonian field has zero divergence. Counting both endpoint and colour orders in the symmetric output gives the coefficient \(-1/2\) multiplying this primitive in units of \(s
u\).
hypotheses: Keep the four-current lower brackets through order \(s^2\). The pure gauge source with one axion requires \(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\operatorname{ad}_a^4)=\gamma K(a,a)^2\) and \(\nu=-3s^2/\gamma\). In the displayed example \(\gamma=9\). The identity with one \(E\) and two \(J\) currents holds at cubic order on the whole transverse polynomial plane.

In the two-negative-current simple-pole sector, keep polynomial endpoint coefficients, adjoint colour equivariance and total output degree \(\deg p+\deg t-4\) for axion label \(p\) and gauge label \(t\). For perfect colour, full transverse \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) equivariance determines the solution uniquely. Prescribing its values on the constant and both linear gauge modes gives the same uniqueness without transverse symmetry. Nonperfect metric colour can admit central corrections. For the pure marked \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) table, the separate \(FJJ\) and \(JJJ\) calculations give a free cubic vertex algebra. Other metric colour algebras and microscopic generator identifications have their own comparison problems.

statements.title: The scalar Hamiltonian bracket determined by the diagonal collision
statements.text:
Fix \(\{x,y\}=1\) on a transverse symplectic plane. The Poisson brackets of \((x^3,y^3)\) and \((x^2y,xy^2)\) are \(9x^2y^2\) and \(3x^2y^2\). For the ordered one-loop collision, antisymmetrize the two Hamiltonian variations of the normalized endpoint primitive and subtract the variation for their Poisson bracket. Apply the resulting map to \(x\), divide by the difference of the two endpoint \(x\)-coordinates, then set the endpoints equal. The scalar readings on the two pairs are \(3\) and \(-1\). Write \(B_m(f,g)\) for the result of contracting the \(m\)-th derivatives of \(f\) and \(g\) across the two inputs with \(m\) copies of the Poisson bivector, then multiplying. Thus \(B_1\) is the Poisson bracket, and the scalar coefficient extracted from this collision is \(B_3/12\).

Let \(A=k[V]\). For the local scalar brackets specified below, Jacobi holds precisely for
\[
 [f,g]_t=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{\kappa(t)^j}{(2j+1)!}\,B_{2j+1}(f,g),\qquad \kappa(t)\in t k[[t]].
\]
On a fixed pair of polynomials only finitely many contractions contribute. The first correction \(tB_3/12\) fixes \(\kappa'(0)=1/2\). If the coefficient of \(t^j\) lowers total polynomial degree by \(4j+2\), then \(\kappa(t)=t/2\). In general use the unique parameter \(t'=2\kappa(t)\). With \(t'=u^2/2\), the bracket is the commutator of the Moyal product \(\mu\exp(u\pi/2)\) divided by \(u\), where \(\pi\) is the bivector and \(\mu\) is multiplication.

To see why the quintic term is forced, evaluate on exponential generating functions for polynomial inputs. Covariance makes the symbol an odd series \(F(z)\) of the symplectic pairing, with \(F'(0)=1\). The three-term Jacobi identity gives its addition law and hence \(F''=\kappa F\). In the homogeneous parameter, at pairings \(1,2,3\) the two cubic terms contribute \(+1/4\) to the coefficient of \(t^2\) in the cyclic Jacobiator. The term \(t^2z^5/480\) contributes \(-1/4\).
hypotheses: Let \(V\ne0\) be finite-dimensional symplectic over a characteristic-zero field \(k\). Take an alternating \(k[[t]]\)-bilinear bracket on \(k[V][[t]]\) with the Poisson classical fibre. Every coefficient must be a finite-order bidifferential operator with polynomial coefficients. Require translations and the full linear symplectic group to preserve it. Fix the Poisson bracket of every pair of linear Hamiltonians at every formal order.

The calibration \(t=u^2/2\) in the original parameter uses the homogeneous choice. For \(\kappa=t/2+t^2/7\), making that substitution directly gives an extra \(6u^4x/7\) on \((x^4,y^3)\). The result concerns the scalar diagonal. Descent and covariance of the full celestial fields and a physical coproduct require separate constructions.
statements.cite: J. E. Moyal, Quantum mechanics as a statistical theory, DOI 10.1017/S0305004100000487. D. B. Fairlie, P. Fletcher and C. K. Zachos, Trigonometric structure constants for new infinite-dimensional algebras, DOI 10.1016/0370-2693(89)91418-4.

statements.title: The diagonal correction survives quotienting by constants
statements.text:
On a Darboux plane with \(\{x,y\}=1\), quotient the polynomial Hamiltonians by constants. The two cubic pairs used to calibrate \(B_3/12\) give constants, so their diagonal values disappear. Use instead the combination of input pairs \(5(x^4,y^3)-12(x^3y,xy^2)\). Its Poisson brackets cancel. The third transvectants on the two pairs are \(144x\) and \(-36x\). The normalized combination gives \(96x\), whose derivative at the origin is \(96\).

For any \(k\)-linear one-cochain \(\alpha:A/k\to A/k\), that derivative vanishes on the same combination of its Chevalley–Eilenberg coboundaries. The bracket terms cancel and the four input Hamiltonians vanish to order at least three, so their Hamiltonian vector fields vanish to order at least two. The class of \(B_3/12\) in \(H^2(A/k,A/k)\) is therefore nonzero. An equivalence linear over \(k[[t]]\) and equal to the identity modulo \(t\) cannot trivialize this marked deformation. A distinct test concerns Jacobi: omitting the canonical quintic term on the triple \((x^5,y^5,x^2y)\) leaves \(600t^2x\) at second order, which also survives the quotient.
hypotheses: Use polynomial Hamiltonians on a nonzero finite-dimensional symplectic space over a field \(k\) of characteristic zero and the induced coefficientwise local brackets modulo constants. The witness lies on one Darboux plane. Constants have zero bracket. The derivative at the origin is well defined modulo constants even for an arbitrary linear primitive.

The cohomological obstruction concerns equivalences that induce the identity modulo the parameter. The Jacobi calculation concerns the specified finite Taylor polynomial. Intrinsically defined operations on the quotient and operations on the full celestial fields require their own comparisons.

statements.title: The coefficient ring of the ordered Hamiltonian product
statements.text:
On a Darboux plane with \(\{x,y\}=1\), an ordered product realizing the marked bracket must account for the commutator of \(x,y\). Put \(A=k[V]\) and \(R=k[[t]]\). Let \(L_\kappa\) be the scalar Lie bracket with transvectant coefficients \(\kappa(t)^j/(2j+1)!\) in odd orders, for nonzero \(\kappa\in tR\). A local covariant unital product on the same functions, equal to ordinary multiplication modulo \(t\), can have raw commutator \(dL_\kappa\) for nonzero \(d\in R\) exactly when \(\kappa=w^2\) with \(w\in tR\). For each such \(w\) its symbol is \(\exp(wz)\), where \(z\) pairs the two momenta, and \(d=2w\). The unit and associativity give \(G(0)=1\) and \(G(u+v)=G(u)G(v)\) for the symbol. The linear and cubic commutator coefficients then give the two identities for \(d\) and \(\kappa\).

The diagonal collision fixes \(\kappa=t/2+O(t^2)\), of valuation one. Adjoin a root over \(R\) to obtain \(R'=R[w]/(w^2-\kappa)\cong k[[w]]\), free on \(1,w\). The Moyal parameter is \(u=2w\), so \(t'=2\kappa=u^2/2\). Reducing the product modulo \(w\) gives ordinary multiplication. Reducing modulo \(t\) gives \(fg+w\{f,g\}\) on plain inputs over \(k[w]/(w^2)\). Its raw commutator on \(x,y\) is \(2w\). If it came by scalar extension, even up to an \(R'\)-algebra isomorphism, from an associative \(R\)-algebra \(C\), reduction modulo \(w\) would make \(C/tC\) commutative. Every extended commutator would then lie in \((t)=(w^2)\), contradicting this value.

The symmetric Jordan product \(J_\kappa\) and the raw commutator divided by \(2w\) both descend to \(R\). The left-minus-right Jordan associator on \((x^2,y,y^2)\) is \(-4\kappa y\). Restricting scalars retains the ordered product on \(A[[t]]\oplus A[[t]]\): identify \((a,b)\) with \(a+wb\). The product of \((f,0)\) and \((g,0)\) is \((J_\kappa(f,g),L_\kappa(f,g))\), so the commutator of \((x,0),(y,0)\) is \((0,2)\). Bilinearity and the relation \(w^2=\kappa\) determine both components for arbitrary pairs.
hypotheses: Use polynomial functions on a nonzero finite-dimensional symplectic space over a characteristic-zero field, coefficientwise finite-order bidifferential operations, translation and full linear symplectic covariance, and the constant unit \(1\). Fix the bracket of linear Hamiltonians. Opposite multiplication exchanges the signs of \(w\).

The scalar Lie bracket induces an operation modulo constants. The unital associative product and its symmetric part act on functions. The no-descent argument also applies to the completed tensor product for a separated \(t\)-adically complete algebra \(C\). Matching products on full celestial fields requires an independent map.

statements.title: The marked four-tower vertex algebra through cubic order
statements.text:
In the formal vacuum presentation of pure self-dual Yang–Mills theory with one axion, take \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(K=\operatorname{tr}_2\), \([e,f]=h\), \(K(e,f)=1\), \(K(h,h)=2\). The four towers are the positive and negative gauge currents \(J,L\) and the closed currents \(E,F\). Keep both transverse polynomial labels, both longitudinal bracket parameters and the translations of the two output fields. In the simple pole of \(J_a[p]\) with \(J_b[q]\), project to the constant normal product \(:F[0,0]L_{[a,b]}[0,0]:\). Divide the coefficient by \(\ell\nu\), with \(\ell=s\) and \(\nu=-3s^2/8\). On the ordered pairs \((x^2,y^2)\) and \((xy,xy)\) the linearly transverse-equivariant values are \(-4/3\) and \(+2/3\). At coincident endpoints the coefficient is minus one third of the second Poisson transvectant, giving these two numbers directly.

The displayed Fernández–Paquette coefficient for the \(FL\) word satisfies the three-positive-current Ward equation and gives \(-2,0\) on the same pairs. With the separately determined \(EJ,FJ\) brackets in force, a local change of the positive current changes the \(FL\) coefficient by \(-\eta(pq)+p(V)\eta(q)+q(V)\eta(p)\), where \(V\) is the negative endpoint and \(\eta\) vanishes below total input degree four. On the indicated output \(\eta(x^2y^2)=-2/3\). The three \(EL\) coefficients retain their separate derivative placements and spectral term. In the three-positive-current identity the remaining scalar is symmetric in the three labelled inputs, so the cyclic colour commutators cancel by Lie Jacobi. The homogeneous changes are current redefinitions. Full transverse equivariance fixes the representative on the marked linear generators.

The \(EJJ,FJJ\) identities use their respective two-negative-current operations. The \(LJJ\) identity has no cubic contribution, and the other sixteen unordered triples have at most one positive current. Their possible outputs are regular with the remaining field. This covers all twenty types. Longitudinal differentiation gives every descendant identity. With degree \(|p|+2\) on a generator of transverse degree \(|p|\) and zero degree on translation and the spectral variable, every bracket lowers the sum of its input degrees. Ordered monomials in derivatives of the strong generators, omitting \(E[0,0]\), are therefore a free basis of the universal vertex algebra over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^4)\). Its associated graded is the symmetric differential algebra. Translation gives the relative chiral algebra on the affine coordinate line.
hypotheses: Use the specified purely even four-tower algebra, its normalized lower brackets, the separate all-polynomial \(EJJ\) and \(FJJ\) operations and the change of the \(FL\) coefficient on linearly transforming transverse generators. The invariant quartic trace factor is \(8\) for this trace form. Keep the order of the fields, the divided residue and both output slots.

An unmodified mixed table can fail the \(EJJ\) identity. A map from microscopic quantum defect generators to these marked fields must be constructed separately. This cubic basis is over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^4)\). With the ordered three-field residues fixed, the [quartic Ward identities](#s-celestial-quartic-cartan-constraint) hold on all polynomial jets and give a free ordered basis over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^5)\). Other colour algebras require their own lower brackets and Ward identities.

statements.title: Quartic Ward identities and an ordered basis for the marked four-current algebra
statements.text:
Insert \(J_h[1],J_e[x^2],J_f[y^2]\) in that order in the formal vacuum of pure self-dual \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) gauge theory with one axion. The bracket of the last two currents can produce two negative currents \(L\). Which double pole makes the three contours obey Jacobi? Here \([1]\) denotes a constant transverse label, \(T\) differentiates along the curve, and \(\lambda,\mu\) are the contour parameters. Set \(L_a=L_a[1]\) and extract the coefficient of \(\lambda^1\mu^0L_h^2\) at order \(s^4\). The fixed lower brackets give \(-s^4/8\). Holding the other brackets fixed, changing the printed cubic \(FL\) coefficient to the linearly equivariant one adds \(s^4/4\) to this coefficient.

In the total order-\(s^4\) bracket of \(J_e[x^2]\) with \(J_f[y^2]\), which receives both two-open-loop terms and one-loop terms with two axion vertices, take the constant transverse part of each output field and give the coefficients in units of \(\nu^2=9s^4/64\). Write \(B_{hh}\) for the coefficient of \(L_h^2\) in the double pole and \(A\) for the three-field simple pole. In the order \(J_i(L_jL_k)\) the contraction of \(A\) with \(J_h[1]\) gives \(W(A)=8/3\). The Ward identity \(W(A)-2B_{hh}=8/9\) fixes \(B_{hh}=8/9\). Now replace the first two inputs by \(J_h[x],J_e[x]\). Their tree bracket is \(2J_e[x^2]\), so this identity also detects the coefficient of \(L_eL_f\). The resulting double pole is \((8/9)L_h^2+(44/9)L_eL_f\). The two-field simple pole is \((8/9)(TL_h)L_h+(44/9)(TL_e)L_f\). Its coefficient on \(L_e(TL_f)\) is zero.

For arbitrary polynomial inputs \(p,q\), the [constant-output bracket](#ch19-marked-sl2-cubic-closure) multiplies these colour coefficients by \((p_{xx}q_{yy}-2p_{xy}q_{xy}+p_{yy}q_{xx})(0)/4\). This is the second [Poisson transvectant](#ch19-poisson-transvectant), evaluated at the origin and divided by four. It equals one on \(x^2,y^2\). Apply this projection after composing. The intermediate bracket on \(J_e[x],J_f[y]\), for example, contains the axion field \(-sF[1]\).

Insert a gauge-current spectator with linear label \(x\) or \(y\) and set its contour frequency to zero. Jacobi now expresses the unknown operation on \(xp,q\) or \(yp,q\) in terms of operations whose first input is \(p\). Constant and linear first inputs give zero by the transverse weight bound. This proves uniqueness in the prescribed class. To check that the resulting brackets satisfy Jacobi, move the two distinct transverse endpoints to \((1,0)\) and \((0,0)\) by affine covariance of the combined open and closed brackets. In particular \(\partial_xF[4xy]=F[4y]-TE[xy^2]\). This longitudinal term is needed for transverse translation covariance. The shear \(y\partial_x\) fixes these endpoints and reduces the remaining equation to the inputs \(x^i,x^j y\), for all \(i,j\geq 0\). Read the double pole in its symmetric lift and the simple pole with the derivative on the first labelled output. In each coefficient the open contribution and the two orders of axion exchange sum to zero. For \(i=j=1\) their respective pairs are \((16/3,32/9)\), \((0,-16/9)\) and \((-16/3,-16/9)\), in units of \(\nu^2\). The two rational cancellations hold for every pair of exponents, and polynomiality includes coincident endpoints.

For the fixed cubic brackets and ordered three-field residues, the two-field quartic operation is unique in the local polynomial class. The full brackets satisfy the [generator Jacobi identities at every transverse output degree](#ch19-quartic-current-outputs) for all polynomial inputs. Sesquilinearity gives every longitudinal translation descendant. Over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^5)\) the enveloping vertex algebra is free on ordered normal monomials in the four towers and their longitudinal derivatives, with \(E[1]\) omitted.

Give a generator of transverse degree \(n\) filtration degree \(n+2\), and give longitudinal translation degree zero. The quartic three-field terms lower the sum of the input degrees by two and the two-field terms lower it by four. The [ordered-monomial argument](#ch19-marked-sl2-cubic-pbw) then gives the basis over the quartic coefficient ring. Its associated graded is the symmetric differential algebra.
hypotheses: Use the formal vacuum algebra of pure \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) self-dual gauge theory with one axion. The positive and negative gauge currents \(J,L\) and the closed currents \(E,F\) have transverse labels in \(\mathbb C[x,y]\), with \(E[1]\) omitted. Fix \([e,f]=h\), \(K(a,b)=\operatorname{tr}_2(ab)\), \(K(e,f)=1\), \(K(h,h)=2\), \(\ell=s\) and \(\nu=\hbar/(16\pi^2)=-3s^2/8\). The two-loop unit is \(\nu^2=9s^4/64\).

Fix the linearly transverse-equivariant cubic brackets and the ordered three-field residues. In the bracket of two positive currents, sum the three placements of the positive letter in the right-associated product \(J_i(L_jL_k)\). In the mixed bracket use the ordered three-negative-field residue. Their common ordered scalar on \(x^2,y^2\) with three constant outputs is \(-1/6\) in units of \(\nu^2\).

The \(d,e\) terms of Fernández and Paquette, from one loop with two axion vertices, can contribute to the two-field poles at order \(s^4\). Beyond the open chain computed with the equivariant cubic coefficient, the axial double pole adds \(28/9\) on \(L_aL_b\) for the transverse inputs \(x^2,y^2\), in units of \(\nu^2\). Omitting it leaves \(+7s^4/8\) as the coefficient of \(\lambda L_eL_f\) on the positive-spectator triple. For the graph grading see Fernández and Paquette, arXiv:2412.17168v2, equations (2.19)–(2.21), PDF p. 19 (printed p. 17). For the two-field coefficients see Appendix B.6.2, PDF p. 62. The Ward equations fix the total poles in this marking. Individual graph amplitudes and identification of the microscopic currents remain open.

rows.name: Celestial self-dual gravity and the Moyal deformation
rows.summary: The Poisson bracket of \(x,y\) is the constant \(1\). Both constant towers are retained in the graded duality for polynomial Hamiltonian currents. With a Laurent loop variable, the [Hessian three-cocycle](#s-an-obstruction-beyond-local-cochains) is nonzero even in all algebraic cochains with adjoint polynomial coefficients. The [formal Moyal dual](#s-polynomial-moyal-cochains-are-not-closed) exists, but at numerical nonzero parameter the ghost of \(1\) has infinitely many terms in its differential. Smooth quantum modules, continuous compatibility with products and brackets, and the global bulk comparison remain open.

object.note: Universal level-zero Hamiltonian currents, with both constant modes retained

dual.note: Poisson graded dual; formal Moyal dual; numerical polynomial dual fails

modules.note: Algebraic Laurent-mode modules over a field; smooth comparison open

fusion.note: Classical principal-parts complexes on smooth inputs at distinct points

bulk.note: Identify local bulk operations with vacuum self-extensions in the stated gravity theory

lines.note: Classical Moyal twist on one affine twistor chart

states.note: For the universal sphere vacuum and outgoing mode bounds \(k\le2-|\alpha|,\ k\le-6-|\alpha|\) in the two towers, ordinary coinvariants are the vacuum line. Derived or physical state comparisons remain open.

dictionary.note: Local classical Moyal comparison; quantum and global maps open

statements.title: Tree-level algebraic duality
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(R=\mathbb C[v_1,v_2]\) with \(\{f,g\}=\partial_1f\,\partial_2g-\partial_2f\,\partial_1g\), and let \(\mathfrak a=(R,\{\ ,\ \})\otimes\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with even \(\epsilon\) and both constant Hamiltonians retained. The universal level-zero current vertex algebra is \(V(\mathfrak a)=U(\mathfrak a[t,t^{-1}])\otimes_{U(\mathfrak a[t])}\mathbb C\); its polynomial ghost algebra is the dual of the homological Chevalley–Eilenberg coalgebra of \(\mathfrak a[t]\), restricted jointly by the shifted fibre degree \(\deg(v^\alpha)=\alpha-(1,1)\) and \(t\)-degree, and is quasi-isomorphic to the corresponding restricted dual of \(\operatorname{Bar}U(\mathfrak a[t])\). The cobar of that coalgebra recovers \(U(\mathfrak a[t])\), whose primitives and translation recover \(V(\mathfrak a)\).

statements.title: An obstruction beyond local cochains
statements.text: Let \(S=\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,z,z^{-1}]\) carry the Poisson bracket in \(v_1,v_2\), and give \(S\) its adjoint module structure over \(\mathfrak h=(S,\{\ ,\ \})\). With \(\mathrm{vol}=dv_1\wedge dv_2\wedge dz\), \(\partial^1=\partial_2\), \(\partial^2=-\partial_1\), and \(J_f=(\partial^a\partial_bf)\), define \(\iota_{\psi(f,g)}\mathrm{vol}=\operatorname{tr}(dJ_f\wedge dJ_g)\) and \(\Phi(f,Y)=\sum_{a,b=1}^2\partial_a\partial^b\bigl(Y(\partial^a\partial_bf)\bigr)\). The cocycle \(\Omega_H(f,g,h)=\Phi(f,\psi(g,h))+\Phi(g,\psi(h,f))+\Phi(h,\psi(f,g))\) represents a nonzero class in \(H^3(\mathfrak h;S)\) computed with all algebraic cochains. No algebraic two-cochain has differential equal to this cocycle.

statements.title: Polynomial Moyal cochains are not closed
statements.text: For polynomial functions on \(\mathbb C^2\), set \(f*_hg=m\exp(\tfrac h2(\partial_1\otimes\partial_2-\partial_2\otimes\partial_1))(f\otimes g)\) and \(b_h(f,g)=(f*_hg-g*_hf)/h\). At every fixed \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\), the finite-polynomial ghost dual is not preserved by the Chevalley–Eilenberg differential: the constant coefficient of \(b_h(v_1^{2r+1},v_2^{2r+1})\) is \((2r+1)!h^{2r}/2^{2r}\) for every \(r\ge0\). The homological Chevalley–Eilenberg coalgebra remains defined, and \(h\)-adic cochains provide the formal dual.

statements.title: Quantum smooth modules and the physical comparison
statements.text: For the universal Hamiltonian current algebra over \(\mathbb C\) and, separately, its \(h\)-adic Moyal deformation or specialization at fixed \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\), construct a completed dual and an equivalence for discrete smooth modules, with common domains for collision operations and exchange. Extend the classical twist on an affine twistor chart to a global comparison with an independently quantized bulk theory, keeping the graviton and axion contributions to the quantum brackets separate.

statements.title: Separate graviton and axion kernels
statements.text: If the physical graviton and axion contributions are assigned a common loop kernel, the checked linear residual constrains their sum; it does not identify the two contributions separately. Finite tests imposing equality of those sectors do not establish an all-input physical kernel identity. The Hessian obstruction remains a statement about the fixed Laurent Hamiltonian source and adjoint polynomial module, even with all algebraic cochains, while an essentially higher source is a different target.

rows.name: D3 branes and Hilbert-scheme vertex algebras
rows.summary: At every rank the boundary BRST algebra is a proper odd-zero-mode kernel in the specified numerical Hilbert-scheme sections. Formal sheaf cohomology retains its sharp range, determinant torsion and nonseparated information. At reduced rank two, the two largest-spin torsion components and the first two occurrence representations are determined at every positive fermion charge. At rank two the torus-finite part of \(H^1\) maps isomorphically to that of its separated completion. Finite torsion intervals at bounded horizontal highest weight contribute zero after torus-finite specialization. Continuous smooth duality, finite-rank collision fusion and the independent bulk/defect comparison remain open.

object.note: Exact BRST kernel at every rank; finite parts precede \(\hbar=1\)

dual.note: Classical bar models and the curved bar of finite words in vacuum modes

modules.note: Completed smooth-module duality preserving the vacuum

fusion.note: Collision tensor category for the finite-rank boundary algebra

bulk.note: Formal sheaf cohomology through degree \(N-1\), torsion and nonseparated blocks; independent physical bulk map open

lines.note: Native defects and their action on boundary modules

statements.title: The boundary algebra is a proper kernel
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for every integer \(N\ge1\), let \(C_{\mathrm{fr}}\) be the polynomial relative \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) BRST complex with adjoint and fundamental symplectic bosons and fundamental fermions at numerical \(\hbar=1\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be the corresponding Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex sheaf on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\). Put \(K_N=H^0(C_{\mathrm{fr}})\) and \(V_N=\Gamma(M_N,\mathcal D)_{\mathrm{fin}}/(\hbar-1)\), taking the torus-finite part before specialization, and write \(\chi^-=\phi\gamma\) for the invariant contraction of a fundamental fermion with a fundamental symplectic boson. The natural map identifies \(K_N\) with \(\ker(\chi^-_{(0)}:V_N\to V_N)\), and \(V_N=K_N\oplus\tau_{(-1)}K_N\) as graded vector spaces, where \(\tau\) is an odd global section of conformal weight zero with \(\chi^-_{(0)}\tau=N\).

statements.title: The sharp formal cohomology range
statements.text: For every integer \(N\ge1\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the \(\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\)-complete Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller vertex sheaf on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\). For each of \(\mathcal D\), every quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar^m\mathcal D\) with integer \(m\ge1\), and the classical quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar\mathcal D\), its sheaf cohomology is nonzero exactly in degrees \(0\le k<N\). These groups are taken before numerical specialization.

statements.title: An exact determinant-torsion algebra
statements.text: For \(N\ge2\), on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex sheaf over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), let \(\beta\) be the connecting map for \(0\to\mathcal D\xrightarrow{\hbar}\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/\hbar\mathcal D\to0\), and put \(\kappa_r=T^r\beta(\phi\psi)\), where \(\phi\psi\) is the classical invariant contraction of the two fundamental fermions. The normal-cup subalgebra generated by the scalar vacuum and the \(\kappa_r\), using finite sums and finite products, is \[\frac{R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Lambda(e_0,e_1,\ldots)}{(\hbar e_r\ (r\ge0),\ \Lambda^{\ge N})},\qquad e_r\mapsto\kappa_r.\] Each \(e_r\) has sheaf degree one, intrinsic even parity and conformal weight \(r+1\); the exterior sign comes from sheaf degree, and there is no completion in the translation index. Every nonempty increasing product of fewer than \(N\) generators is nonzero and not \(\hbar\)-divisible, remains nonzero in every finite \(\hbar\)-quotient, and vanishes under torus-finite specialization at \(\hbar=1\).

statements.title: A completed D3 duality and bulk map
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for the boundary vertex algebras at every finite rank \(N\ge1\) and their polynomial rank-parameter family, construct a completed chiral Koszul dual together with a specified category of smooth modules and a functorial equivalence preserving the vacuum and collisions. Compare that construction with independently defined twisted bulk observables and defects, including the normalization of the rank parameter; the classical bar models and the finite-word vacuum-mode algebra do not supply this comparison. In rank two the [torus-finite projection](#ch14-torus-finite-classes-and-separated-completion) identifies the torus-finite parts of the formal \(H^1\) and its separated completion. A continuous duality for the full completed complex must retain both the formal torsion and the nonzero kernel of projection to the separated completion. A rank-changing Hall action cannot commute with the conformal modes in the naive way: the central charge changes by \(-3(2N+1)\), so a compatible stress-tensor intertwining law must be supplied. The stable trace comparison holds only in \(2h\le N\), with its first deficit at weight \((N+1)/2\).

statements.title: Completed rank-two torsion blocks
statements.text:
Put \(t=\hbar\), of torus weight one. For the reduced formal vertex sheaf on \(\operatorname{Hilb}^2(\mathbb C^2)\), complete the direct sum of the two-chart complexes \(t\)-adically before taking its degree-one cohomology \(E\). This module is derived complete and contains torsion of arbitrarily large finite order. Its nonseparated part \(\bigcap_{n\ge1}t^nE\) is the nonzero Milnor term, the kernel of all fixed-conformal-weight projections. Write \(M_{\rm fin}\) for the finite sums of torus weight vectors in a module \(M\). The [projection to the separated completion](#ch14-torus-finite-classes-and-separated-completion) \(\widehat E_{\rm sep}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1} E/t^nE\) induces an isomorphism \(E_{\rm fin}\simeq(\widehat E_{\rm sep})_{\rm fin}\) of graded \(\mathbb C[t]\)-modules. It remains an isomorphism after taking these finite parts modulo \(t-1\).

At fixed conformal weight and reduced fermion number \(f\), the integral chart powers require flavour \(F\equiv f\pmod 2\). A finite interval \([i,j)\) has torus birth \(\mu=i-f/2\) and relation weight \(\delta=j-f/2\). In a homogeneous representative of a kernel class of weight \(u\), each nonzero monomial \(t^{u-\mu}\) is divisible by \(t^{j-i}\), so \(\delta\le u\). The [endpoint estimate](#ch14-generator-weights-at-fixed-horizontal-spin) \(\mu+\delta\ge-1\) bounds its order by \(2u+1\). Only finitely many entries of a \(t\)-adically vanishing family can have such orders, and their primitives give a boundary. In an abstract completed direct sum of maps \(t^n\), \(n\ge1\), give the target generators weights \(1/2-n\). The family \((t^n)_n\) then represents a nonzero kernel class of weight \(1/2\). Its only coordinatewise primitive \((1)_n\) lies outside the completed direct sum. Here \(\mu+\delta=1-n\).

For weights \(s_\ell\), let \(V(s)\) consist of the scalar families with only finitely many nonzero entries at \(s_\ell\ge B\) for each real \(B\). The [torsion intervals at specialization](#ch14-torsion-at-torus-finite-specialization) contribute \(V(\mu)/V(\delta)\). Since \(\delta\ge0\), the denominator consists of finite-support families. This quotient vanishes [at bounded horizontal highest weight](#ch14-specialization-at-bounded-horizontal-spin). On the infinite support of a representative of a nonzero class, the reduced births tend to \(-\infty\), while the reduced charges, highest weights, relation weights and interval lengths all tend to \(+\infty\). The full interval quotient is zero exactly when the actual birth weights are uniformly bounded below, and otherwise has complex dimension \(2^{\aleph_0}\). Which alternative occurs over all sectors is open. Free summands contribute a separate \(V(s)\) for their generator weights. Adjoining the global symplectic-boson and \(bc\) spectators before completion adds the same nonnegative weight to both endpoints, including shift zero for the vacuum. The isomorphism on finite parts and the specialization criterion hold for the full sheaf as well. The ordinary vertex-module interpretation additionally requires conformal local finiteness.

statements.title: The top torsion representation at every positive reduced charge
statements.text: In the rank-two calculation, remove the \(\mathrm{Sb}\otimes bc\) spectators and work over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\). For positive reduced fermion number \(r\), put \(a=\lfloor(r-1)/2\rfloor\), \(h=r(r-2)/2+q\), \(d=2q-r\) and \(\mu=a-r/2\). Torsion first occurs at \(q=a+1=\lceil r/2\rceil\). At every \(q\ge a+1\), its full highest-weight-\(d\) component is \[\mathcal T_{r,q}[d]\cong R/(\hbar^{q-a})[\mu]\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{d}\mathbb C^2.\] The divided \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) action is defined on the torsion-free sheaf before cohomology. The projected normal-current map between adjacent top components is \(\hbar\) times the specified Cartan product; lower-spin outputs can occur before projection. Spectators shift total charge and conformal weight.

statements.title: The next torsion spin and the first two occurrences
statements.text:
In the spectator-free rank-two calculation, let \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), take positive reduced fermion number \(r\), and set \(a=\lfloor(r-1)/2\rfloor\), \(d=2q-r\), with conformal weight \(h=r(r-2)/2+q\). For \(q\ge a+2\), the multiplicity module of highest weight \(d-2\) is \(R/(\hbar^{q-1})[-1/2]\) when \(r=1\); it is \((R/(\hbar^{q-1-a})[-1/2])^{\oplus2}\) when \(r\ge3\) is odd; and it is \(R/(\hbar^{q-1-a})[-1]\oplus R/(\hbar^{q-2-a})[0]\) when \(r\) is even. Zero-length summands are omitted. The first two occurrence energies have complete representation descriptions.

For \(r=1,\ q=3\), the conformal weight is \(5/2\) and \(d=5\). At highest weight \(d-4=1\), the three graded torsion intervals before the birth shift \(-1/2\) are \([0,1),[0,2),[1,2)\). Their lengths are \(1,2,1\), and their generators have torus degrees \(-1/2,-1/2,+1/2\). The [two-chart calculation](#fig-d3-three-torsion-intervals) removes the flavour-weight \(-3\) intervals from those at \(-1\) to isolate the doublets. The same subtraction counts a specified interval at highest weight \(m\) by removing its multiplicity at flavour \(-m-2\) from that at \(-m\).

At any reduced fermion number \(f\), integral Laurent powers require \(F\equiv f\pmod 2\) for a flavour \(F\) to occur. Every finite interval \([i,j)\) there satisfies the [endpoint bound](#ch14-rank-two-relation-weights) \(2j-|f|\ge |F|\). In a highest-weight-\(m\) multiplet, flavour \(m\) gives relation weight \(j-f/2\ge m/2+\max(0,-f)\). The same flavour subtraction bounds the degree in which the representation can occur. Write \(\ell-f/2\) for a torus weight. If \(2\ell-|f|<-m-2\), the chart matrices at flavours \(-m\) and \(-m-2\) have the same rows in shifted degree \(\ell\) and no columns there. Equal dimensions leave no copy of \(\operatorname{Sym}^m\mathbb C^2\) in that degree of polynomial \(H^1\). Thus occurrence requires \(2\ell-|f|\ge-m-2\) on the whole degree-one cohomology. At the birth \(\ell=i\), this gives the [bounds at fixed horizontal highest weight](#ch14-generator-weights-at-fixed-horizontal-spin) \(|f|-2i-2\le m\le 2j-|f|\) and \(i+j\ge |f|-1\). The degree and interval bounds persist on completion of each fixed sector.

At \(f=r>0\), adding birth and length gives \(q-r/2=d/2\) in the top component and \(q-1-r/2=(d-2)/2\) in each nonzero summand of the next component. At \(h=7/2,\ f=-1\), the doublet has interval \([1,2)\) at both flavours \(\pm1\). Its relation has weight \(5/2\), strictly above the bound \(3/2\). At even charge \(f=2s>0\), the first torsion energy \(q=s\) gives the singlet interval \([s-1,s)\). Its torus birth is \(-1\), its relation weight is \(0\), and \(i+j=2s-1\). It attains both bounds on \(m=0\). At highest weight \(m\le M\) the torus births are bounded below by \(-(M+2)/2\). A uniform bound as charge, conformal weight and highest weight all vary, and a closed formula for the all-weight interval character, remain open.

rows.name: M2 branes and the two-matrix algebra
rows.summary: Polynomial transport is established through arity five at every positive rank and through all arities at ranks at most four. The particle cohomology duality at \(c=0\), the rational full-complex model and the integral model for \(N\le3\) have different inputs. At fixed nonzero numerical \(\hbar\), algebraic sewing has \(\operatorname{Tor}_1=0\) and a split degree-two flux cap at every rank. Its degree-two flux class has zero Yoneda square at every positive rank. The fixed marked cocycle has no primitive of uniform finite spatial jet order at nonzero numerical Weyl parameter. The remaining flux kernel and other higher operations, all-rank all-arity transport and the independent five-dimensional physical comparison remain open. For the universal rank parameter \(\nu\), the all-arity bound is total input degree 24 with the specified quadratic-relative lower maps. Arity five in every polynomial degree has its separate fixed-ternary hypotheses.

object.note: The full \(GL_N\)-invariant polynomial antighost complex \(K_N^{\rm full}\) is nonformal over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\) for \(N\ge3\). The [absolute traceless rank-two complex](#s-bb-m2-absolute-rank-two-source) has a separate degree-three Chevalley class and a nonzero secondary operation.

dual.note: Cohomology curved dual; rational full-complex model at all ranks; integral model for \(N\le3\)

modules.note: At \(c=0\), fixed \(\hbar\ne0\), ordinary derived particle modules have the stated curved comodule/contramodule comparison; a separate integral full-complex quotient is known for \(N\le3\)

fusion.note: Obstructions to strict counital curved cooperation; physical fusion open

bulk.note: The fixed flux class has zero algebraic Yoneda square in every positive rank. Its prescribed cocycle has no uniformly finite spatial-jet primitive at nonzero numerical Weyl parameter.

lines.note: First-order algebraic line model; supported quantum line map open

states.note: At fixed \(\hbar\ne0\), the sewing kernel is idempotent: \(\operatorname{Tor}_1=0\), while \(\operatorname{Tor}_2\) has a split nonzero flux cap at every rank

dictionary.note: Integral arity five at all ranks; all arities for \(N\le4\)

statements.title: Polynomial transport without inverting the parameter
statements.text:
Let \(N\ge1\), work over \(\mathbb Q[h]\), and give \(L_h=\mathbb Q[x,y][h]\) the divided Moyal bracket \(b_h=(f*_hg-g*_hf)/h\), with \([x,y]_* =h\). Let \(K_N\) be the polynomial \(GL_N\)-invariant quantum two-matrix BRST complex, with \([X_{ij},Y_{kl}]=h\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}\), the moment matrix \(YX-XY+hNI\), antighost degree \(-1\), and \(\operatorname{Tr}\psi=0\), using divided graded commutators in the target. The first map sends one polynomial \(f\) to its symmetrized trace \(J(f)=\operatorname{Tr}\operatorname{Sym}f\). To extend it to an \(L_\infty\) map one needs a multilinear component \(J_n:\Lambda^n L_h	o K_N\) of ghost degree \(1-n\) on each group of \(n\) inputs. These are the Taylor maps. They exist over \(\mathbb Q[h]\) through arity five on all polynomial inputs, and in every arity when \(1\le N\le4\). At each proved arity, coupling equations use the arity-completed space \(\prod_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q[h]}(\Lambda^nL_h,K_N)\) with divided convolution bracket; the ordinary associative convention instead uses source bracket \(hb_h\) and Taylor maps multiplied by \(h^{n-1}\). Over \(\mathbb Q[
u,h]\) the construction through arity four applies to all polynomial inputs. At fifth order, the relation \(
u E=\delta_h\widehat\zeta\) for the obstruction \(E\) gives a primitive at each \(
u=N>0\) by division by the integer \(N\). The [degree-24 theorem](#atlas-c-brane-m2-degree24-candidate) bounds total input degree. A [separate primitive for fixed lower maps](#atlas-c-brane-m2-universal-fixed-ternary-transport) gives arity five in all polynomial degrees under its additional symbol and homology hypotheses.

statements.title: The degree-two correction to algebraic sewing
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), with algebraic tensor products and ordinary derived functors, fix \(\hbar\ne0\) and \(N\ge1\), let \(W=\mathbb C\langle x,y\rangle/(xy-yx-\hbar)\), \(\mathfrak g=W^{\mathrm{Lie}}\), \(U_N=U(\mathfrak g)/(z-N1)\), where \(z\) denotes the central Lie element \(1_W\), and \(A_N=(W^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\). For the algebraic power-sum map \(U_N\to A_N\), \(J(f)\mapsto\sum_i f^{(i)}\), the multiplication \(A_N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U_N}A_N\to A_N\) is never a quasi-isomorphism. The module \(F_N=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_N]^{S_N}\), with \(y_i=-\hbar\partial_{x_i}\), has no flat first-order lift as the central value varies from \(N\), and its resulting class in \(\operatorname{Ext}^2_{U_N}(F_N,F_N)\) is nonzero. For every \(N\ge1\), the kernel of \(U_N\twoheadrightarrow A_N\) is generated by one Newton relation \(e_{N+1}\) and is idempotent. Hence \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_1(A_N,A_N)=0\), while \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\ne0\) has a split flux-cap surjection onto \(A_N\). The first positive sewing Tor degree is therefore two at every rank.
statements.antecedents: Gaiotto–Oh (2019); Etingof (2014); Joseph (1970); Lowen (2004); Pinczon–Ushirobira (2005); Costello (2017).

statements.title: Higher transport and the five-dimensional theory
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb Q[h]\), extend the polynomial Moyal-to-two-matrix transport to every arity at the remaining ranks \(N\ge5\), without inverting \(h\), and determine the permitted changes of lower Taylor maps. The integral full-complex model beyond matrix size three is a separate category-level question. For independently quantized five-dimensional noncommutative Chern–Simons theory, construct supported bulk, line and surface observables and compare their products and junctions with the algebraic transport, retaining the loop parameter, Moyal parameter and rank normalization.

statements.title: The Harish–Chandra sewing bimodules
statements.text: For the same algebraic power-sum map at \(N\ge1\) and fixed \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\), every \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_j(A_N,A_N)\) is a direct sum of the Harish–Chandra summands \(D(\tau)=(\tau\otimes W_\hbar^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\), with possibly infinite multiplicities, and is projective as a left and as a right \(A_N\)-module. Projectivity over \(A_N^e\) is not asserted. After choosing a section of the flux cap, \[\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\cong A_N\oplus K_N^{\mathrm{flux}},\qquad K_N^{\mathrm{flux}}\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{U(W_\hbar^{\mathrm{Lie}})}_2(A_N,A_N).\] The kernel vanishes for \(N=1\). Its vanishing at higher rank, all higher multiplicities, multiplication, higher operations and formality remain open. Ordinary \(\operatorname{Hom}\) and \(\operatorname{Ext}^1\) comparison hold for every module at every rank.

statements.title: The particle cohomology category at nonzero Weyl parameter
statements.text: At Cherednik coupling \(c=0\) and fixed numerical \(\hbar\in\mathbb C^\times\), put \(B_N=((W_\hbar\otimes\Lambda\theta)^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\). Fullness of the symmetric idempotent in the Weyl–exterior crossed product identifies ordinary unbounded derived \(B_N\)-modules with the specified equivariant coderived comodules and contraderived contramodules over a curved conilpotent coalgebra. The small relative presentation has curvature \(\hbar\sum_i\xi_i\eta_i\), and its even generators \(u_i\) act locally nilpotently in the comodule interpretation. This is a cohomology-algebra theorem, not formality of the full BRST complex. The fullness argument fails at \(\hbar=0\), \(N\ge2\).

statements.title: Full invariant models and a nonzero fourth operation
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C(\hbar)\), the relative curved cobar based on \(D_N(1)\) models the full \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\)-invariant two-matrix complex at every rank, retaining its scalar odd factor. For \(N\ge3\), \(j_*[m_4]=-[\beta\smile\beta]\ne0\) has exact \(\hbar^2\) order and is detected in three-cycle sectors; the polynomial integral complex and every nonzero numerical fibre are nonformal. At \(N=3,4\), a transpose-equivariant minimal model has only \(m_2,m_4\); an \(m_6\) first has room at \(N=5\), without a nonvanishing assertion. Separately, for \(1\le N\le3\) an integral comparison over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\), without inversion or completion, has a curved discrete-module quotient modelling the ordinary unbounded category. Its derived zero fibre is formal; nonflat modules require derived specialization.

statements.title: The absolute rank-two source model
statements.text: In the absolute polynomial Weyl–Clifford BRST algebra for traceless rank-two matrices over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\), the three positive ghosts give the degree-three Chevalley class \(\chi=\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3\). Cohomology occurs in degrees \(-1,0,2,3\). On the Weyl coordinates \(s,t\), with \([s,t]=\hbar\), let \(\theta\) denote the exterior generator of degree minus one. The square–anticommutator operation on \(s\theta\) and \(\chi\) is the singleton \(\{\hbar^2s^2\}\). The two possible indeterminacy groups \(H^{-3}\) and \(H^1\) vanish. Under scalar extension to a commutative \(\mathbb C\)-algebra with \(\hbar\mapsto\lambda\), the contraction survives. If \(\lambda^2\ne0\) this class obstructs associative formality. At \(\lambda=0\) there is a strict formality zigzag. A nonzero square-zero parameter kills this detector and leaves the formality question open. The relative complex omits \(\chi\), so this secondary operation has no such pair of inputs there.

statements.title: Universal polynomial Hamiltonian transport through total degree 24
statements.text:
Give the polynomial Hamiltonians \(L_h=\mathbb Q[x,y,h]\) the divided Moyal bracket \((f\star_h g-g\star_h f)/h\), with \([x,y]_\star=h\). In the universal cyclic-trace complex over \(\mathbb Q[
u,h]\), trace of the identity is \(
u\) and trace of the antighost is zero. Start with the normalized homogeneous, \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-equivariant arity-five extension with the tree-adapted ternary map. Its higher components vanish on quadratic inputs. A closed change of the fifth component supported on five-tuples of total polynomial degrees 22 and 23 suffices to extend to every arity on inputs of total degree at most 24. The first four components stay fixed. Specialization at each positive integer rank also gives this range over \(\mathbb Q[h]\).

The sixth obstruction has ghost degree \(-4\). Its first possible nonzero class has total input degree 24 and takes values in the three-dimensional \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-module of highest weight two. On the Poisson Lie algebra of polynomials of degree at least three, the sixth homology in weight 12 contains no copy of that module. The cocycle therefore factors through the chain boundary. A rational equivariant splitting supplies the fifth-component correction on these inputs, and translation extends it to linear inputs. Obstructions of arity at least seven start in total degree at least 30. The construction inverts neither \(h\) nor \(
u\).
hypotheses: Use the effective universal two-matrix complex, divided commutators, and the specified lower components. Polynomial input degree is the sum of the degrees in \(x,y\). The full space of Taylor maps is a product over arities. Each individual value is polynomial.

The numerical obstruction detector has a smaller invariance domain. The lower maps and permitted changes must be quadratic-relative. If only classical single-trace normalization or \(r_{(4,0)}=0\) is fixed, a ternary change shifts the detector by \(-4147200z(x)z(y)\), where \(z(f)=\operatorname{Tr}((\operatorname{Sym}f)\psi)\) and \(\psi\) is the antighost.

statements.title: Universal arity five with a fixed ternary map
statements.text:
Fix the symmetrized trace \(J\), the prescribed binary component and the tree-adapted ternary component of the map from the divided Moyal Lie algebra to the effective two-matrix complex over \(\mathbb Q[
u,h]\). Under the hypotheses below these three components extend through arity five on every polynomial input. If \(E\) is the universal fifth obstruction and \(\delta_h\) the Chevalley–Eilenberg differential for the divided bracket, the finite resolution by ordered symbols yields a polynomial cochain \(\Xi\) with \(\delta_h\Xi=E\). A closed change of the fourth component then makes the fifth defect exact. The primitive is defined before specialization, including at \(
u=0\), without dividing by \(
u\) or \(h\).

Knowing only \(\delta_h\widehat\zeta=
u E\) gives the positive-rank specialization. Here \(\widehat\zeta-
u\Xi\) is closed, so the connecting class of this particular cocycle vanishes. Universal arity six on inputs of arbitrary degree remains open.
hypotheses: Use the universal Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt homology model with its cycle lifts, the stable comparison at sufficiently large positive ranks, and the ordered-symbol projection for the effective universal target.

Use the all-weight third homology calculation for the Poisson Lie algebra of polynomials in \(x,y\) of degree at least three. Fix the three lower Taylor maps above, use the arity-completed full Hom with divided convolution bracket, and take polynomial values at each tuple.

rows.name: M5 branes, Miura algebras and surface fusion
rows.summary: The universal Miura image has coassociative rank addition and a derivative term sensitive to the order of the surfaces. For separated sources a native tree calculation fixes the sign of the connected linear line–surface term. With the fixed elementary right-action Ward normalization the order-odd two-surface reading agrees with the Miura stress tensor, \(+a/2\) on the marked second-colour state at unit level. The same test gives \(-a/2\) for the second elementary Weyl coefficient. Coincident contact terms, magnetic calibration and a common quantum comparison of surface, line and junction operations remain open.

object.note: Universal Miura image over \(\mathbb C[a,k]\); surface recognition open

dual.note: No completed dual of the Miura surface algebra

modules.note: No smooth-module equivalence for a surface-algebra dual

fusion.note: Algebraic Miura rank addition; physical surface fusion open

bulk.note: No vacuum-endomorphism algebra for the Miura surface object

lines.note: Connected separated tree exchange \(+\hbar eJ_c(x)/(4\pi^2 y)\) in the fixed positive-action conventions. The coincident quantum junction remains open.

states.note: Serre duality and relative cyclic traces on the Hopf-link thick subcategory; physical sewing open

dictionary.note: Reflection implication under existence and uniqueness of defect quantization

statements.title: Miura composition as a Moyal product
statements.text: For positive integers \(N_1,N_2\), take independent Heisenberg currents with \(J_i(z)J_j(w)\sim k\delta_{ij}/(z-w)^2\) over \(\mathbb C[a,k]\), and form the universal Miura images of \(\prod_{i=1}^N(a\partial+J_i)\). If \(\widehat U\) is the Weyl symbol obtained from the normally ordered symbol by \(\exp(-\tfrac a2\partial_z\partial_p)\), the coproduct is \[\widehat U^{(12)}=\widehat U^{(1)}\exp\!\left[\frac a2\left(\overleftarrow\partial_p\overrightarrow\partial_z-\overleftarrow\partial_z\overrightarrow\partial_p\right)\right]\widehat U^{(2)}.\] This is a coassociative, vacuum-preserving vertex-algebra map from rank \(N_1+N_2\) to the tensor product of the two Miura images. After inverting \(k\), its stress tensor has central charge \(c(N)=N-N(N^2-1)a^2/k\).

statements.title: Reflection and the first surface correction
statements.text: Consider one-flavour noncommutative Chern–Simons theory on \(\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb C^2\), with \([z_1,z_2]_* =c_{\mathrm M}\), surface \(t=z_2=0\), fixed classical surface currents, current level and universal or finite-rank boundary condition for the surface algebra, and logarithmic flux odd in the loop parameter \(\hbar\). Assume a perturbative defect quantization exists with coincident-point counterterms compatible with \(t\mapsto-t\), and that its Ward equations are reflection covariant with solutions unique modulo changes that are the identity on the classical currents. Then the first-order surface deformation class vanishes. If the currents and source coupling themselves admit a reflection-equivariant choice, their first-order coefficients vanish in that choice.

statements.title: One comparison for surfaces and junctions
statements.text: For an independently renormalized five-dimensional noncommutative Chern–Simons theory with M5 surface defects, construct the surface coefficient complexes and compare physical surface fusion with the rank-adding Miura coproduct. Construct, on the same domains, the line-fusion and mixed line–surface junction maps and compare them with the shifted affine Yangian operations, retaining their distinct parameters and units.

statements.title: Algebraic Miura reflection and the derivative term
statements.text: For the universal Miura images over \(\mathbb C[a,k]\), use the fixed PBW basis of normally ordered differential monomials in the Weyl fields \(\widehat U_r\). Transposition, reversal of the independent Heisenberg factors and PBW independence show that the scalar structure constants at every pole of \(\widehat U_i(z)\widehat U_j(w)\) lie in \(\mathbb C[a^2,k]\). The rank-addition coproduct has derivative contribution \[\frac a2\bigl(N_1\,1\otimes\partial\widehat U_1-N_2\,\partial\widehat U_1\otimes1\bigr)\] in \(\Delta\widehat U_2\). These formulas concern universal Miura images, without an assertion for arbitrary exceptional simple quotients. They do not require a physical defect interpretation.

statements.title: The conditional physical normalization
statements.text: In the positive-action Gaussian for disjoint marked line and surface sources, the inverse-Hessian pairing is \(-eJ_c(x)/(4\pi^2y)\). The connected mixed expectation has coefficient \(+\hbar eJ_c(x)/(4\pi^2 y)\). With the elementary right-action Ward marking and its magnetic coefficient, \(q=K\hbar/(4\pi^2c_{\mathrm M})\) and \(a_{\rm tree}=\hbar/(4\pi^2)\). The one-current excitation in the second of two unit stacks gives \(+\hbar/(8\pi^2)\) times the vacuum. Matching an independently supplied magnetic convention, the coincident contact terms and a quantum junction still requires a map that transports the marked sources.

rows.name: Three-dimensional gravity and Liouville theory
rows.summary: Finite original-coefficient Riesz action integrals, their full formal HPL line/covariance comparison and an infinite normalized numerical original-cycle Gaussian are available under supplied Ward-filling hypotheses. Finite uncut analytic sewing gives a nonzero output in the specified rooted vacuum channel for each fixed word of at least three positive inputs. The complete dense common input functor recovers the elementary source topologies. Exact source contacts and unary normalization sharpen the native operation comparison. On its small reflected source family the coefficient-heat calculation gives a numerical finite part and a based local line. Numerical exhaustion by the original sharp cutoffs, the unnormalized physical cap and the full identification with Einstein-gravity states and operations remain open.

statements.title: Positive sewing is rigid from a local crossing domain
statements.text: Fix real \(c>1\), \(Q=\sqrt{(c-1)/6}\), principal weights \(h(P)=Q^2/4+P^2\) with \(P>0\), and normalized Virasoro sphere blocks \(F_p^s(x)\), \(F_p^t(x)\). Write \(C_0\) for the Barnes-normalized trinion coefficient and \(\rho_0\) for the principal spectral density. Use the [normalized unitary fusion transform](#ch10-definition-normalized-boundary-hypothesis). With \(C_s=C_0(P_1,P_2,p)C_0(p,P_3,P_4)\) and \(C_t=C_0(P_2,P_3,p)C_0(p,P_1,P_4)\), it carries \(2^{1/4}\sqrt{C_t}F_p^t\) to \(2^{1/4}\sqrt{C_s}F_p^s\) in \(L^2(d\nu)\), \(d\nu=\rho_0(p)\,dp/\sqrt2\). Thus the squared marked \(s\)-block has density \(\rho_0 C_s|F_p^s|^2\,dp\). At zero bulk cosmological constant the boundary three-point formula with one vanishing boundary cosmological constant supplies the positive-label input above 25. The [fusion theorem and its continuation](#ref-ch10-02) give the marked unitary for \(c>25\), at \(25\), and by descent for \(1<c<25\). Let \(C:(0,\infty)^3\to(0,\infty)\) be finite, measurable and fully symmetric, and let \(B:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\) be finite measurable; suppose that for almost every external quadruple the two channel integrals, including \[G_s(x)=\int_0^\infty\frac{C(P_1,P_2,p)C(p,P_3,P_4)}{B(p)}\lvert F_p^s(x)\rvert^2\,dp,\] are locally bounded and equal throughout \(\lvert x\rvert<1,\ \lvert1-x\rvert<1\). Then, almost everywhere, \(B=a^2/\rho_0\) and \(C=K\,a(P_1)a(P_2)a(P_3)C_0\), where \(K>0\), \(a=\sqrt{B\rho_0}\), \(C_0\) is the Barnes-normalized three-point coefficient, and \(\rho_0(P)=4\sqrt2\sinh(2\pi bP)\sinh(2\pi P/b)\). Choose \(b+b^{-1}=Q\), with \(0<b\le1\) for \(c\ge25\) and \(b=e^{i\theta}\), \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), for \(1<c<25\). Local boundedness on the lens gives a common form core for the two channel integrals. Fusion intertwines the spectral projections of their density multipliers. Its kernel is nonzero almost everywhere, so the remaining multiplier is constant in the intermediate momentum.

statements.title: Boundary traces and the vacuum weight
statements.text: Fix real \(c>1\) and assume two positive principal Virasoro actions of weights \(h(P)=(c-1)/24+P^2\) are realized on \(L^2(\mathbb R_+,dP;\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal F))\), where \(\mathcal F\) is the oscillator Fock Hilbert space and the actions are \(L_n\xi=\pi_P(L_n)\xi\), \(\bar L_n\xi=\xi\pi_P(L_{-n})\), with their common finite-energy domain and trace-compatible positive sewing. Their faithful all-temperature state data are parametrized by measurable \(w>0\) almost everywhere with \(\int_0^\infty w(P)e^{-\beta P^2}\,dP<\infty\) for every \(\beta>0\), and have caps \(\Psi^w_\beta(P)=\sqrt{w(P)}e^{-\beta H_P/2}\), where \(H_P=P^2+N-1/24\) and \(N\) is the oscillator number operator on \(\mathcal F\). The Ward identities leave \(w\) free, while equality of the amplitude with the normalized modular vacuum amplitude at every temperature selects \(w=\rho_0\) almost everywhere. Here \(\rho_0(P)=2\sqrt2[\cosh(2\pi QP)-\cosh(2\pi\widehat QP)]\), \(Q=\sqrt{(c-1)/6}\), \(\widehat Q^2=Q^2-4\).

statements.title: Preparing a gravitational state from the bulk
statements.text: Construct regulated half-solid-torus integrals for real three-dimensional Einstein gravity in a fixed asymptotically anti-de Sitter solid-torus sector, with an invertible real coframe, Brown–Henneaux boundary conditions and a fixed boundary map, whose mixed pairings converge as both regulators are removed independently. Prove that the resulting vectors satisfy the Virasoro Ward identities, temperature evolution and physical sewing, have the normalized modular vacuum amplitude, and use the same stress charge as the local bulk action. This requires an independently defined gravitational integral and its comparison with the boundary representation.

statements.title: Finite normal words and independent-height primitive limits
statements.text:
Ordinary and first-normal boundary insertions cover every fixed finite word in the universal \(e,h,f,b,c\) source through bare orders zero and one, with its actual source differential. Independent-height ordinary and first-normal one-vertex \(u,h\) primitives have boundary and fixed-positive-height interior extensions, with their exact spatial contacts. Selected same-root second-normal rows retain their grouped Ward and reference-scale heat limits. The coincident finite PBW conversion has zero fixed normal projection with its full Hom companion retained.

Scope: Fix every source, field, component, jet and derivative stage; no estimate is uniform as those stages grow. Boundary finite words use one height derivative before zero-height restriction, compact simultaneous tangential ratios, compact positive running scales and the separately specified source normal-contact extensions. The independent-height theorem covers the one-vertex \(u,h\) matrix and its ordered \(h,s\) spectators in \(a\le a_0<\min(1,\sqrt{L_0}/16)\), with upper heat time \(L\in[L_0,L_1]\subset(0,\infty)\). Here \(r_\pm\ge0\) are root heights, \(d\) is tangential separation and \(a^2=(r_++r_-)^2+2|d|^2\). Its boundary estimate has no restriction on height, separation or cutoff ratios. Only the separated zero-lower-source representation requires \(0<\sqrt\epsilon\le b/8\), with \(b^2=(r_+-r_-)^2+2|d|^2\). The interior constant may depend on the positive mean height. The second-normal theorem retains its selected zero-jet, field-number-three rows; higher incoming normal tree and unary constructions have their own finite-moment normalization.
hypotheses: Fix every source, field, component, jet and derivative stage; no estimate is uniform as those stages grow.
