Their differentials use zero central contractions. Multiplication by \(\prod_{i<j}(t_i-t_j)\) identifies the exterior complex with the symmetric one. Taking the differential-module dual on each finite perfect stage gives the [supported pro-duality](#ch13-supported-duality-and-the-direction-of-comparison) \(V_n^\sharp:(\mathcal C^+_{I,n})^\sharp\simeq(\mathcal C^-_{I,n})^\sharp\). If \(\mathcal C^{>0}\) is the occupied subcomplex and \(\mathcal Q\) its vacuum quotient, the dual triangle starts \(\mathcal Q^\sharp\to\mathcal C^\sharp\to(\mathcal C^{>0})^\sharp\). The transpose of a cut includes the Vandermonde factors across the cut. Their product for three groups is independent of the order of the two cuts. The comparison retains finite normal derivatives, composite states, both vacuum maps and the nonsplit spectator attachment. Each finite output uses a finite stage over \(\mathbb C[\kappa]\), and the comparison commutes with numerical specialization at that stage. The [forward field comparison](#s-geometric-marked-field-comparison) remains open for the prescribed state readout, both vacua, marked curvature and original collision maps.

statements.title: The additive weighted coend decides its fixed-carrier target
statements.text: The contact-aware additive derived-coend formula, with every incoming simplex and the split positive vacuum retained, has countably infinite-dimensional scalar cohomology in every integer degree on both \(\mathbb A^1\) and \(\mathbb G_m\). On the unchanged affine-line carrier, a nonempty degree-zero class is independent of the empty unit, so that carrier cannot have the prescribed \(H_0=k\), regardless of a later multiplication. The result supplies no field-valued product and does not exclude a changed carrier. The enhanced geometric and operation-valued comparisons remain additional constructions.

statements.title: Strict exterior torsors transport the uncurving mark
statements.text: For finite-rank exterior torsors and algebraic possibly unbounded dg modules with direct-sum totalization, strict cotensor by \(L_a=(\Lambda(\eta),d\eta=a)\) transports the prescribed uncurving marks monoidally, with actual composition, unit and inverse torsors. At nonzero shift the underlying complex is acyclic; ordinary-derived tensor therefore destroys this marked statement. The theorem is for these strict finite exterior torsors and does not identify a common groupoid of all programme basepoints.

statements.title: A geometric realization of the rational-exchange integral
statements.text: Construct a natural map from the original-base all-surjection algebraic integral to an independently defined Ran or proper-support de Rham integral on the proposed global geometry. It must identify the full diagram, the two units, normal derivatives, supported collisions and shuffle products, and specify any completion needed to take a limit. The algebraic identification of its degree-zero cohomology with intrinsic modes is already available.

open.heading: Fusion and higher operations
open.intro: Finite representation categories and calculations on charge tops provide inputs to comparisons on complete modules.

statements.title: Nonabelian affine line fusion
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional nonabelian Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field with invariant level form \(\kappa\) and invertible \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\), compare the moving affine centralizer, the restricted bar construction in the transverse line direction and line fusion on modules induced from finite-dimensional charge tops. The comparison must specify weight and length completions and preserve all induced states, nonlinear translation homotopies, products and three-module coherence. Extend the secondary operations on affine cochains to configuration-indexed operations with coherent boundary action.

statements.title: A nonlinear module duality
statements.text: For the universal regular \(W_3\) algebra over discrete \(\mathbb C\) at any central charge, construct a polarized curved-bar equivalence with the smooth derived category, or construct such an equivalence using a different null class on the full contramodule category. With the full contramodule category and the smooth right adjoint \(F_c\) fixed, the new null class must contain the graded-free object \(Q\) for which \(F_cQ\) is contractible and the counit cone survives the product-generated exact-triple quotient. Compare this equivalence with quantum Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction; the algebraic bar construction and smooth-module resolutions alone do not give the localized equivalence.

statements.title: Continuous Virasoro fusion on completed inputs
statements.text: For real \(c>1\), construct an intrinsic admissible source assignment for arbitrary objects of the common continuous Ward recipient, and prove the corresponding represented fusion category with compatible repeated collisions and inverse domains. Fixed positive point-module inputs already have a representing recipient; full five-point interior sewing, entangled mixed Ward identities and coefficient-one vacuum units hold on their declared stages under \(H\) and the retained analytic hypotheses. The actual outer primary sewing does not extend to the whole common recipient, so its finer cluster-quotient source must be retained in the categorical construction. Preserve the separate geometric tree theorem at fixed \(c>25\).

statements.title: Hall products, coproducts and spectral exchange
statements.text: For a quiver moduli problem over \(\mathbb C\) and an oriented equivariant cohomology theory with an explicit coefficient ring, compare the extension-correspondence product with a shuffle product on one coefficient lattice. Define the localized direct-sum coproduct and chamber-dependent stable-envelope maps on that same lattice, with all denominators, completions and geometric-to-spectral parameter maps explicit, and prove their compatibility. A field realization must also extend these operations across their collision loci.

statements.title: The whole ordinary unit at raw rank-one level minus three
statements.text: Decide whether the actual affine unit is invertible on every ordinary unbounded \(Y_1(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\)-complex. The specific Verma telescope killed by zero-mode base change, all inflated ghost-quotient complexes and the stated lower-cochain-bounded representatives already have invertible unit. An obstruction has to survive in the cone of the actual map on a different source. A sufficient positive route would give a finite nullhomotopy of multiplication from the fibre of the ghost quotient as a map of bimodules.

open.heading: Independent bulk theories and line defects
open.intro: The bulk comparison must use observables and defects constructed from the bulk theory itself.

statements.title: Derived extensions of the ordinary charged-ray comparison
statements.text: The supported Cauchy-regulated ordinary ray intertwiners include every finite descendant, their graph winding and the corresponding oriented Fock braiding. The original inverse graph-transport convention has its marked sign discrepancy. Extend the ordinary comparison to derived defects and nonsplit marked vacuum extensions. Identify the mixed operations on that category with the corresponding derived vacuum endomorphisms. For a physical cap fix the outgoing charge, external source, absolute normalization and a topology in which its removal and sewing converge.

statements.title: A nonabelian bulk–boundary–line theorem
statements.text: For perturbative holomorphic-boundary \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) Chern–Simons theory on \(\mathbb C\times\mathbb R_{\geq0}\), normalize \((e,f)=1\), \((h,h)=2\), take \(\kappa_0\ne0\) and coefficients \(\mathbb C((\hbar))\), with boundary affine level \(\kappa_0/\hbar-2\). Construct supported maps from independently quantized bulk observables to derived endomorphisms of the boundary vacuum and from finite-dimensional Wilson representations to boundary modules. Prove that the same maps preserve normalized secondary operations, endpoint couplings, line fusion and their higher coherences on common coefficient and completion domains.

statements.title: Higher-dimensional punctures and quantum obstructions
statements.text: For a cyclic local field theory over \(\mathbb C\) with a defect, construct a map from its complex of local deformations to the defect deformation complex that carries the quantum obstruction to the corresponding defect obstruction. In the algebraic punctured-affine models in complex dimensions two and three, retain \(R\Gamma(\mathbb A^d_{\mathbb C}\setminus\{0\},\mathcal O)\) as a dg algebra, or transfer every higher product together with an explicit \(A_\infty\) quasi-isomorphism. Compare the normalized local operations and supports before identifying an anomaly or a spectral coproduct.

open.heading: States and gravitational sewing
open.intro: An algebra of observables and a fusion category leave the preparation of a state undetermined.

statements.title: A state prepared by an independent gravitational bulk
statements.text: For perturbative three-dimensional Einstein gravity with negative cosmological constant, in a fixed topological sector with invertible coframe, construct an independently renormalized bulk amplitude on a region with a cut. Identify its state space and observable action with the boundary construction, prove compatibility with fillings and sewing on common analytic domains, and derive the normalization of the cut measure from the bulk. The comparison must retain the boundary conditions and finite counterterm prescription rather than infer a state or a universal charge shift from Virasoro symmetry alone.

glossary.definition: On the word \(123\), the nonempty binary cuts are \(1|23\) and \(12|3\). For each consecutive cut of a coherent word coefficient system, take the derived external product of its block coefficients. Restrict it to the locus where different blocks are disjoint, then take the open direct image to the full configuration space and sum over the cuts. Monotone collisions identify the coefficients by coherent extraordinary pullback. The convolution is nonsymmetric, with unit \(k\) on the empty configuration and zero elsewhere. [Support at a collision of the first and third labels](#ch05-the-support-remembers-which-cuts-were-allowed).

Cut the ordered word \(123\) after its first label. Wherever point \(1\) is separated from both \(2\) and \(3\), the coproduct of a strong cut coalgebra identifies the three-point coefficient with the external product of the \(1\) and \(23\) coefficients. The definition requires this equivalence on the separated locus of every consecutive cut and coherent coassociativity for successive cuts. [Connected duality for consecutive cuts](#ch05-ordered-cuts-give-a-finite-geometric-bar-construction).

For consecutive-cut convolution, the unit is \(k\) at the empty configuration and zero at every occupied configuration. A local field vacuum is identity-field data at occupied positions, including its insertion and principal-part identities. There is also a product at the same positions. On coalgebras its tensor unit is the dualizing coefficient system \(J\). Transporting this tensor through bar and cobar gives \(A\diamond A'=\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}(B_{\mathrm{cut}}A\otimes^!B_{\mathrm{cut}}A')\) with unit \(\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}J\). A scalar vertex character or an occupied vacuum requires its own marking.

There are two specified coefficient categories. Word systems are complexes on \(X^n\) with coherent extraordinary-pullback identifications along monotone surjections and consecutive-cut convolution. Full ordered collision systems live on the schemes formed by gluing total-order charts; their collision maps use surjections with ordered fibres, and their symmetric convolution sums over all ordered decompositions into subsets. Restriction to an increasing chart and projection onto consecutive summands transport coalgebras from the second category to the first; the comparison is generally not strong monoidal.

Fix the positive-mode Lie subalgebra of a local mode algebra. The semiderived smooth category is the homotopy category of smooth complexes modulo those whose restriction to that subalgebra is coacyclic. Here coacyclic complexes form the smallest triangulated subcategory containing totalizations of short exact triples and closed under coproducts and retracts.

A module-like object over a complete curved algebra, equipped with coherent summation operations for coefficient families tending to zero. Its degree-one connection squares to the action of the curvature; a topology on the contramodule itself is additional data.

For a curved ghost contramodule, remove the negative ghost coefficients by the contramodule quotient, including all their summation relations; the result is a dg module over the positive-mode cochain algebra. It is Becker-coacyclic when its Hom complex into every dg module with graded-injective underlying module is acyclic.

For an augmented differential graded algebra \(H\), the augmentation makes the ground field \(k\) an \(H\)-module. From \(k\), shifts, finite cones and retracts generate \(\operatorname{thick}(k)\) in \(D(H)\). Also allowing arbitrary coproducts gives \(\operatorname{Loc}(k)\). To extend a comparison proved on \(k\) to the latter category, one must control those coproducts. [The translated spectral bar comparison](#s-the-spectral-bar-comparison-on-augmentation-generated-catego).

The \(\hbar\)-adically complete sheaf of vertex superalgebras on \(\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\) constructed by local framed \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) BRST reduction of adjoint and fundamental symplectic bosons with fundamental fermions. Its quotient modulo \(\hbar\) is the jet sheaf of the corresponding reduced supermanifold. Formal sheaf cohomology, finite \(\hbar\)-quotients and torus-finite numerical specialization are distinct constructions.

The operation on sheaf cohomology obtained by combining the Čech cup operation with the vertex-algebra \((-1)\)-product on local sections. Associativity must be proved on the relevant subspace; the determinant-torsion theorem establishes it on the displayed subalgebra.

For the formal Hilbert-scheme vertex sheaf \(\mathcal D\), these are \(\kappa_r=T^r\beta(\phi\psi)\), where \(\beta\) is the connecting map for multiplication by \(\hbar\) and \(\phi\psi\) is the classical contraction of the two fundamental fermions. The first class has a logarithmic cocycle representing the first Hodge Chern class of the tautological determinant line. Their generated positive-degree subalgebra is killed by \(\hbar\); its exterior signs come from sheaf degree, while the intrinsic parity is even.

The subspace of elements whose torus orbit spans a finite-dimensional representation. For the formal vertex sheaf, this subspace is taken before numerical specialization of the formal parameter; reversing these operations can change the result.

A Ward map satisfies the current or stress-tensor Ward identities at its inputs and output; the rational construction includes an output insertion at infinity with restricted contragredience. A represented Ward product is a module with a universal insertion map, so that morphisms to an allowed output module are naturally the corresponding Ward maps. Its representing object is the Ward output; scalar conformal-block identities or a pentagon on spectral labels alone do not supply this universal property.

The subspace of vectors whose rotations around the boundary point span a finite-dimensional space. In the boundary and endpoint complexes this selects the algebraic sum of rotation-weight components, rather than an unrestricted product over energies.

The observable complex with an additional differential supported on a prescribed line; in the abelian model this term is \(-i\alpha I_L\). It specifies the line source on compact tests without asserting that a globally regulated exponential insertion has the same limit.

A marked vacuum extension is a short exact sequence \(0\to\mathbf1\xrightarrow{i}J\xrightarrow{p}\mathbf1\to0\) with its actual injection, projection and a common identification of the unit. Marked charge extensions similarly retain their end modules and maps. Preserving the marking requires intertwining both maps; an unmarked isomorphism of the middle objects is weaker.

At \(c=-22/5\) the usual spin-three bracket has a coefficient proportional to \(1/(22+5c)\). The regular universal \(W_3\) algebra uses an even stress field \(T\) of weight two and an even field \(U\) of weight three. In its mode bracket \([U_m,U_n]\) the coefficient of \((m-n)\Lambda_{m+n}\) is one, with \(\Lambda=:TT:-3\partial^2T/10\). The linear and central terms use \(a_c=(22+5c)/16\). The Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt basis retains the state \(U_{-3}\mathbf1\) at the exceptional charge. [The regular commutator on the vacuum](#ch12-nonlinear-fields-the-w3-example).

A discrete module for a local mode algebra is smooth when every vector is annihilated by all sufficiently high positive modes. The cutoff may depend on the vector; a uniform cutoff, an energy grading and finite-dimensional weight spaces are additional hypotheses.

An ordinary module has diagonalizable \(L_0\), finite-dimensional weight spaces, and weights bounded below in finitely many integral cosets. A grading-restricted generalized module permits generalized \(L_0\)-eigenspaces under the same finiteness and lower-bound conditions.

A collision operation includes the map obtained when field insertions meet a distinguished module insertion, together with the vacuum insertion and all normal derivatives. Retaining all marked collisions asks for these maps at every finite number of points and their composition identities.

A curved differential graded algebra has a degree-one derivation \(d\) and a degree-two element \(h\) with \(d^2=[h,-]\) and \(dh=0\). For the universal mode algebras here, its continuous Koszul-dual cochains retain the central cocycle as \(h\); the completion and the module localization are part of the duality data.

A module supported at a finite set \(S\) has, for each vector, a power of \(P_S(t)=\prod_{s\in S}(t-s)\) whose multiples annihilate it through both current and ghost operations. The supported localization inverts exactly the maps sent to quasi-isomorphisms by smooth induction. This differs from inverting all quasi-isomorphisms of the underlying ghost complexes.

At nonzero Heisenberg level \(\kappa\), a polynomial Fock module with zero-mode coefficient space \(E\) is \(E[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), using finite polynomials. Creation modes multiply by \(x_m\), annihilation modes act by \(m\kappa\partial_{x_m}\), and the zero mode acts on \(E\).

At each fixed number of fields, observables are completed projective bornological tensor powers of compactly supported smooth forms, represented by compact smooth kernels in the corresponding number of variables. The direct sum over field number remains algebraic, so an observable has only finitely many field-number components.

A finite Weyl filtration is a finite filtration whose successive quotients are affine modules induced from finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g[[z]]\)-modules killed by a sufficiently high power of \(z\). Its exact structure comes from exact sequences of smooth affine modules.

For a module with generalized energy eigenspaces \(X_{[h]}\), the energy completion is \(\prod_hX_{[h]}\), replacing the direct sum over energies by a product. For a complex, completion term by term is a separate operation from totalization.

A fusion lattice near shifted level \(\kappa_0\) is the module over \(\mathbb C[[\varepsilon]]\), with finite free generalized-energy blocks, obtained by deforming fusion to \(\kappa_0+\varepsilon\) and embedding it into the generic fibre over \(\mathbb C((\varepsilon))\). Associators and braidings preserve this lattice and specialize by reduction; it need not be the lattice supplied by a generic Weyl basis.

Let \(G\) be the simply connected compact group of the given simple Lie type. In ambient universal-affine fusion at positive integral level, each Verlinde multiplicity space for finite sums of simple integrable modules at distinct points is tensored with \(H_b(\Omega G;\mathbb C)\) in homological degree \(b\). Passing to fusion in the simple vertex algebra applies the augmentation to this factor and retains loop degree zero. Multiplication on the full derived fusion object remains open.

If the simples of a finite semisimple tensor category are \(L_i\) for \(i\in I\), let the \((i,j)\) part of the fibre of \(M\) be \(\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,M\otimes L_j)\). The long bimodule fibre is the direct sum of these spaces over both indices. The idempotents of \(\mathbb C^I\) select the end labels. In a tensor product over \(\mathbb C^I\), a factor ending at \(j\) composes only with a factor beginning at \(j\). [Fusion with a finite-base fibre](#s-minimal-model-fusion-with-a-finite-base-fibre).

A null vector in the intermediate Virasoro module represents zero in its simple quotient, as do all its descendants. A three-point form factors through this quotient precisely when it vanishes on the entire contravariant radical. To contract two forms through the simple module this condition is needed on both sides.

For a Gram matrix over \(\mathbb C[[\varepsilon]]\) that is invertible over \(\mathbb C((\varepsilon))\), the Smith exponents are the powers of \(\varepsilon\) in its diagonal invariant factors. Positive exponents describe the orders at which null directions appear; all positive exponents equal to one means the derivative pairing on the radical is nondegenerate.

A source treated through its formal Taylor coefficients, which are multilinear functionals of smooth compactly supported test inputs. A finite-parameter source family is a power series with zero constant term in those parameters. Convergence after assigning numerical parameter values is a separate assertion.

For an \(E_3\)-algebra, the fundamental class of the two-point configuration sphere defines a binary operation of cohomological degree \(-2\), called the Browder bracket. Its sign depends on the chosen orientation of that sphere.

The scalar distribution identity \(\partial_{\bar z}(1/z)=\pi\delta_0\), in the convention \(d^2z=dx\,dy\), illustrates a term supported only where two points coincide. Such distributional contributions are called contact terms. In the formal source identities the Cauchy Green operator and the cutoff prescription fix their extension to the diagonal. The values of a kernel at separated points alone leave that extension undetermined.

For real \(c>1\), a positive principal label \(P>0\) specifies the highest weight \(h(P)=(c-1)/24+P^2\). The associated positive highest-weight representations form the continuous family used in momentum integration and Hilbert completion; the vacuum is a separate representation.

A module for a vertex algebra whose fields satisfy vectorwise lower truncation and the vertex-module identities, with no prescribed conformal grading, positive-energy bound or finite-dimensionality. For the finitely generated current presentations used here, sufficiently high modes kill each individual vector.

For formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\), the completion has the form \(M=\bigoplus_w\prod_{j\ge0}\hbar^jM_0[w+j]\). Boundedness below and finite type mean respectively that \(M_0[w]=0\) below a lower bound and that each \(M_0[w]\) is finite-dimensional; neither permits an unrestricted product over all weights.

For a positive finite-type RTT lattice \(M\), the cochains are \(\mathcal K(M)=M\widehat\otimes B\), with differential \(d_B+\tau_M\), where \(B\) is the RTT ghost algebra and \(\tau_M\) is the universal twisting cochain evaluated on the Yangian action. The tensor and mode sums use weightwise and \(\hbar\)-adic completion, and sufficiently high mode evaluations lie in \(\hbar^NM\) for every fixed \(N\). Arbitrary-value full linear duals need not satisfy this restriction.

The matrix-current presentation uses \(R(x)=1-\hbar P/x\), where \(P\) interchanges the two vector factors, and \(\bar R(x)=g(x)R(x)\), with \(g(x+n\hbar)=g(x)(1-\hbar^2/x^2)\) and \(g(x)=1+\hbar/(nx)+\cdots\). The mixed relation uses \(\bar R\) with shifts \(\pm K\hbar/2\).

For a scalar kernel \(\gamma\), draw a directed edge \(i\to j\) at a configuration when \(\gamma(Z_j,Z_i)=0\). The wheel locus is the locus of configurations with a directed cycle, or its image in the symmetric configuration space; it can lie away from ordinary collision diagonals.

forms: shuffle subalgebra generated in weight one
glossary.definition: The big shuffle algebra contains the full polynomial or Laurent-polynomial coefficient space in every weight, with its prescribed permutation character and shuffle product. The smaller algebra is the subalgebra generated by weight-one coefficients; wheel conditions can make this inclusion proper.

The extension of a Hall or shuffle algebra by commuting moment operators \(p_r\). In the one-loop example, \([p_r,b_s]=b_{r+s}\), and dressing the coproduct by the corresponding Cartan series makes separation of sites compatible with these actions.

On the basis indexed by subsets of finite sites \(t_i\), let \(n_i\) measure occupation and let \(c_i\) create an unoccupied site and kill an occupied one. The currents are \(E(u)=\sum_i\frac{c_i}{u-t_i}\prod_{j\ne i}(1+\eta/(t_i-t_j))^{n_j}\) and \(P(u)=\sum_i n_i/(u-t_i)\), expanded at infinity.

The additive pair of polynomial degrees in the two transverse twistor coordinates. In the finite quantum gauge quotient, \(J[\alpha]\) and \(E[\alpha]\) have degree \(\alpha\), while \(\widetilde J[\alpha]\) and \(F[\alpha]\) have degree \(\alpha+(1,1)\); vertex translation leaves this pair unchanged.

A degree-one coupling \(I\) obeys its Maurer–Cartan equation after quotienting states by the image of total translation: \(QI+\tfrac12I_{(0)}I=D_{\mathrm{tot}}H\). Since a total derivative has zero zero-mode, this identity can produce a square-zero operator on coefficient modules.

For a chosen splitting of loop modes into nonnegative and negative powers, the co-vacuum is the module induced from the trivial representation of the negative-mode subalgebra. The usual vacuum is induced from the nonnegative modes; their derived invariants and coinvariants can behave differently.

All linear maps from finite exterior powers of the Lie algebra into the coefficient module, without a support or continuity restriction. For unbounded derived Hom, product totalization retains every component contributing to a fixed total degree.

At every finite power of the formal parameter, the exchange has rational coefficients with finitely bounded pole orders on each input. The bound may grow as the precision increases, so the complete output need not belong to an algebraic tensor product with one uniform pole bound.

The homological Chevalley–Eilenberg complex of current-valued rational functions with poles at the insertion points and vanishing at infinity, with coefficients in the tensor product of the inserted modules. Partial fractions separate the underlying vector spaces into local principal parts, while Taylor expansions at the other insertion points enter the mixed differential.

A class of complexes declared to become zero in a derived localization. For curved or topological duality, this class must be defined through the actual functors and topology; ordinary acyclicity need not give the required localization.

A coefficient bundle on an elliptic curve whose pullback to the universal cover has prescribed transformations under the two periods. Those transformations are part of the exchange-field data and must be compatible with its poles, translation and collision operations.

The splitting of Laurent current modes into the nonnegative modes that annihilate the vacuum and the negative creation modes. The associated ghost representation depends on this splitting and on the finiteness needed for its determinant cocycle.

In the celestial gauge algebra \(E[p]\) and \(F[p]\) are the two axion current families, with \(p\) a transverse polynomial. The axion coupling \(s\) is the formal parameter in their interaction with gauge currents. In the pure theory with one axion, if \(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\operatorname{ad}_a^4)=\gamma K(a,a)^2\), the one-loop coefficient in this marking is \(\nu=-3s^2/\gamma\). With \(K(a,b)=\operatorname{tr}(ab)\) in the defining representation this gives \(-s^2/3\) for \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) and \(-3s^2/8\) for \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\). [The marked axion and gauge currents in a residue](#ch19-cubic-ward-identity).

Natural comparison maps between tensor products that vary meromorphically with the spectral separation and satisfy coherence where the products are defined. The Drinfeld products here depend on that separation.

The graded-commutative algebra generated by odd variables dual to Lie-algebra generators and their derivatives, with the Chevalley–Eilenberg differential. Polynomial means finite support in those variables; it does not permit an unrestricted product over the generator labels.

The kernel of the zero-mode operator of an odd vertex field. In the Hilbert-scheme example the field is \(\chi^-=\phi\gamma\), and its zero mode annihilates exactly the image of the boundary BRST algebra.

The actual unital image of finite products of vertex-mode operators acting on the algebraic direct sum of the vacuum algebra's conformal-weight spaces. It has no completion in the mode indices; its curved bar does not by itself classify modules for a completed vertex algebra.

For the Moyal product with parameter \(h\), the bracket \(b_h(f,g)=(f*_hg-g*_hf)/h\) is polynomial in \(h\) on polynomial inputs, because the numerator is divisible by \(h\). At \(h=0\) it becomes the Poisson bracket.

The convolution bracket on multilinear maps whose target bracket is the graded commutator divided by \(h\). In the polynomial two-matrix setting that commutator is divisible by \(h\), so the operation is defined without inverting the parameter.

The invariant algebra \((W_h(\mathfrak{gl}_N\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_N^*)\otimes\Lambda\mathfrak{gl}_N)^{GL_N}/(\operatorname{Tr}\psi)\), with odd \(\psi\) of degree \(-1\). Its differential is the invariant restriction of \(h^{-1}[\Omega,-]\), where \(\Omega=c^a\mu_a-\tfrac12f_{ab}^{d}c^ac^b\psi_d\), \(\{c^a,\psi_b\}=h\delta^a_b\), \(\mu=YX-XY+hNI\), and \(f_{ab}^{d}\) are the structure constants of \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\).

The vertex subalgebra generated by the coefficients of the ordered differential operator \(\prod_{i=1}^N(a\partial+J_i)\) inside the universal rank-\(N\) Heisenberg algebra. It retains the universal parameter family; a simple quotient at a special parameter is a separate object.

A half-space propagator built from the heat kernels \(g_s(t-t')\mp g_s(t+t')\), using the minus sign for Dirichlet and plus sign for Neumann boundary conditions. One integrates over a heat-time interval \([\epsilon,L]\) and applies the gauge-fixing differential.

The four-point block obtained by contracting the two highest-vector-normalized three-point Ward forms with the inverse Virasoro Gram matrix at every descendant level. In the first channel it is normalized as \(F_p^s(x)=x^{h(p)-h_1-h_2}(1+O(x))\), with powers positive on \(0<x<1\); the second channel uses \(1-x\) and exchanges the first and third labels.

For \(Q=b+b^{-1}\), let \(\Gamma_b\) be the Barnes double-gamma function with periods \(b,b^{-1}\), normalized by \(\Gamma_b(Q/2)=1\). The coefficient is \(C_0(P_1,P_2,P_3)=\dfrac{\Gamma_b(2Q)}{\sqrt2\,\Gamma_b(Q)^3}\dfrac{\prod_{\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3=\pm1}\Gamma_b(Q/2+i\sum_j\epsilon_jP_j)}{\prod_{j=1}^3\Gamma_b(Q+2iP_j)\Gamma_b(Q-2iP_j)}\).

A vector or continuous functional assigned to a boundary component filled on one side. In the positive boundary trace model, a cap at inverse temperature \(\beta\) is \(\sqrt{w(P)}e^{-\beta H_P/2}\); pairing caps yields the corresponding sewn amplitude. On the unit harmonic disk, a nonzero cap amplitude \(v\) of finite norm gives the density \(|v|^2/\|v\|^2\) relative to the boundary measure. Replacing \(v\) by \(\lambda v\), with \(\lambda\ne0\), preserves this probability law and multiplies its Hermitian self-pairing by \(|\lambda|^2\). A phase leaves that self-pairing unchanged. Against a fixed reference cap, the complex pairing acquires \(\lambda\) when \(v\) is in the linear slot and \(\bar\lambda\) when it is in the conjugate-linear slot. An independent filling must supply its own vacuum amplitude in the identified vacuum line. [The sourced disk and collar pairing](#ch11-neutral-ray-pair).

At central charge \(c>1\), this is \(Z_{\mathrm{vac}}(4\pi^2/\beta)\), where \(Z_{\mathrm{vac}}(y)=e^{yc/24}\prod_{j\ge2}(1-e^{-jy})^{-1}\). It fixes both the vacuum character and its scalar normalization.

For the two commuting positive Virasoro actions, this is the union of the spectral subspaces on which \(L_0+\bar L_0\) is bounded above. Each mode acts on this common invariant domain before Hilbert completion.

The pentagon identity for integral kernels that change the internal representation labels in successive fusions. Its validity on label Hilbert spaces does not alone construct a tensor product representing the trivalent Ward maps.

The adjoint Chevalley–Eilenberg class represented by the cocycle \(\Omega_H\) built from derivatives of the Hamiltonian Hessians. Its nonvanishing prevents an algebraic two-cochain from cancelling that particular cubic residual.

The idempotent-complete triangulated subcategory of \(D_c^b(S^3;\mathbb C)\) generated by \(\mathbb C_{S^3}\) and \(i_{j*}\mathbb C_{K_j}[-1]\), where \(K_1,K_2\) are the two coordinate circles forming the positively oriented Hopf link and \(i_j:K_j\hookrightarrow S^3\). It consists of objects obtained from those generators by finite cones, shifts and direct summands.

The vector space of continuous linear functionals, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on bounded subsets of the original locally convex space. This topology retains convergence information that the algebraic dual does not specify.

For compactly supported complex \(g\in L^2(\mathbb R)\), set \(h(u)=\int g(y)\overline{g(y-u)}\,dy\) and \[Q(g)=\int_{\mathbb R}h(u)(e^{u/2}+e^{-u/2})\,du-\sum_{m\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(m)}{\sqrt m}\bigl(h(\log m)+h(-\log m)\bigr)-(\log(4\pi)+\gamma_E)h(0)-\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{u/2}}{2\sinh u}\bigl(h(u)+h(-u)-2e^{-u/2}h(0)\bigr)\,du,\] where \(\Lambda\) is the von Mangoldt function, \(\gamma_E\) is Euler’s constant and logarithms are natural. Its extended-real value may be \(+\infty\); its finite-energy domain consists of the inputs for which it is finite.

For a prime \(p\), a \(\delta\)-ring has a Frobenius lift \(\varphi(a)=a^p+p\delta(a)\); the iterates \(a,\delta a,\delta^2a,\ldots\) are arithmetic jet coordinates. In a \(p\)-torsion-free ring the Frobenius lift determines \(\delta\).

For a profinite set \(S\), the constant profinite formal scheme over \(\mathbb Z_p\) has coordinate algebra \(C(S,\mathbb Z_p)\) of continuous functions, with its \(p\)-adic topology. A label on a test algebra may vary across its idempotent components; it is not required to be one globally constant element of \(S\).

Over the integers, \(t^p/p!\) cannot be formed by dividing by \(p!\) at the prime \(p\). In a divided-power algebra \(\gamma_j(t)\) is a specified element. Multiplication obeys \(\gamma_a(t)\gamma_b(t)=\binom{a+b}{a}\gamma_{a+b}(t)\). The notation \(\Gamma_R(t_1,\ldots,t_m)\) denotes the free algebra with these divided powers. Where \(j!\) is invertible, \(\gamma_j(t)=t^j/j!\).

The arithmetic normal carrier retains independent displacements \(v\) and their iterated \(\delta\)-coordinates around each arithmetic point. Addition of displacements gives a coproduct \(\Delta\) on their coordinate algebra \(H_r\), and normal distributions multiply by \((\lambda*\mu)(f)=(\lambda\otimes\mu)\Delta(f)\). The finite-weight distributions are \(\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z_p}(H_{r,d}^{\mathrm{alg}},\mathbb Z_p)\), with \(\operatorname{wt}(t_i)=p^i\) and \(\operatorname{wt}(w_j)=p^{r-1+j}\).

For the moduli stack \(\mathcal P\) of perfect complexes on \(X\), the group \(K_0^{\mathrm{semi}}(X)=\pi_0(\mathcal P)\) indexes connected components under direct sum. Specifying a class in this group retains more information than specifying only a numerical Chern character.

A square root of the determinant line of self-extensions, together with compatible square-root isomorphisms for direct sums and exact triangles. The compatibility includes associativity over every actual ordered filtration; it is additional structure beyond an isolated square root.
The \(\mu_2\)-torsor of square-compatible isomorphisms between two orientation lines. Its class in \(H^1(-,\mu_2)\) measures whether those fixed square roots can be identified globally.

Vanishing-cycle coefficients for compact moduli of sheaves or perfect complexes after removing the elliptic translation direction. Their comparison requires compatible orientations and maps on actual extension correspondences, beyond the numerical reduced invariant.

The weight-ten genus-two Siegel cusp form \(\chi_{10}\) is normalized here by \[\chi_{10}(y,q,p)=pq(y+y^{-1}-2)\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{20}(1-yq^m)^2(1-y^{-1}q^m)^2+O(p^2).\] The inverse-Igusa series is its reciprocal Fourier expansion in the corresponding positive chamber.

A state or trace functional compatible with cyclic rotation of composable operations and with the proposed sewing maps. A scalar generating series alone does not specify such a functional or its preparation by a cap.

The finite-length, grading-restricted module categories obtained by local lifts through the simple-current boundary extensions in the abelian mirror construction of Ballin–Creutzig–Dimofte–Niu. In the two-flavour example the charge maps are 1 ↦ (1,1) and 1 ↦ (1,−1); the extension and tensor unit are retained, so these are smaller than all smooth current modules.

A stable envelope maps fixed-point equivariant cohomology into the cohomology of a symplectic resolution after choosing a chamber and polarization. Comparing the maps for two chambers gives an exchange operator on that equivariant coefficient space.

The proposed complex threefold maps properly and flatly to \(\mathbb P^1\), with smooth fibres complex two-tori, multiple fibres of multiplicities three and four at zero and one, and a reduced non-normal crossing fibre at infinity whose normalization is the degree-six del Pezzo surface. The uniformization, marked period lattice, finite quotient fillings, logarithmic transforms and toric cusp gluing are geometric hypotheses; the underlying smooth topology is a separate question.

Over \(\mathbb C\), put \(A_n=\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_n,u_1,\ldots,u_n]\otimes\Lambda(du_1,\ldots,du_n)/(\sum z_iu_i-1,\sum z_i du_i)\), with \(d(u_i)=du_i\), \(d(z_i)=d(du_i)=0\), and \(L_n=\mathfrak g\otimes A_n\). The regular subalgebra is \(P_n=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_n]\), and the negative subalgebra is \(N_n=\mathfrak g\otimes\operatorname{span}\{u^\alpha\omega_n:\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\}\), where \(\omega_n=\sum_i(-1)^{i-1}u_i\,du_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widehat{du_i}\wedge\cdots\wedge du_n\). The internal weights are \(\operatorname{wt}(z_i)=1\), \(\operatorname{wt}(u_i)=\operatorname{wt}(du_i)=-1\); \(du_i\) has cohomological degree one, and the model uses polynomial functions, algebraic symmetric algebras and ordinary quasi-isomorphisms.

The direct sum over internal weights of homogeneous Hom complexes, with each homogeneous Hom still retaining the products required over source components. Its restricted weight dual and the unrestricted full Hom need not have the same elements or multiplication. For an internally graded space \(V\), the restricted weight dual is \(V^\vee=\bigoplus_w(V_{-w})^*\).

The principal-parts module is \(T_n=(z_1\cdots z_n)^{-1}\mathbb C[z_1^{-1},\ldots,z_n^{-1}]\). Multiplication by a regular polynomial is followed by deleting every monomial with a nonnegative exponent in at least one variable; this defines the regular-mode action on the top local-cohomology summand.

For \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\), this is the completed algebra of odd degree-one generators \(c_{ij,s}\), \(s\ge1\), with weight \(s-1\), series \(c(y)=\sum_{s\ge1}c_sy^{s-1}\), differential \(dc(y)=-c(y)^2\) and translation \(Tc_s=sc_{s+1}\). Its relations are \[c_{ij}(y)c_{kl}(y')+c_{kl}(y')c_{ij}(y)=\frac{\hbar}{y-y'}\bigl(c_{kj}(y)-c_{kj}(y')\bigr)\bigl(c_{il}(y)-c_{il}(y')\bigr),\] with weightwise completion and formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\). The restriction on its cochains is decay of sufficiently high mode evaluations modulo every power of \(\hbar\).

For rank-\(n\) RTT series \(T^*(u)=1+\hbar\sum_{q\ge1}b_qu^{-q}\), with \(T^*_{jl,0}=\delta_{jl}\), the action on Koszul cochains is \(\rho_M(c_{ij,s})=\sum_{l=1}^{n}\sum_{q\ge0}T^*_{jl,q}\otimes c_{il,s+q}\). This combines the coefficient-module mode action with the ghost action and converges on the positive weightwise-complete lattices. It is a left \(B\)-action commuting with the ordinary right \(B\)-action.

A primitive for the Ward or master-equation term on the complement of the singular insertion or divisor. Sewing requires its extension and boundary values to agree across the cuts used to join regions.

Sewing in which all pieces and their common boundary use compatible regulators before any regulator is removed. The boundary identities and their higher compatibility maps must hold for that single regulated construction.

The finite-dimensional coefficient module from which an affine or Heisenberg module is induced. For a horizontal affine top, \(\mathfrak g\) acts and positive loop modes act trivially; generalized Weyl induction permits finite jets killed by a sufficiently high power of \(z\).

Operations combining bulk observables, boundary fields and the maps by which the bulk acts on the boundary, indexed by configurations in a space with boundary. Their coefficient objects retain holomorphic collision singularities, composition in the transverse real direction and coherence with vacuum insertions.

forms: restricted bar construction in the transverse line direction
glossary.definition: The bar construction for multiplication along the transverse real direction, formed as the derived relative tensor of two augmentation modules. With diagonal exceptional tensor and dualizing unit \(J\), it is \(J\otimes_F^!J\) for an augmented transverse algebra \(F\). A line-algebra dual then requires its own restricted or continuous dual and completion.

A compactly cut off lift \(v\) of a meromorphic vector-field germ \(u\) generates the formal source flow \(\partial_s\mu=\bar\partial v+v\mu^{\prime}-\mu v^{\prime}\). The Virasoro punctured-flow identity relates the source functional along successive such flows to ordered insertions \(e^{sT[u]}\) and their central anomaly factor. It determines the contact terms for overlapping cutoffs.

glossary.term: Strongly rational and holomorphic vertex operator algebras
glossary.definition: A strongly rational complex vertex operator algebra is simple, self-contragredient, rational, of CFT type \(V=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}V_n\) with \(V_0=\mathbb C\,1\), and \(C_2\)-cofinite: the quotient by the span of \(a_{(-2)}b\) is finite-dimensional. Rationality means complete reducibility of admissible modules. It is holomorphic when its only irreducible ordinary module is itself.

After choosing a Cartan subalgebra of \(V_1\), its currents generate a Heisenberg vertex algebra. The Heisenberg commutant consists of the states whose fields commute with these currents, equivalently those annihilated by their nonnegative modes.

For the holomorphic vertex operator algebras considered here, the Heisenberg charges occurring with the vacuum module of the commutant form a positive-definite even lattice \(L\). The corresponding lattice vertex algebra is the mutual commutant of the Heisenberg commutant.

A lattice genus consists of lattices isometric over \(\mathbb R\) and over \(\mathbb Z_p\) for every prime \(p\). For the strongly rational holomorphic class with strongly rational Heisenberg commutant considered here, a hyperbolic genus consists of the holomorphic extensions with that commutant, an associated lattice in the same lattice genus, and the compatible discriminant gluings. Isomorphism classes include the identification of Cartans up to conjugacy.

The mass is the sum of reciprocal orders of the specified finite symmetry groups over the isomorphism classes in the genus. For a lattice it uses the full orthogonal group; for the holomorphic vertex operator algebras here it uses the finite image of the Cartan-preserving automorphism group on the associated lattice, retaining the kernel of its action on the discriminant group.

A positive-definite even lattice \(L\) has finite quadratic group \(D=L^*/L\), with \(Q(a)=(a,a)/2\bmod\mathbb Z\). A discriminant gluing identifies this form with the negative of the form labeling the commutant’s invertible modules, so that the paired summands have integral conformal weight; for the stated strongly rational holomorphic class with positive nonvacuum commutant weights, they extend the tensor-product vertex algebra. In a higher-genus amplitude, one such identification acts on every handle.

A standard section of the induced representation used for an Eisenstein series is a parameter-dependent section whose restriction to the maximal compact subgroup is independent of the parameter. Here the section is fixed by a real Gaussian and finite lattice-coset characteristic functions. Its meromorphic continuation fixes the regularized value before comparison with the genus average.

The metaplectic group is the double cover of a real symplectic group on which square roots of the determinant automorphy factor can be chosen coherently. Half-integral-weight theta and Eisenstein series use this cover together with the Weil representation; the compatible factors make the combined summand independent of the chosen lift.

Plumbing glues two coordinate discs by \(zw=q\), with \(q\) the sewing parameter. A formal sewing amplitude is expanded in finitely many such parameters using graded states and their duals. An amplitude continued as a section has the prescribed conformal-anomaly line and coordinate transition laws; it need not be a globally defined scalar function on moduli.

\(\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)\) is the category obtained by adjoining filtered colimits to \(\mathcal C\). The Virasoro field object here is a direct sum of simple sectors: each state has finite sector support, even though a field output is completed in conformal weight inside its finitely many possible sectors.

For irrational Virasoro parameter, the two degenerate fusion directions have quantum \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) fibres. Their tensor fibre includes the cross-parity correction to braiding and twist, so the two fundamental rows have mixed full monodromy \(-1\). Its coherent tensorator is retained when constructing the fields.

An uncurving mark specifies the change of differential used to compare a curved or marked module problem with ordinary complexes. In the exterior example, \(\lambda\in k^r\) changes \(D\) to \(D-\sum_i\lambda_iN_i\); the weak equivalences are the maps that become quasi-isomorphisms under that particular change.

A dg bi-Galois object is a dg algebra with commuting left and right Hopf coactions, scalar coinvariants, and invertible left and right canonical Galois maps. Strict means that these maps are actual dg isomorphisms on the specified algebraic complexes. In the exterior example both Hopf algebras are \(K\).

For a right \(K\)-comodule \(M\) and a left \(K\)-comodule \(L\), \(M\mathbin{\square}_KL\) is the equalizer of the two coaction maps from \(M\otimes L\) to \(M\otimes K\otimes L\). The strict algebraic cotensor used here is formed in dg complexes with direct-sum tensor totalization.

A realized vacuum diagram assigns a quasi-coherent coefficient sheaf to the vacuum at every finite configuration, with its finite-map, unit-insertion and disjoint-fusion comparisons. Admissibility here requires the stated coherent comparison isomorphisms, no nonzero sections supported on collision diagonals, and normalization of the empty coefficient as an algebra with its true unit. These are geometric hypotheses on the full diagram.

Such a system gives categories over finite configuration spaces, compatible parameter pullbacks and external fusion on disjoint configurations, together with coherent unit and partition maps. In the weak form used here, external fusion on the whole categories need not be an equivalence, although the specified vacuum comparisons for surjections and disjoint fusion are required to be invertible.

For a nonnegatively energy-graded complex, an energy-additive operation sends inputs of energies \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) to energy \(e_1+\cdots+e_n\). A nullary such operation has energy zero. This grading condition is separate from covariance under translation or geometric support.

The constant ghosts are the energy-zero generators \(c_0^a\) of the polynomial affine Chevalley–Eilenberg complex. They form the subcomplex \(C^*(\mathfrak g;k)=\Lambda\mathfrak g^*\), with its Chevalley–Eilenberg differential and, for a nondegenerate invariant form, the degree-minus-two inverse-form bracket.

For complexes \(A,B\) over the indicated ground field, a degree-\(j\) element of full algebraic Hom assigns a linear map \(A^n\to B^{n+j}\) at every \(n\). The components form a product over \(n\). The differential is \(\delta f=d_B f-(-1)^j f d_A\). In particular a boundary formula evaluated on a nonclosed input includes its contribution from \(d_A\). Continuity, differential-module linearity and geometric support require their own hypotheses.

A relative cofibration of dg operads retains a specified source operad while permitting homotopically free extensions of its operations. In the concrete cellular presentations used here, generators are adjoined in well-ordered stages and each new differential lies in earlier stages; retracts give the general cofibrations. This is the hypothesis that allows an action to be extended while keeping already specified operations fixed.

An operadic augmentation is a morphism from an operad to the identity operad, which has only its identity operation in arity one. For an integer-weighted operad it is weight-preserving when every nonzero-weight element maps to zero and the identity has weight zero. A strict algebra unit together with multiplication can obstruct such an augmentation.

The reduced bar cooperad of an augmented operad is built from finite trees decorated by suspended elements of its augmentation ideal. Its differential combines the internal differential and contraction of internal edges; conilpotence means iterated reduced decomposition terminates on each finite tree. The weight-zero quotient used here projects every output factor to weight zero.

For a complex with differential \(d\) and translation \(T\), a degree-minus-one map \(K\) with \(dK+Kd=T\) is a translation nullhomotopy. On a cycle \(b\) it gives a primitive \(K b\) of \(Tb\). The choice of such a primitive for the image of an odd exterior generator is part of a derived map. The homotopy equation alone imposes no Leibniz rule for \(K\). [The one-generator mapping space](#ch07-ordinary-exterior-sources-and-the-map-they-compute).

A roof represents a map after localization by a diagram \(A\leftarrow R\to B\) whose left arrow is an allowed equivalence. The geometric roof pairing uses a resolving object and its independently defined configuration operations to compare the two pairings. Its nullhomotopy on separated configurations is retained as part of the comparison data.

After gauge transport of a two-position pairing, choose an output coordinate \(u_t=tz_1+(1-t)z_2\) and normal coordinate \(w=z_1-z_2\). Extracting the \(dw\) coefficient and then normal derivative order zero gives a state operation. The endpoint extractions use \(t=0\) and \(t=1\); their average is distinct from extraction at the midpoint.

glossary.term: Positive PBW weight and the finite-support dual
glossary.definition: For the one-position affine bar, the positive PBW weight assigns \(2n+1\) to \(j_n=x_{-n-1}\) and \(c_n\), and adds weights in monomials and bar words. Completion allows infinite sums as this positive weight increases. The continuous graded dual has finite support in the completed weight direction, so an algebraic inverse with an unbounded fixed-energy word tail can fail to act on it.

For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a characteristic-zero field, with \([x_a,x_b]=f_{ab}^{\ c}x_c\) and invariant symmetric form \(\beta\), the polynomial dg model \(Y_\beta\) has generators \(y_{a,n}\) of degree zero and \(\eta_n^a\) of degree one, \(n\ge0\), with relations \([y_{a,i},y_{b,j}]=f_{ab}^{\ c}y_{c,i+j}\), \([y_{a,i},\eta_j^b]=-f_{ac}^{\ b}\eta_{i+j}^c\), and anticommuting \(\eta\)-generators. Its differential is \(Q\eta_n^a=\tfrac12 f_{bc}^{\ a}\sum_{i+j=n-1}\eta_i^b\eta_j^c\) and \(Qy_{a,n}=n\beta_{ab}\eta_{n-1}^b+f_{ab}^{\ c}\sum_{i+j=n-1}(\eta_i^b y_{c,j}+y_{c,j}\eta_i^b)/2\), while translation sends either mode \(a_n\) to \(na_{n-1}\), with negative-index terms zero. Its elements are finite PBW words; the full restricted bar resolution maps quasi-isomorphically to this model and has additional generators dual to composite PBW entries, which the comparison kills.

For a closed marked surface of genus \(g\ge2\), the two arguments specify the conformal structures on the oppositely oriented ends of the quasi-Fuchsian manifold. After choosing a base point, the classical Liouville action determines a Hermitian holomorphic polarization \(F_o\); the kernel is \(K_c(X,\overline Z)=\exp(cF_o(X,\overline Z)/(24\pi))\). Its domain here is the whole smooth marked product, without nodal points or a moduli quotient.

glossary.term: Hermitian holomorphic kernel and positive type
glossary.definition: A Hermitian holomorphic kernel \(K(X,\overline Z)\) is holomorphic in \(X\), antiholomorphic in \(Z\), and satisfies \(K(X,\overline Z)=\overline{K(Z,\overline X)}\). It is of positive type if \(\sum_{i,j}\overline a_iK(X_i,\overline{X_j})a_j\ge0\) for every finite set of points and coefficients. Such a kernel is a Gram pairing of Hilbert-space evaluation vectors.

The holomorphic polarization of a real-analytic potential \(\Phi\) is a function \(F(z,\overline w)\) whose diagonal is \(\Phi(z)\). Its diastasis is \(D(z,\overline w)=\Phi(z)+\Phi(w)-F(z,\overline w)-F(w,\overline z)\), which removes the ambiguity of adding the real part of a holomorphic function to \(\Phi\). The normalization at a base point fixes the remaining holomorphic gauge used in the kernel.

For harmonic Beltrami representatives on a closed hyperbolic surface, the full Weil–Petersson Hermitian pairing used here is \(H(\mu,\nu)=\int\mu\overline\nu\,dA\). Its form is \(\omega_{\mathrm{WP}}=iH_{j\bar k}\,dt_j\wedge d\bar t_k\). This normalization fixes the scale \(c/(24\pi)\) in the projective-immersion criterion.

A quasicircle is the image of the circle under a quasiconformal map. A normalized exterior univalent map belongs to the Weil–Petersson class when its Grunsky operator is Hilbert–Schmidt. This universal welding domain is distinct from the Teichmüller space of a fixed closed surface.

For a normalized univalent map \(f\), the mixed coefficients of \(\log((f(z)-f(w))/(z-w))\), or its differentiated kernel, define the Grunsky operator on a Bergman Hilbert space. In the finite-genus setting here it maps conjugate holomorphic one-forms to holomorphic one-forms, is equivariant for the fixed surface group, and has norm less than one. Hilbert–Schmidt and ordinary trace-class properties must be distinguished from a finite fundamental-domain trace.

A Bers slice parametrizes marked quasi-Fuchsian structures while holding the conformal structure of one boundary component fixed. It realizes the other Teichmüller variable in a bounded domain of holomorphic quadratic differentials, with the surface-group equivariance fixed.

The Bergman space \(A^2(\mathbb D)\) here is the Hilbert space of square-integrable holomorphic one-forms on the disc. For bounded operators commuting with a torsion-free cocompact group whose disc quotient is a closed surface of genus \(g\ge2\), integrating the diagonal kernel over one fundamental domain gives the finite group trace, normalized here by \(\tau_\Gamma(1)=g-1\). This trace is defined on the equivariant algebra, and need not agree with an ordinary trace on the full Hilbert space.

At a point, the full mixed jet matrix of order \(m\) has entries \(\partial^\alpha\bar\partial^\beta K\) with \(|\alpha|,|\beta|\le m\), or the congruent Taylor matrix divided by \(\alpha!\beta!\). Every independent several-variable derivative is included. Restriction to a holomorphic curve instead tests a one-variable matrix and is weaker.

glossary.term: Projective Hilbert space and Fubini–Study form
glossary.definition: Projective Hilbert space is the space of complex one-dimensional subspaces of a Hilbert space. For a local nonzero holomorphic vector representative \(v\), the Fubini–Study form used here is \(i\partial\bar\partial\log\|v\|^2\). A holomorphic isometric immersion pulls this form back to the specified Kähler form; projective unitary monodromy means that continuation around a loop acts on its image lines by a unitary operator modulo scalars.

The injectivity radius at a point of a curvature-minus-one hyperbolic surface is the largest radius on which the exponential map is injective. A disc of any smaller radius embeds isometrically. The large-disc obstruction uses a radius bound at one point, not a lower bound at every point of the surface.

A Beltrami differential locally has the form \(\mu(z)\,d\bar z/dz\) and describes a deformation of complex structure through \(\bar\partial f=\mu\partial f\). For \(\|\mu\|_\infty<1\), normalized solutions are quasiconformal maps. Compact support and surface-group periodization specify the actual families used in the closed-surface counterexamples.

The unitary Virasoro minimal charges are \(c=1-6/[p(p+1)]\) for integers \(p\ge2\); \(p=2\) is the zero-charge endpoint. The positive minimal charges correspond to \(p\ge3\). Their appearance in the universal positivity theorem does not by itself settle the fixed-genus kernel.

A real-valued potential is strictly plurisubharmonic when its Hermitian Hessian \((\partial_i\bar\partial_j\Phi)\) is positive definite. If the potential is real analytic it admits a local holomorphic polarization; positivity of this Hessian alone is weaker than positive type of its exponential kernel.

A tensorator for a strong monoidal functor \(F\) is a natural isomorphism \(F(X)\otimes F(Y)\cong F(X\otimes Y)\), together with the unit identification, satisfying the associativity and unit coherence diagrams. It is part of the fibre functor used to assemble the degenerate Virasoro fields.

For \(Z=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}Z_e\) with energy-preserving differential, an energy retraction onto \(A_0=Z_0\) consists of inclusion \(i\), projection \(p\), and an energy-preserving degree-minus-one map \(H\), with \(pi=1\), \(H|_{A_0}=0\), and \(dH+Hd=1-ip\). The affine contraction uses division by the positive integer energy on each positive-energy summand.

glossary.term: Cofree conilpotent coalgebra and Taylor components
glossary.definition: The algebraic cofree conilpotent symmetric coalgebra on a graded vector space \(W\) is the direct sum of its finite symmetric powers, with coproduct obtained by all splits of the inputs. Project the value of a coderivation on \(n\) inputs to the cogenerators \(W\). This gives a graded symmetric multilinear map \(S^nW\to W\), its Taylor component of arity \(n\). For a coalgebra map the projection takes values in the target cogenerators. All these components together determine the map or coderivation. On \(S^c(Z[3])\), a degree-one square-zero coderivation encodes the shifted Lie operations of arity \(n\) and degree \(4-3n\) on \(Z\).

For a degree-zero product \(\mu\) and degree-minus-two bracket \(b\), the Leibniz defect is \(L_b(a;x,y)=b(a,\mu(x,y))-\mu(b(a,x),y)-(-1)^{|a||x|}\mu(x,b(a,y))\). A Leibniz cell is a degree-minus-three operadic generator with differential this defect. Assigning it a homotopy \(M\) with \(\delta M=L_b\) realizes the Leibniz identity up to that specified homotopy.

Adjoin even free fields \(t,p\) and odd free fields \(\eta,\iota\), with \([p_\lambda t]=[\iota_\lambda\eta]=1\), \(Qt=\eta\), \(Q\iota=p\), and write a subscript \(i\) for \(T^i\). The path substitution is \(\Gamma_s(u_i)=u_i-\kappa s t_{i+1}\), \(\Gamma_s(c_i)=c_i-s\eta_i-ds\,t_i\); \(h_{\mathrm{path}}\) integrates its \(ds\) coefficient, while \(h_{\mathrm{cone}}(a)=\int_0^1\sum_i\iota_i(\partial_{u_i}a)(u+sp,c)\,ds\). The comparison uses \(h=h_{\mathrm{path}}-h_{\mathrm{cone}}\), the endpoint \(\phi(u_i)=u_i+p_i\), \(\phi(c_i)=c_i\), and projection \(P\) that kills all auxiliary fields.

In the finite fusion-operator example, identity level means that the level endomorphism \(\eta:H\to H\) is \(\operatorname{id}_H\). It is a specified datum of that example, distinct from the choice of bicharacter and comodule braiding.

glossary.term: Raw output gauge and diagonal distribution
glossary.definition: For an output coordinate \(u\) and translation homotopy \(K\), the raw output gauge is \(g_u=1+du\,K\), before adding comparisons between different choices of output coordinate. In the algebraic differential-module direct image along a diagonal, \(\delta v\) denotes the generator associated to a state \(v\); zero normal order means that no normal derivatives have been applied to this generator. The midpoint counterexample compares these raw gauges on that generator.

Let \(j:U\hookrightarrow X\) include the distinct-position locus, let \(L\) be its local system, and let \(i:x\hookrightarrow X\) be a collision point. The complex \(i^*Rj_*L\) computes cohomology on the intersection of \(U\) with a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(x\). A sheaf extending \(L\) supplies a map from its stalk at \(x\) to this complex. Four unit charges at level two give a two-dimensional space in each of degrees two and three. Different attaching maps can have the same ranks. [The four-ray calculation](#ch04-gaussian-collision).

On a punctured disk take a complex rank-one local system with full-turn monodromy \(-1\). Its circle cochain differential is \(-1-1\), so the derived direct image has zero stalk at the puncture, just as extension by zero does. A coefficient \(L\) has clean extension across a boundary if the canonical map \(j_!L\to Rj_*L\) is an isomorphism there. For the four-ray collision this test must be made again at the full diagonal. [The four-ray link](#ch04-gaussian-collision).

Let \(j\) include the separated configurations and \(i\) the closed collision stratum. The open coefficient \(L\) determines a complex \(i^*Rj_*L\) at the collision, its link. To specify an extension with closed coefficient \(V\), give an arrow \(V\to i^*Rj_*L\). The resulting complex is \(Rj_*L\times^h_{i_*i^*Rj_*L}i_*V\). For four level-two unit charges, different arrows can give the same stalk and costalk dimensions. [Four charged rays](#ch04-gaussian-collision).

A loop that rotates a cluster of labelled points once, keeping the outside points away. For a rank-one charged Gaussian coefficient at level \(k\), it acts by \(\exp(2\pi i\sum_{a<b}\alpha_a\alpha_b/k)\), with the sum over pairs inside the cluster.

For an adjunction \(\Phi\dashv\Psi\), the natural map \(X\to\Psi\Phi X\). Here \(\Phi\) is derived tensor with the affine regular-top object and the source uses ordinary quasi-isomorphisms. Invertibility for every source is equivalent to full faithfulness of \(\Phi\).

For long roots of squared length two, the shifted level is \(s=\ell+h^\vee\), where \(\ell\) is the scalar central level of the affine mode algebra and \(h^\vee\) is the dual Coxeter number. Critical level means \(s=0\). [The ordinary induction unit](#atlas-k-affine-unit-levels).

In the one-loop Hall algebra over \(R=\mathbb Q[\hbar]\), evaluation at the origin reads the constant term of a root polynomial. More generally a finite root jet is an \(R\)-linear functional on symmetric root polynomials of a fixed charge which vanishes above some finite total degree. In charge one the convention is \(J_i(f)=\partial_x^i f(0)\), so \(J_i(x^i)=i!\). Transposing a Hall product sends an output jet to a functional on the ordered pair of inputs. [The transpose on two singletons](#ch15-one-loop-on-finite-root-jets).

Let \(t\) be a local parameter acting injectively on the terms of a cochain complex, as it does in the free parameter family here. Lift a cocycle modulo \(t\) to \(x\). Then \(dx=ty\), and the cohomology class of \(y\bmod t\) is the first Bockstein. Adding \(tz\) to the lift adds the boundary \(dz\) to \(y\). A nonzero class obstructs lifting to a cocycle modulo \(t^2\).

For the zero-mode-free harmonic disk, a real collar with transfer parameter \(0<q\le1\) multiplies a monomial of energy \(E\) by \(q^E\). Both \(p_1^2\) and \(p_2\) have energy two. Propagating either state on one side of a pairing therefore multiplies that pairing by \(q^2\). This Gaussian transfer is the Mehler collar. [The energy-two measurement](#ch11-relative-phase).

A densely defined linear map is closable when the closure of its graph is still the graph of a linear map. In particular, a sequence of inputs tending to zero cannot have outputs tending to a nonzero value.

Over a commutative ring \(R\), a finite free matrix factorization of \(W\in R\) is a \(\mathbb Z/2\)-graded finite free module with an odd endomorphism \(Q\) such that \(Q^2=W\,1\). Boundary operators have differential \(B\mapsto QB-(-1)^{|B|}BQ\). For \(W=x^3\) the two off-diagonal entries \(x,x^2\) give the stabilized residue field at the origin. [The cubic boundary](#ch19-boundary-potential).

At a formal critical point of a potential \(W\) over \(k\), take \(k[[x_1,\ldots,x_r]]\) modulo the ideal of its partial derivatives. For \(W=x^3\) in characteristic zero, the classes of \(1,x\) form a basis. The identity defect realizes their multiplication. A numerical sphere amplitude also requires a trace. [The identity defect and residue trace](#ch19-diagonal-and-trace).

The ordinary vertex algebra obtained by taking the universal envelope of the vertex algebroid for the dressing action of \(\mathfrak g[u]\) on the negative-loop group at a chosen invariant level. Its functions and currents depend on a vertex coordinate independent of \(u\). At level zero, group multiplication lifts to a coproduct on fields.

The complex surface \(\operatorname{Tot}_{\mathbb P^1}\mathcal O(2)\) parametrizing oriented affine lines in Euclidean three-space. Marking a point on the line adds a real fibre to give the five-dimensional correspondence space.

The associative quotient of a nonnegatively integer-graded vertex algebra in which the class of a homogeneous state \(a\) of weight \(h\) acts on the lowest graded piece of a module by the zero mode \(a_{(h-1)}\). For the vertex translation \(T\), one has \([Ta]=-h[a]\).

A tensor combining two systems of coefficients on the same configuration of points. For associative chiral algebras on words one can take the extraordinary tensor of their bars and then apply cobar, provided the cut maps respect the regrouping of factors. With braided coefficients the regrouping includes the specified exchanges.

For polynomials on a symplectic vector space, \(B_m(f,g)\) contracts the \(m\)-th derivative of each input against the other using \(m\) copies of the Poisson bivector. With \(\{x,y\}=1\), \(B_1\) is the Poisson bracket and \(B_3(x^3,y^3)=36\). The first scalar diagonal correction is \(B_3/12\). In the marked four-current bracket, keeping both negative-current outputs constant instead gives the factor \(B_2(p,q)(0)/4\). On \(p=x^2,q=y^2\) it equals one. [Constant transverse output in the Ward identity](#ch19-marked-sl2-cubic-closure). [The coordinate formula for the Poisson transvectant](#ch19-poisson-transvectant).

essay_lead: Two probes can each support a consistent action. What does acting twice do after they are joined? In a free field the positions of charged probes also enter their product. An independent disk filling measures the resulting state, and a joint reading of two harmonics distinguishes preparations with identical single-mode laws.

decisive.heading: Which bulk and boundary operations admit a common construction?
decisive.intro: A proposed duality makes predictions about independently specified objects. The questions below identify the source of each prediction, the operation that could test it and the hypotheses under which the comparison is defined.

questions.title: A Koszul duality for endpoint fields and their collisions

question.title: Realize the coefficient dual by the two ordered endpoint products
question.text:
For a smooth physical endpoint category construct the functor, its adjoint and both ordered products. Identify its filtered transverse bar or module-\(\operatorname{Hom}\) dual with the polynomial line algebra by maps compatible with both adjunction triangles. The comparisons must retain numerical and Jordan charge sectors, the positive filtration, empty unit, occupied vacuum, spectral tensorators, total-position connection and the independently normalized associator. They must extend the regular operations to supported collisions, including the nonconsecutive \(13\mid2\) channel.

Three algebraic inputs are available on distinct domains. The ordinary affine induction unit is invertible in every simple type at nonrational shifted level under its native realization assumptions. The horizontal restricted-current comparison applies to every ordinary unbounded binary pair on its specified jointly torsion smooth output tests. At precision three and noncritical numerical level, the four-colour algebraic marked comparison holds in all rooted degrees on the restricted whole Laurent source with prescribed positive inserted maps. The physical binary junctions and their unit and counit must still realize the latter operations independently.

questions.why: A junction of two physical lines has an input order, a unit and a collision product. Identifying the adjunction and both ordered products would let the coefficient dual compute these junction fields. Analytic specialization and generation of the physical category require additional comparisons.

known.title: Two point-kernel theories are already distinguished
known.text: For the polynomial Heisenberg point algebra, the ordinary derived kernel is the local-cohomology coring \(R\Gamma_{(t)}\mathbb C[t]\), with image the \(t\)-power-supported sector. A separate product-bar/hybrid homotopy–derived enhancement has the diagonal Koszul coring and retains every algebraic unbounded charged complex and all module-linear maps. Finite independent point tensors and the specified polynomial, fixed-field and energy-product bounds are established. These point kernels do not yet supply actions and balanced unit/counit for the unaugmented geometric transverse monoid.

known.title: Separated charge transport has finite higher operations
known.text: On fully separated configurations, the reduced exterior model has a strictly unital finite \(A_\infty\) automorphism and inverse, with finite insertions for arbitrary finite commuting charge matrices, including Jordan blocks. The absolute spectral cocycle is interpreted by rational substitutions before a common Laurent expansion. The formal comparison criterion retains its full normalized universal Maurer–Cartan hypothesis; it does not supply the missing supported Taylor target or a finite numerical-charge homotopy for an unspecified comparison.

known.title: Algebraic induction is an equivalence at every level
known.text: For every finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and every level, including critical level, algebraic induction gives the full unbounded enhanced equivalence after exactly its induction-detected class \(W_F\) is inverted. Restricted twisted coinduction supplies the inverse and marked adjunction; \(W_F\) is a proper subclass of ordinary line-module quasi-isomorphisms. The separate ordinary first-kind adjunction has a full Hom model under its specified native hypotheses. With the coherent smooth action, compatible common Taylor cutoffs and enhanced tensor–Hom adjunction, its actual unit at nonrational shifted level in every simple type is invertible on every ordinary unbounded source, and its image is exactly \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\) in the ungraded convention and \(\operatorname{Loc}\{W\langle a\rangle:a\in\mathbb Z\}\) in the graded convention. Under the coherent native-action and actual adjunction inputs, together with the actual unit and full smooth/algebraic comparison on common-lower-energy subcategories, critical and specified negative levels have explicit nonzero sources with zero realization. The marked all-energy, completed-energy and geometric fusion comparisons retain their own carriers and weak classes.

known.title: Finite-quotient point duality includes critical level
known.text: For the general-linear Yang double of rank \(n\ge2\) at each finite quantum precision, point duality holds between termwise \(R_N\)-free complexes of smooth modules, with \(R_N=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^N)\), \(N\ge1\), and graded-projective curved contramodules, using reduction-defined null classes. Support estimates, finite base change, adjunction and unit/counit are retained, including critical level. The formal limit, ordinary-derived equivalence and factorization-module comparison are stronger statements and remain separate.

known.title: Induction preserves the marked comparison in every energy
known.text: For every finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra, every level and every finite horizontal top, the actual contragredient object and normalized marked arrow are identified in every energy. At raw level zero the vacuum arrow has rank one and its entire cone is computed. The full algebraic induction null class is the explicit thick, direct-sum-closed class generated by exact totalizations and ghost-zero inflated acyclic smooth current modules. The separate ordinary first-kind unit is globally invertible for every simple type at nonrational shifted level under its native hypotheses, while critical and specified negative levels admit unit kernels under the coherent native action, actual adjunction, and actual-unit/full smooth-algebraic comparison on common-lower-energy subcategories. The completed-energy equivalence uses a different carrier and weak class.

known.title: Derivative coefficients of the four current and ghost fields
known.text:
Take the three trace-free currents of \(\mathfrak{gl}_2\), the trace current and their four ghosts, with coefficients in \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\). In the resulting state complex the coefficient derivative identity holds at every exterior length, jet order and numerical level. Its second-order exterior differential operator has order at most three, and the generator-left quadratic and cubic ghost rows are explicit. To record field values, assign an inserted state a Laurent-valued map on the algebraic current states \(V\). The covariant complex \(Q=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M,\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(V,V((u))))[-1]\) has both rooted actions, marked degree \(1-n\) and a scalar-vacuum dg retract. At a fixed noncritical level the [marked evaluation on Laurent series](#ch17-all-retained-marked) also requires one ghost cutoff and finite right support on each whole series.

Scope: All four colours, ordinary Koszul signs and algebraic state inputs are retained. Combined kernels are formed before coincident-germ substitution. The exterior-operator order bound is not a rooted Taylor-arity bound; generator-left products do not assert arbitrary composite-left products.
hypotheses: All four colours, ordinary Koszul signs and algebraic state inputs are retained. Combined kernels are formed before coincident-germ substitution.
The exterior-operator order bound is not a rooted Taylor-arity bound; generator-left products do not assert arbitrary composite-left products.

known.title: Full bars retain the selected unary maps and Wilson roofs
known.text: The selected binary collision extends to every finite full-bar arity with literal tree and block faces, source units and the prescribed mixed unary value. Polynomial collision modules have an actual two-sided-bar comparison. Finite Wilson inputs admit affine roofs under the stated irreducibility hypotheses; the ADE associator comparison retains its level range and physical-realization condition. A product span preserves both algebraic and physical deletion systems when no endpoint-preserving base map can identify them. Completed sources and larger geometric recipients remain additional.

known.title: The polarized geometric left vacuum is identified
known.text: At nonzero Heisenberg level, the prescribed polarized induced left vacuum is equivalent to the geometric vacuum module with its left action, ordered cuts, chart overlap, descendants and nonsplit pole extension. Finite numerical and Jordan right-chart modules have an explicit nilpotent-form gauge roof. Wick-coordinate coefficient completion preserves the coefficient action and localization attachment, while ordinary vacuum projection is discontinuous in that topology. The universal all-charge balanced bimodule and common all-strata completion remain distinct targets.

known.title: Completed induction has its own support theorem
known.text: The complete induction equivalence uses degreewise products of discrete energy fibres, continuous module maps, separate degreewise lower energy bounds and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), a bound \(e\ge L_\varepsilon-\varepsilon q^2\) for \(q\ge0\), with no negative-tail growth bound. Its actual unit and counit are continuous vector-complex deformation equivalences. Ordinary quasi-isomorphisms lie in its detected weak class, strictly at every simple critical level; equality holds in the specified energy-preserving and termwise bounded-above cases. The original algebraic induction theorem has a detected class strictly smaller than ordinary quasi-isomorphisms. The separate ordinary first-kind adjunction has a full unbounded model, an equivalence in all simple types at nonrational shifted level with the regular-top localizing image under native hypotheses, and critical and specified negative-level unit kernels under the coherent native action, actual adjunction, and actual-unit/full smooth-algebraic comparison on common-lower-energy subcategories. These ordinary results do not replace the completed carrier or its support condition.

known.title: A marked evaluation on the completed ordered source
known.text:
At each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\), \(\mathcal E_{\rm ten}=\mathcal P+\mathcal J+\Xi\), with \(\Xi=d_Q\mathcal H+\mathcal H d_{\rm ten}\), is an actual continuous dg bimodule evaluation for the full smooth native algebra. It is defined on every homogeneous element of the ordered polynomial marked carrier and its specified restricted Laurent extension. It has both coefficient-indexed Ward laws and transports through the finite and global Cartan isomorphisms.

Scope: The source is pointwise Hom on algebraic inserted CE inputs, with arbitrary completed left current values and exact RTT-pullback right-module quotients.
