In the polynomial carrier, each inserted input has one finite Laurent interval across all right slices. In the Laurent carrier, each fixed right slice and inserted input has one Laurent floor, one ghost cutoff and one finite right PBW support for the entire series. The recipient consists of Laurent-valued maps on algebraic inserted and rooted states. Trace currents and trace ghosts are retained. This is a particular checked evaluation; identification with the full prescribed physical right adjoint and full physical \(R_2\) normalization are separate.
hypotheses: The source is pointwise Hom on algebraic inserted CE inputs, with arbitrary completed left current values and exact RTT-pullback right-module quotients.

known.title: One finite horizontal family carries the native comparisons
known.text: A single selected family has its exact unary map, native Cartan closure, physical facets and units, Wilson and right-affine-bar roofs, binary tensorator and every finite native comparison for simple ADE \(\mathfrak g\), with long roots of squared length two, \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus(\mathbb Q\cup\mathbb R_{<0})\) and reflected affine level \(-k-h^\vee\). On the original point-source polynomial positive-weight continuous bar duals, shuffle restriction has an \(A_\infty\) inverse and a polynomial homotopy satisfying both relative identities. Contractible higher choices in the productwise external parameter model retain the canonical ternary normalization. In the separate rank-one abelian \(P=0\) example, exact unary data allow inequivalent ternary classes over the same fixed tensor base; no nondegenerate-\(P\) or varying-base obstruction is asserted. Further completed sources and larger geometric vacuum or block recipients retain their separate comparisons.

known.title: Endpoint coefficient comparisons preserve native attachments
known.text: The native polynomial cuts, finite-profile Laurent bars and separated smooth charged diagrams retain their established attachments and full matrix Homs. Whole-word image coordinates carry the controlled duality, and the mixed Laurent source supports the actual cut, inverse and supplied raw higher cells with its ordered support bounds. A fixed Cauchy root has a root-linear contraction on genuine complete balanced tensors without flatness; interval-profile transport moves the root action and sources together. Finite source quotients and functional-refinement pro diagrams provide their stated full-Hom comparisons. A larger regular energy-product source has a fixed raw-cell continuity obstruction, and its actual zero jet fails every uniform Laurent-shift bound. Common regular supported recipients, normalized-history homotopies and global physical sewing remain distinct comparisons.

known.title: A native right-linear contraction survives balanced tensor
known.text:
The exact ordered augmentation admits a continuous strong deformation retraction linear for the actual completed right \(A\)-action. Its homotopy is \(h_A=k(dk+kd+i\epsilon)^{-1}\). Ordinary balanced tensors inherit the contraction, including the Ward target \(A\otimes_{A_{\rm alg}}W_{\rm Ward}\).

Scope: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology. Every fixed numerical level, including zero and critical level. The assertion concerns the stated ordinary balanced tensors and does not identify a physical marked right adjoint.
hypotheses: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology.

known.title: The coefficient source carries the actual native state differential
known.text:
The pointwise Hom coefficient source on the actual native state complex has the all-source Cartan frame, literal \(\kappa/\Gamma\) square, full unit-relative map and compatible enlarged-stage finite-input diagram through \(R_3\). Restriction along the prescribed \(j_\hbar:B\to M\) is dg and degreewise surjective, with kernel \(\operatorname{Hom}(M/j_\hbar B,K[1])[-1]\).

Scope: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology. Every numerical level for the source maps; optional marked evaluation only at fixed \(K\ne-2\). Each algebraic input has finite word support, but its bound may vary with the input. The graded section retains its differential defect; the restriction kernel is not asserted acyclic. Differential and translation use enlarged windows, not frozen native weight quotients. The prescribed \(j_\hbar\) derived comparison and its action homotopies are established over the literal \(R_2\) quotient at each fixed finite loop cutoff, with the signed projection and proper-cone squares. This does not assert a strict full-current raw action or the corresponding full \(R_3\) physical comparison.

known.title: The sampled evaluation loses actual cohomology classes
known.text:
The sampled map kills a cubic source cycle generating a split free cohomology summand and the independent classes from every finite family of distinct nonrepeating trace exterior lists. These are nonzero classes in the actual ordered source, transported by the finite and global frames. Hence this particular sampled map is not a quasi-isomorphism, and a homotopy of it cannot restore injectivity.

Scope: Each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\); algebraic inserted and rooted states; the polynomial marked carrier or its restricted Laurent extension has a common floor, ghost cutoff and finite right support per right slice and inserted input. The same source-local conclusion holds at its stated \(R_2\) and \(R_3\) scopes without assuming cohomology base change. Only a physical comparison requiring this map to detect those classes is excluded.

known.title: The rank-one affine induction unit at nonrational shift
known.text:
For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\), native \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\) and raw affine level \(\ell=-k-2\), the actual unit \(L\to\Psi\Phi L\) is an equivalence for every ordinary unbounded \(Y_k\)-module, including nonzero ghost actions. The actual realization is fully faithful with image exactly \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\), or \(\operatorname{Loc}\{W\langle w\rangle:w\in\mathbb Z\}\) in the graded convention.

Scope: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately. The exact supported graded unit on the free object \(B\) and the prescribed strict smooth right-module model are retained inputs. Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed. The derived native ideal theorem, the full-domain reduction and the actual all-inflated unit are combined with their exact maps. The image is not asserted to be every smooth object or every object with torsion cohomology.

known.title: The native polar diagram has a fifth-order obstruction problem
known.text:
Determine the actual fifth-order residual for the prescribed \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) polar comparison in diagram form over \(k[K]\), retaining its native source, lower-order maps and operation identities. The collision-only strict Hopf-twist ansatz is a separate proposal, with a proposed order-\(\hbar^2\) obstruction; neither an all-order native comparison nor uniqueness is established by that proposal. The existing all-order elliptic theorem concerns its own specified family and does not settle this diagram comparison.

Scope: The source and prescribed operations belong to the native diagram-form polar problem. A strict Hopf twist, published existence of other quantum vertex structures and a distinct elliptic family are not replacements for that comparison. No new all-order theorem, uniqueness statement or universal native realization follows from this obstruction question.

known.title: Every source has an actual all-level realization model
known.text:
For every simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) and every native \(k\), the strict model \(Q=C_{\mathfrak g}\otimes B\), with \(C_{\mathfrak g}=\bigoplus_{E\ge0}U(t\mathfrak g[t])_E^\vee\), has the full affine action and original coherent right-\(B\) structure. Its ghost-twisted tensor computes actual realization on every ordinary unbounded \(B\)-module. This does not assert invertibility of the unit for arbitrary ghost-active modules.

Scope: Write \(B=Y_k(\mathfrak g)\), with normalized raw affine level \(-k-h^\vee\). The native polynomial dg algebra, original affine resolution and right-module lifts, coherent regular-top object, actual tensor–Hom adjunction, homogeneous endomorphism comparison and compatible Taylor/coherence input remain hypotheses. Ordinary unbounded graded and ungraded realizations are supplied separately, with algebraic internal sums of arbitrary support. No common energy bound, cohomological bound or finite-fibre assumption is imposed.

known.title: Every inflated ghost-quotient complex has its actual unit
known.text:
At every simple type and native parameter, including critical level and raw rank-one level \(-3\), the original signed unit is invertible on every ordinary unbounded \(H=U(\mathfrak g[t^{-1}])\)-complex inflated along \(B\to H\), hence on every inflated \(U(\mathfrak g)\)-complex. Its value at the inducing vacuum has sign \(+1\).

known.title: A finite bimodule-map nullhomotopy would give every unit
known.text:
For the actual fibre \(J\to B\to H\), nullity of one finite map \(\mu_N:J^{\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N}\to B\) in the actual derived bimodule category, together with units on every unbounded inflated \(H\)-complex, gives an explicit natural inverse to every unit. The construction is finite and does not require the right adjoint to preserve coproducts. The native all-inflated premise is supplied; native map nullity remains to be proved.

Ordinary unbounded graded and ungraded realizations are supplied separately, with algebraic internal sums of arbitrary support. No common energy bound, cohomological bound or finite-fibre assumption is imposed. The nullhomotopy must retain both B-actions in the selected graded or ungraded category. known.title: Every finite native ideal tensor power survives at raw minus three
known.text: For raw \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) level \(-3\), \(B=Y_1\) and \(R=U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\), every finite word \(B_1\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_3\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\cdots\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_{2N-1}\) is nonzero. The fibre of the ghost quotient \(B\to U(\mathfrak{sl}_2[t^{-1}])\) is a different bimodule. Finite nullity for its multiplication map and the full ordinary unit at this raw level remain open.

known.title: Intrinsic joint torsion is not fully faithful at positive-current sl2
known.text:
The actual inclusion \(D(\mathcal T)\to D(\mathcal S)\) for \(t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t]\) is not fully faithful in the ordinary unbounded graded and ungraded conventions. A shifted sum/product construction detects a nonzero \(\prod V_n/\bigoplus V_n\) defect in the actual torsion unit. At raw affine cocycle form zero, the specified positive-current splitting transfers the failure to affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), where the intrinsic torsion counit differs from cellularization on the displayed cellular object.

Scope: This is an unconditional result about the actual intrinsic torsion categories and their maps; it is not a native first-kind unit counterexample. The splitting transfers the failure of full faithfulness to affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) at raw form zero. Generation is tested on different objects. See the [positive-current tower](#ch06-theorem-a-complex-orthogonal-to-all-positive-current-cells) and [the quadratic tower at critical level](#ch06-theorem-a-critical-affine-complex-orthogonal-to-the-regular-top).

known.title: The tempting graded quotient is cellular with nonzero derived torsion
known.text:
For the specified graded positive-current construction, \(F=P_{\mathcal S}/P_{\mathcal T}\simeq Q[1]\), where \(Q=C_{\rm cof}\otimes(\prod V_n/\bigoplus V_n)\). Thus \(F\) is cellular and \(\mathbf R\Gamma(F)\simeq Q[1]\ne0\), even though termwise \(\Gamma F=0\). The displayed complex is not K-injective and is not an outside-cellular or derived-torsion-kernel witness.

Scope: Algebraically energy-graded positive-current sl2, ordinary unbounded derived categories, and the exact stated sum/product construction. No ungraded quotient formula, affine transfer, full essential-image equality or native-unit theorem is asserted.

known.title: The literal raw marked projection and its proper cone contract
known.text:
At every fixed numerical level through \(R_3\), the literal projection from the exact normalized intrinsic raw marked carrier to the existing ordered current target has a continuous coefficient-module-linear chain SDR. Its actual global-frame transport and proper unit-relative cone projection have the corresponding SDRs; their closed kernels are explicitly contractible. The degreewise finite perturbation retains the order-two product and products of first-order corrections.

known.title: A precision-three endpoint homotopy restores the reversed scalar field
known.text:
At each fixed \(K\ne-2\), the actual continuous endpoint-bimodule homotopy \(H_3\) gives \(\overline E_3=E_3-d_QH_3-H_3d_{\mathcal N}\) on the exact uniform-Laurent all-marked carrier. It restores the reversed physical scalar field while preserving both Ward laws, the prescribed minimal \(q/\omega\) pairings and the actual Cartan, current and proper-unit-cone diagrams. Exact restriction by \(j_\hbar\) retains the order-two \(H_1j_1\) term.

known.title: Critical current-invariant ghost-vacuum states survive freely
known.text: At \(K=-2\), every algebraic current-invariant state tensored with the ghost unit is a cycle of the four-colour \(R_3\) differential, including the Sugawara states. The frame equation on this subspace permits zero second-order correction. On the full state complex there is a choice of translation-compatible frame \(1+\hbar F_1+\hbar^2 F_2\) with the prescribed first coefficient. The graded algebraic state cohomology is free over \(R_3\) on the entire classical critical cohomology, with compatible reductions to lower precision. The regular products on the two corrected critical marks have their own rotation theorem. [Critical rotation on the two corrected marks](#s-critical-rotation-on-two-corrected-marks). The full singular field, the normalized all-degree marked comparison and the independent physical adjunction remain to be determined.

The state frame uses a choice of contraction and commutes with total translation and constant \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\).

known.title: Two cohomology classes undetected by the trivial current modules
known.text:
In degree \(-1\) and energy \(-2\) the linear functionals dual to the current modes \(f_1\) and \(h_1\) lift to two independent cohomology classes of a smooth complex \(X\). The uppermost column of the Koszul tower records these functionals. Their representatives use a common tail \(t^5\mathfrak{sl}_2(k)[t]\), even though the powers of the augmentation ideal needed to kill their successive components are unbounded. The smooth inverse limit has a nonzero, jointly torsion cohomology module in every strictly negative degree.

Let \(\mathcal S\) be the category of smooth algebraically integer-energy-graded modules over \(B=U(t\mathfrak{sl}_2(k)[t])\), for a field \(k\) of characteristic zero. Write \(I=\ker(B\to k)\) and let \(D_I(\mathcal S)\subset D(\mathcal S)\) consist of complexes whose cohomology vectors are each annihilated by some power of \(I\). The complex of maps from the trivial module in any fixed energy into the K-injective tower is contractible. Thus \[\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal S)}(k\langle e\rangle,X[j])=0\quad(e,j\in\mathbb Z),\qquad \operatorname{Loc}\{k\langle e\rangle:e\in\mathbb Z\}\subsetneq D_I(\mathcal S).\] Indeed, the class of objects with no maps to any shift of \(X\) is closed under shifts, cones and coproducts. It cannot contain \(X\), whose identity is nonzero.

Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(U\) forget the energy grading of the completed complex \(X\). The ungraded complex \(UX\) still has jointly torsion, nonzero cohomology, and \(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb C,UX[j])=0\) for every \(j\). Indeed, the exact right adjoint to forgetting puts a copy of its input on each integer energy sheet. Applied to \(UX\), it gives \(X\otimes V\), where \(V\) has one trivial line in each energy. The Koszul contraction extends to this tensor product by taking the smooth limit of the tensor-extended stages. Adjunction now gives the stated vanishing.

[The positive-current Koszul tower](#ch06-theorem-a-complex-orthogonal-to-all-positive-current-cells).
hypotheses: The grading is an algebraic direct sum over integer energies. The mode \(xt^r\) lowers energy by \(r\), and maps preserve energy. Smoothness means each vector is killed by some tail \(t^N\mathfrak{sl}_2(k)[t]\). The smooth product retains families with a common tail in each energy.

Use the Koszul tower in which the top column resolves a module placed in cohomological degree \(-1\) and a column indexed by a multiset of \(s\) mode indices \(a\) adjoined along the branch of currents \(et^a\) resolves a module placed in degree \(-s-2\).

Termwise joint torsion and bounded-below joint torsion cohomology still imply cellularity. The [common-tail criterion](#ch06-common-tail-completeness) and the [energy-floor bound](#ch06-energy-window) give further sufficient conditions.

known.title: The regular-top cells miss a torsion complex at critical level
known.text:
Let \(v\) generate the opposite right affine vacuum for \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), annihilated by the nonpositive modes. Normalize \((e,f)=1\) and \((h,h)=2\), write \(x_j=xt^j\), and let \(\ell\) be the raw level. The quadratic element \(S_2=h_1^2/2+e_1f_1+f_1e_1\) satisfies \((vS_2)e_{-1}=2(\ell+2)ve_1\). At \(\ell=-2\) the even-weight quadratic singular vectors give commuting operators on the restricted graded dual of this vacuum. Their Koszul tower \(Z\) is an actual smooth graded affine complex.

Put \(B=U(t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t])\) over \(\mathbb C\), and let \(W=A_{-2}\otimes_B\mathbb C\) be the affine module with regular horizontal top. The restriction of \(Z\) has jointly augmentation-torsion cohomology, with \(H^{-1}(\operatorname{Res}Z)=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}B_d^*\) for the grading by mode weight. All derived maps from every energy shift of \(W\) into \(Z\) vanish by adjunction with restriction. Hence the shifts of \(W\) generate a proper subcategory of the smooth complexes with jointly torsion cohomology. With long roots of squared length two the same construction works at \(\ell=-h^\vee\) for each finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra.

Write \(U\) for forgetting the grading. The complex \(UZ\) still has nonzero jointly torsion cohomology, and \(\operatorname{Hom}(UW,UZ[j])=0\) for every integer \(j\). Here one needs the quadratic tower itself. At each sufficiently deep current cutoff, its added Koszul branches contribute below any fixed cohomological degree, uniformly in energy. One can therefore tensor the restricted tower with a trivial line in every energy sheet and compute the smooth limit by the tensor-extended stages. Their signed face complexes contract in each multiset of quadratic modes. The exact adjunction for forgetting energy, followed by affine induction–restriction, gives the ungraded vanishing.

[The critical affine tower](#ch06-theorem-a-critical-affine-complex-orthogonal-to-the-regular-top).
hypotheses: Use the unbounded derived category of algebraically integer-energy-graded smooth affine modules over \(\mathbb C\), with degree-preserving maps and all energy shifts of the inducing module. Joint torsion is measured vector by vector using the augmentation ideal of the strictly positive-current enveloping algebra.

The critical witness uses quadratic singular vectors of the opposite right vacuum. Whether the regular top generates all complexes with jointly torsion cohomology at noncritical raw levels remains open.

known.title: A trace pair on two separately framed intervals
known.text:
Compose the holonomies of two separately framed oriented intervals to prepare the full trace, and use the rooted interval alone to prepare the bare trace. Extension and restriction of scalars along the holonomy pullbacks of de Rham algebras give adjoint functors. The unit \(p\mapsto1\otimes p\) and counit \(b\otimes n\mapsto bn\) satisfy both triangles by multiplication. On a free pair the tensorator multiplies the edge factors with their graded sign.

For the invariant trace ghost, pullback of the logarithmic one-form under multiplication adds the two interval forms. The signed singleton \(I[0]\) reads \(-1\) on both preparations in either root order. For the ordered trace jets \(i_0i_1\), pairing with \(I[0]\wedge I[1]\) gives \(+1\) for the full germ and \(-1\) for the bare root in the same orientation. These are model coefficients on two specified states. The [physical adjunction and its two products](#problem-physical-adjunction) require independent constructions on the full endpoint domain.
hypotheses: Use \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), independently framed inputs, the original trace dual, both original ordered tensor evaluations and the same orientation when returning to the labelled intervals.

known.title: Rotation of the two corrected critical marks
known.text:
At \(K=-2\) fix the corrected critical inputs \(\eta_\hbar,\Omega_\hbar\). Normalize the free-ghost probe by assigning coefficient one to the divided second ghost derivative in the contact applied to the constant Cartan ghost. A frame \(U_*=\exp(\hbar F+\hbar^2B_*)\) from the 23-contact family gives the rotation \(C_s=U_*s^NU_*^{-1}\), where \(N\) grades energy. On the finite invariant module of these marks and their two signed roots the outgoing map \(j_0U_*^{-1}\) is a chain map over \(R_3\). Both regular ordered products and both vacuum axes are transported. The reverse retained order uses its explicit homotopy. The stated sewing also holds with a rooted central matter state as spectator.

Enlarging this calculation to include the constant Cartan ghost \(h_0\) exposes two independent coefficient tests. In the order of the \(h_0\) and \(\eta_0\) rows, the possible contact column is proportional to \((2,4)\), and the required column is \((0,2)\). The functional \((1,-1/2)\) kills the first column and gives \(-1\) on the required one. This rules out that extension of the local contact construction. The normalized all-degree critical marked comparison and independent physical products remain open. [The retained marked comparison](#ch17-all-retained-marked).
hypotheses: Use the algebraic critical states over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\) with the prescribed first frame, original translations, unit axes, signed roots and outgoing absolute complex. The regular comparison uses \(s\ne0\). The reverse retained homotopy is evaluated on its specified marked inputs at half radius.

questions.title: Supported bulk operations and their global recipient

question.title: Construct the native operation system and its boundary action
question.text:
Actual native image composition, full global pure-\(Q\) contact formulas and the separate ungated one-\(Q\) physical-graph theorem are established with their rank, support and jet rules. A specified two-spectator scalar family has a canonical \(C^2\) trace, while its one-\(Q\) marked family has only the stated continuity result. Full repeated marked Ward operations, arbitrary gates and the required physical completion remain. Scalar two-forest exhaustion still fails on its original global domain.

For the universal affine cochain system with nondegenerate shifted form \(\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2\), construct the full regular, localized and supported configuration-operation complexes carrying the native product, the specified secondary operation and an independently defined boundary action. Solve the required relative four-face equations \(\delta F_4=E_4\) and \(rF_4-\delta G_4=h_{\mathrm{proper}}\) on \(12\mid3\mid4\) and \(12\mid34\) in that recipient, with its prescribed separated homotopy. In the mixed-current comparison, retain the original global coefficient domain and branch support, including all three escaping modules. The admitted finite Gaussian and contact-image compositions exist. Identify their actual intermediate-state object with the independent physical recipient, and extend through the required cut motions, nontransverse identifications and coefficient/completion maps.

questions.why: This would identify which higher operations belong to a native bulk and how they act on the boundary. It is a necessary bridge from state-level formulas to local observables and reconstruction. The actual actor category must be specified; representability in an algebraic category already excluded by a no-go theorem cannot be assumed.

known.title: The full projected affine fields agree on algebraic states
known.text: For finite-dimensional complex \(\mathfrak g\), universal balanced affine vacua and absolute ghosts, the specified projected two-copy fields agree on every algebraic state, including regular coefficients. The primary equality requires no inverse form. With invertible \(\beta\), the secondary agrees on all algebraic ghost jets with the endpoint-average operation. Some current-containing inputs fail the distinct residue comparison, so this does not identify the full native supported action.

known.title: The full scalar global answer retains three escaping modules
known.text:
For ordinary scalar mixed distributions with finite order on each compact and no uniform global normal-order bound, the three-position complex has
\[H^2(\mathcal I)=\mathcal E_u\oplus\mathcal E_s\oplus\mathcal E_v\oplus j_AP\oplus j_SP,\qquad s=u+v.\]
Here \(P\) is the joint point principal-part module and \(j_A,j_S\) are the two forest inclusions. Each \(\mathcal E_x\) is the specified locally finite Dolbeault cokernel; it vanishes after restriction to a smaller normal radius. The scalar finite-pole vacuum map has exactly the two forest modules as its degree-two image and \(\mathcal E_u\oplus\mathcal E_s\oplus\mathcal E_v\) as cokernel. The forest sum is intrinsically the simultaneous \(u,v\)-locally-nilpotent submodule and gives the unique polynomial-Weyl-linear section. This is algebraic scalar cohomology. The finite-normal complex and the normal germ limit have different answers; state-valued and all-position recognition remain open.

known.title: Affine antighosts, the coset stress tensor and transfer
known.text:
Take the universal pair of currents for a simple Lie algebra at levels \(\kappa,-\kappa-2h^\vee\), with the invariant form normalized so that the adjoint Casimir is \(2h^\vee\). Their sum \(J_\Sigma=J^{(1)}+J^{(2)}\) has level \(-2h^\vee\). Adding the ghost current gives \(J_{\rm tot}=J_\Sigma+J_{\rm gh}\) at level zero. In this complex Figueroa-O’Farrill’s normally ordered antighost has regular self-product. Its BRST differential is the coset stress tensor. Start with the Sugawara tensor of \(J_\Sigma\) at level \(-2h^\vee\), add the ghost stress tensor and subtract the Sugawara tensor of \(J_{\rm tot}\) at level zero. The resulting tensor has central charge zero. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) the invariant weight-two, ghost-number-minus-one spaces have dimension three. The self-product calculations cover the paired levels \((1,-5),(-2,-2),(0,-4),(-4,0),(5/7,-33/7)\) in rank one and \((1,-7),(-6,0)\) for \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\).

For rational currents at two positions, transport of the twisting morphism identifies the target connection as \(\partial_z+T\otimes1\), where \(z\) is the separation and \(T\) translates the first factor. A separate transfer takes place on a cochain complex with differential \(Q\). Suppose \(Qg+gQ=D\) and \(g^2=(Qw+wQ)/2\), for operators \(g,w\) of degrees \(-1,-3\). Use a \(D\)-equivariant contraction with inclusion \(i\), projection \(p\) and homotopy \(h\), so \(Qh+hQ=1-ip,\ pi=1,\ hi=ph=0\). On the retract, with differential \(d\), put \(K=pgi\) and \(K^{(2)}=pghgi+pwi/2\). Then \(dK^{(2)}+K^{(2)}d=K^2\). The classification of invariant self-products for general simple Lie algebras is open. The identity alone also leaves open the scalar of the second operator on the rank-one energy-zero Chevalley–Eilenberg complex, its independence of the contraction and cubic choice, its normalized ratio to the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov coefficient and the comparison of the full higher operations.
known.cite: For the current and ghost fields, J. M. Figueroa-O’Farrill, Affine Algebras, \(N=2\) Superconformal Algebras, and Gauged WZNW Models (1993), “The BRST Complex of an Affine Lie Algebra” and “When do we have an \(N=2\) SCA?”, arXiv:hep-th/9306164.

known.title: The residue diagram and relative unit resolution
known.text:
The unframed first Chevalley page has one origin-independent comparison for every collision, allowed target deletion and source vacuum absorption on full local Ext. It keeps the coefficient connection, floating output blocks and unrestricted reduced words. The relative James resolution has the full proper-unit-cube matching fibres. Its formal augmentation criterion and filtered version retain their explicit native comparison and connectivity hypotheses.

Scope: The full ordered collision atlas on \(\mathbb A^1\), algebraic states and energy sums, and every output partition are retained. The empty-configuration unit \(K\) is distinct from the positive diagonal vacuum \(J\); the bar-cobar recipient is the entire \(U=\Omega J\). Changing origins uses polynomial-form parameters finite separately on each input; no uniform parameter degree or normal-order bound is imposed. The first-page comparison does not by itself identify the separately normalized-row differential or give chain formality of the entire residue diagram.

At three positions, the six-image cone contains the two-image cone, adds an exact four-copy degree-one extension with no splitting asserted and removes only the same weighted forest image in degree two. The regular chain kernel of the direct comparison remains exact; its geometric composite has a known nonzero cohomological kernel without a full chain-kernel classification. Specialization at zero differs from taking images after specialization. All-position closure and descent remain additional.

known.title: The transverse augmentation locus
known.text:
For universal polynomial affine cochains of a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra with nondegenerate shifted form, the full ordered-atlas transverse monoid has a coherent unital augmentation through a connected space of choices. Its underlying mapping space is connected and simply connected, and every specified underlying map has a nonempty connected fibre of coherent lifts. For simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) at scalar level \(\ell\), the transverse augmentation space is nonempty exactly when \(\ell\ne-h^\vee\). Underlying critical coalgebra maps have their own nonempty mapping spaces after multiplication is forgotten.

Scope: The full ordered collision atlas on \(\mathbb A^1\), algebraic states and energy sums, and every output partition are retained. The empty-configuration unit \(K\) is distinct from the positive diagonal vacuum \(J\); the bar-cobar recipient is the entire \(U=\Omega J\). Characteristic zero; the shifted form is \(\kappa+\tfrac12\mathrm{Kil}\). The scalar-level criterion is pointwise in \(\ell\), for the original universal polynomial source and native transverse product. The all-output comparison retains arbitrary induced rank and all floating sectors before contraction. No noncritical contractibility or parameter-family trivialization is asserted.

known.title: Mixed currents have actual joint and geometric carriers
known.text: The parameter-proper joint-current carrier retains its stagewise moment comparisons, finite-particle cohomology and the distinction between full coefficient modules and polynomial contacts. The selected finite compatible all-mark image has an iterable bulk, sheet, real-wall and critical-normal differential for all native W/p/J sectors. Its disjoint-label Gaussian product has a computed Ward defect, and its mixed-relative source has an intrinsic restricted cone retract. All finite multispectator height boxes retain mutual contractions, jets and total endpoint forms. Actual height pullback and proper homotopy descend on the unmarked-plus-differential image, including the admitted loss of real rank. For finite ungated whole products of scalar ray kernels and holomorphic poles the general second-derivative and separate one-mark estimates use a nonzero retained real form on each ray. Proportional forms are allowed. Physical selection, full normal generators, endpoint grafting, marked/composite height descent and unrestricted completion remain separate.

questions.title: Full base change in the centre construction

question.title: Full base change and the genuine centre comparison
question.text:
For the nonzero-level Heisenberg algebra \(A\), determine whether the required base transitions of the full two-legged cocycle categories induce nerve weak equivalences, with every original source refinement and admissible target link retained. Every base arrow reduces to a surjective factor. For each fixed surjective base arrow and fixed admissible target, incoming tame coverage is a sufficient criterion for the full nerve transition to be a weak equivalence; no converse is asserted. This coverage remains unproved and requires an incoming refinement whose full ideal generated by the image of the base kernel is acyclic. For one exterior generator the actual roof-to-action map \(q_B\) is a weak equivalence with its unit homotopy retained. The zero-detector sector is connected and its marked identity-on-cohomology automorphisms form a contractible space. Distinct questions concern the full nilpotent inclusion and the strict-coslice to infinity-undercategory comparison.

Scope: Use the rank-one Heisenberg algebra \(A=V_\kappa\) over \(\mathbb C\), with \(J_{(1)}J=\kappa\mathbf1\) and \(\kappa\ne0\). The exterior generator \(\epsilon\) has degree one with \(d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0\). Use ordinary tensors and keep both legs of every admitted roof. Impose the stated admissibility conditions on the targets and the maps between them. The ideal generated by a subspace is its closure under the differential and the vertex ideal operations.

known.title: Surjective transitions identify the tame subcategory
known.text:
For a surjective base arrow \(a:d\to d'\), let \(I_g\) be the dg vertex ideal generated by \(h(\ker a)\). Quotienting by \(I_g\) gives \(NG_{d'}\simeq NG_d^a\), where \(G_d^a\) is the full subcategory with acyclic \(I_g\); the full transition is this equivalence followed by inclusion. A base section gives a retraction and injections on components and based homotopy groups. The displayed split example and pullbacks of strict-coslice cocycles are tame. A functorial incoming tame refinement is sufficient for the full split result; relative free/PBW exactness is a possible method, not an equivalent necessary condition. The forward-monotone ideal detector excludes certain outgoing arrows only and supplies no zigzag or \(q_B\) obstruction.

known.title: Self-linking is fixed by the charge
known.text:
Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(A=V_\kappa\), \(\kappa\ne0\), and \(B=\Lambda(\epsilon)\), with \(|\epsilon|=1\) and \(d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0\), using ordinary algebraic tensors. On a full unit-preserving roof, permissible lifts satisfy \(dz=0\), \(dw=Tz\), \(dv=w_{(0)}z\), with \(v\) in the acyclic kernel. The scalar \(f(v)=\operatorname{sl}(\alpha)\mathbf1\) is independent of the lift choices and all roof refinements. A full-roof self-bracket identity proves \[\operatorname{sl}(\alpha)=\frac{\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)^2}{2\kappa}\] on every genuine exterior-actor component, without nilpotent, energy-bounded, split or cofibrant source restrictions. For any quasi-isomorphic resolution target \(i:A\to W\), the same scalar multiple of the vacuum is \(H^0(i)^{-1}[f(v)-f(w)_{(0)}y]\), where \(dy=f(z)\), with all source and target links retained. The specific projected singular-bracket tuple formed from these lifts and their kernel primitives admits the normal form \[(F,\mathcal B,\mathcal V,\mathcal R)=(\gamma J+\beta\mathbf1,\kappa\gamma\mathbf1,\tfrac12\kappa\gamma^2\mathbf1,0),\qquad\gamma=\operatorname{ch}/\kappa,\quad\beta=\operatorname{ct},\] after an allowed path-roof enlargement. Choice/refinement-invariant functions solely of this tuple cannot distinguish components with the same charge and translation pair. This does not classify regular-product constructions or all binary coherent data, and does not make that pair complete. This self-linking detector supplies no third component parameter or obstruction to the image of \(q_B\) on components. The detector \(\Pi\) records \((\operatorname{ch}/\kappa,\operatorname{ct})\) and scalar loops. Since \(\Pi q_B\) is a weak equivalence, \(q_B\) has a left inverse up to homotopy. It is injective on components, with exactly one image component for each pair. The path on the zero-label component and the based-sphere calculation identify \(q_B\) as a weak equivalence. Full base transitions, the nilpotent inclusion and \(\lambda_B\) are separate open questions. The displayed ternary kernel primitives exist, but their invariance and values are not established.

known.title: Incoming tame refinements on specified source classes
known.text:
For the original split base \(U=A\ltimes N\), \(N=B\otimes(P\to L\to Q)\), actual non-tame objects exist. One has \(H^0(I_g)=Q\), \(H^1(I_g)=\epsilon Q\) and \(\Theta=0\), with both an outgoing projection and an incoming surjective tame refinement. Another has \(S=C_B\otimes\mathbb C[z,dz]\), \(I_g=C_B\otimes\mathbb C[z]dz\) and \(\Theta=A\). It has no outgoing arrow to a tame object, while the constructions below give incoming tame refinements. Its three specified old lifts remain non-tame; this does not exclude other lifts. For \(K=\ker p\), the full subcategory satisfying \(K_{(m)}I_g=0\) for every integer \(m\) has a natural incoming refinement \(S\ltimes_p(B\otimes N)\to S\), with an additional \(B\) factor and generated ideal exactly \(B\otimes N\). The output stays in that subcategory, giving its actual nerve homotopy equivalence with the corresponding \(A\)-base category and with its tame intersection. Separately, every admitted tensor source \(S=C\otimes A\) with canonical boundary and a possibly unbounded translation-zero cdga \(C\) has the refinement \(S\ltimes(C\otimes N)\to S\). This is natural for every under-\(A\) arrow between those sources and all prescribed target links. The output can leave the tensor-source class, so no nerve equivalence follows from this coefficient construction. Neither nonzero ideal cohomology nor \(\Theta=A\) is an actual fibre obstruction. The full tame inclusion remains open. A further theorem applies whenever an actual incoming relative presentation \(e:R\otimes A\to\sigma^*g\) is supplied, for arbitrary dg vertex algebra \(R\): \((R\otimes A)\ltimes(R\otimes N)\to g\) is an incoming tame refinement, natural for those presentation diagrams. Such presentations are not universally available. known.title: Every genuine loop detector has scalar image
known.text:
At every point \(\alpha\) of the genuine unit fibre \(\mathscr F_A(B)\), with its specified unit homotopy retained, the state-complex loop detector has exactly \(\operatorname{im}\chi_\alpha=\mathbb C\,\mathrm{id}_{U(A)}\). The actual loops \(\epsilon\mapsto\epsilon+\mu\,ds\) give an additive central section, compatible with basepoint transport, and an isomorphism of groups \[\pi_1(\mathscr F_A(B),\alpha)\cong\mathbb C_{\mathrm{add}}\times\ker\chi_\alpha.\] On the trivial component the two-copy scaling calculation kills the kernel, and convolution by a pointed action transports the result to every component. Thus \(\pi_1\) is precisely the additive scalar group. At the displayed \(q_B\) points, this scalar factor already comes from the source. On a chosen component, the scalar-detector fibre \(\Phi_\alpha\) is connected, with \(\pi_1(\Phi_\alpha)=\ker\chi_\alpha\) and \(\pi_n(\Phi_\alpha)=\pi_n(\mathscr F_A(B),\alpha)\) for \(n\ge2\); these groups vanish and the scalar-detector fibre is contractible. Strict sphere roofs retain their comparison paths: forgetting those paths gives free-sphere orbits, conjugacy classes in degree one. If the required primitive map extends after refinement to an \(f^{\prime}\)-derivation \(E\) with \(Ed=D\), the sufficient pointed nullhomotopy is \[G=f^{\prime}+\theta_n(1-s)D-ds\,\theta_nE.\] The negative final term is necessary in even degree as well. The proved binary vanishing is \(E_0(x_{1(m)}x_2)=0\) for closed degree-one inputs on every kernel-loop roof, for all \(m\). It does not cover arbitrary binary relations with nonclosed inputs or prove that \(E\) exists. Charge and constant give all components in this case. questions.title: An interface compatible with principal reduction

question.title: Compare the reduced affine kernel with the reflected Virasoro kernel
question.text:
Algebraic affine induction and reflected Virasoro comparisons are available with their exact weak classes. They do not themselves construct the independent marked defect-reduction square.

For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and \(t\ne0\), raw affine levels \(t-2\) and \(-t-2\), and \(c(t)=13-6(t+t^{-1})\), construct an independent defect reduction and a natural comparison \[\mathrm{DS}_{\mathrm{line}}\Psi_{\mathrm{aff}}\simeq\Psi_{\mathrm{Vir}}\mathrm{DS}_{\mathrm{aff}}.\] Prove the actual source/image and enhanced weak-equivalence conditions. Retain the coherent two-action kernel, paired constraint characters, ghost polarization, topology and shifts, and match the reduced augmentation to the contragredient universal vacuum at \(26-c(t)\). The first test is the actual marked counit/augmentation square with the anti-action signs; then compare native binary tensorators, position connections and collision faces.

questions.why: This would connect the affine duality, kernel and quantum-line constructions to Virasoro/oper defects through one native theorem. Complementary central charges make the square plausible but do not construct its arrows. A proof on a generated sector would retain the larger all-object and unbounded extension obligations.

known.title: The reflected category and its two vacuum marks are explicit
known.text: At every complex line charge \(c\), the reflected construction gives the stated enhanced equivalence with the full bounded-below subcategory of smooth complexes whose cohomology is jointly \(\mathfrak n_2\)-nilpotent. It imposes no internal-energy bound. The vacuum object maps to \(V_{26-c}\), while the augmentation maps to \(D_\sigma V_{26-c}\). The actual augmentation-induced ordinary-composition roof gives \(R\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C_\varepsilon)\simeq\Lambda(\eta_3)\), \(|\eta_3|=3\), even at nonsimple vacuum charges. The map between the two vacuum objects can still have a nonzero cone; these endomorphism comparisons do not identify the objects or supply fusion.

The scalar map ramifies at \(t=\pm1\); the native degree-three map and that compatibility are not computed by this formula.

known.title: The reflected null class and continuous dual are explicit
known.text: For full unbounded smooth jointly nilpotent Virasoro complexes, the reflected null class is the restriction-preimage of standard coacyclic comodules. It equals ordinary acyclics exactly outside the exceptional line charges \(c=1-\frac{6(p-q)^2}{pq}\), with coprime \(p,q\ge2\); at each exceptional charge an actual acyclic telescope retains a reflected class. Continuous opposition, smooth/continuous adjunctions and multiplicative derived endomorphisms have their stated intrinsic domains. Full ambient torsion also has an unbounded native-induction comparison. At separated supports the actual continuous tensorator is a chain homeomorphism with finite-arity coherences. The native supported-induction kernel is explicit, but its equality with ordinary acyclics or with the coacyclic class remains a different question; the reflected charge classification does not decide it.

known.text: For all unbounded smooth jointly positive-nilpotent Virasoro complexes, the reflected null class is strictly smaller than ordinary acyclicity exactly at line charges c=1−6(p−q)²/(pq), with coprime p,q≥2, and equals it at every other charge. No energy grading or finite-multiplicity hypothesis is imposed. Native induction has a different intrinsic kernel and an independently established all-algebraic torsion comparison. Continuous complementary pairings and separated-support spectral operations retain their own recipients; this does not identify a nonsimple universal vacuum with its contragredient or prove collision and physical-state comparisons.

question.title: Construct the source-dependent quantum comparison
question.text:
Ordinary and first-normal boundary operations cover every fixed finite universal \(e,h,f,b,c\) source through bare orders zero and one, with the antighost scalar sign and full source terms retained. Other higher-normal sectors have their own scopes. This does not identify the independent physical stress target or complete the comparison on all faces of the actions, sources and mapping complexes.

Construct the regulated BV pushforward from the constrained affine theory to the independently prescribed stress theory with stress and fundamental endpoint sources present before integration. Compare the full singular binary operation through weight nine, including nonvacuum outputs, source reassociation, the upper BV term, normal/collision corners and the common composition domain. Derive the physical braid/null parameter and the permitted stress correction from that map. The deciding tests are the actual two-stress/endpoint insertion, the pre-existing \(b_{\mathrm{nat}}=3/4\) requirement and the marked level-two null; a matched central scalar pole alone does not determine them.

question.title: Independent bulk observables and boundary generation
question.text:
Algebraic bulk and boundary models provide inputs to the physical comparison. The independently defined bulk action, unit preparation and full operation-valued annulus identity remain required; a bare extension algebra does not determine the additional coupling data.

In a fixed perturbative Einstein–Cartan sector, with real form, invertible-coframe neighbourhood, boundary polarization and renormalization prescribed independently, construct the unital supported bulk action \(\beta:F_{\mathrm{bulk}}\to Z(\mathcal C_\partial)\) and a boundary-to-bulk map \(a:H\to F_{\mathrm{bulk}}\). Define the physical actor category and its generation theorem on the same supported domains.

known.title: A full annulus identity supplies the inverse
known.text: Let \(F,Z\) be unital associative algebra objects, \(\beta:F\to Z\) a unital algebra map and \(H\) a left \(Z\)-module, with morphisms \(a:H\to F\) and \(\sigma:\mathbf1\to H\). Assume the following identities hold as morphisms: \(a(\beta(f)\cap x)=f\,a(x)\), \(a(\sigma)=1\), and \(\beta a(z\cap x)=z\,\beta a(x)\). Then \(s(z)=a(z\cap\sigma)\) is a two-sided inverse to \(\beta\). The further identity \(\lambda_{\mathrm{bulk}}a=\operatorname{tr}\) gives the stated trace comparison. Unit-hitting, a perfect pairing or the scalar trace of the annulus alone does not imply its operation-valued identity. The criterion presupposes the native maps and their domains.

question.text: For real three-dimensional gravity or for the specified sourced solid-torus theory, choose an independent physical cap and a spatial cut. Remove the two cutoffs independently and prove the spatial sewing identity. The independent harmonic disk supplies two finite free examples. On a nonflat solid-torus meridian, one- and five-mode quantum measures also exist. For compact Ward perturbations on opposite sides of the cut, compare the connected mixed derivatives of the logarithms of the sewn and whole-filling amplitudes at a common scale, then remove the regulators. The product of disjoint test planes has zero connected derivative. The propagating fields and their ghost partners can still contribute.

known.title: The scalar period and formal Ward functional already exist

For the separate angular witness, take \(q=e^{-L}>0\), \(L>0\), \(\omega\in(2\pi/L)\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\), \(e=z\exp(i\omega\log r)\), and \(\psi=(2\pi L)^{-1/2}r^{-2}\). This witness does not assert the same formula for an arbitrary complex twist, and the scalar period results do not construct the full state map.
