known.title: Elliptic current maps include a controlled field collar
known.text: Independent graph-current maps, sixteen compact histories on their stated carrier and the original field-normal collar are constructed with their anchors and outputs. The supported-prefix, earlier-pair-prefix and triangular histories have actual point-current limits; their stated bare fourth moments and restricted zero-trace results remain distinct. A weight of degree \(d\) on the primitive before Green gives these three histories the point-order bound \(4+J+q-d\) at field and kernel jet order \(J\) and coefficient order \(q\). For the zero-jet triangular product, keep the first and third pairs at their second-input anchors and weight the primitive by \(w_1\) before applying Green. Separate the transverse point current \(c_{U-V}\). The remaining bare \(\alpha\) current has variables \(u=U=V\), the middle normal \(w\), and the third central normal \(x\). Its moment on \(u_2^2x_1\) is negative at both middle-pair anchors, one on the compact partner and one on the Green primitive. This test is independent of \(w\), so the moment survives integration in \(w\). Matched within-pair auxiliary scales give a zero summed four-field limit and the specified chosen six-field history. Four independent widths can instead give different summed point limits. The original central contraction compares available trace-zero point values by explicit primitives and branch prisms, retaining the full coefficient differential. These current statements do not close the fixed lower marking or make a nonzero point value an \(H_3\) obstruction.

known.title: The native unit and full polynomial matrix are fixed
known.text: Direct evaluation of the native relative generator, tangent matrix and signed normal projection gives the pure retained unit \(C_q\,1_U1_x1_q\), with \(C_q=C\), followed by \(g_q^{\mathrm{nat}}(C_q)=c_q\). In the named normalized incoming and root/central bases, the chain is \(C^2 1_v1_w\mapsto C^2C_q1_U1_x1_q\mapsto C^21_U1_xc_q\), so \(\kappa_{\mathrm{unit}}=1\) in the compared basis. The original root constant, central density, contact current and all fibre and anchor factors remain separately typed. On the complete finite independent-\(q\) polynomial, exterior and jet complex, the actual forward maps obey \(g_q^{\mathrm{nat}}I_q=\rho_qp_q\), including the independent coefficient differential. The full physical-jet and exterior Taylor matrix therefore fixes both the unreduced contact \(C^2b_jI_qL_j\) and its compared value \(C^2b_j\rho_qp_qL_j\). With the same native matrix, q recipient, labelled frames and retained contraction in the same order, the polynomial and normalized mixed presentations agree coefficientwise, including every finite coefficient of their transferred source. Different sections retain their radial bridge, and different homotopy orders retain their actual prism.

known.title: The protected empty-history source coefficient vanishes
known.text: At the empty matching, one protected \(\mu(U-V)\) coefficient makes both ordered selected homotopy inputs smooth strong-current q families. The original fixed-order full normal word is separately defined on its generated finite current stages and has zero projection on the complete selected row. On the literal normalized mixed carrier, with identity inclusion on the common unreduced retained factor, both terms of the original first source coefficient vanish: \(S_1=-g_N(\delta_N\mathsf w+\iota h_P\delta_Pf_P)=0\). The q-first comparison and fixed-order projection are evaluated separately; their order-comparison cochains are not individually declared zero. Its first source path under the old endpoint, the compact residual \((A_\epsilon i_q-E_\epsilon)p_q\), and the original \(t_0\) remain to be compared.

known.title: Localization has explicit conditional extension tests
known.text: Given actual old localization maps and an enlarged ambient primitive with the exact old restriction, the relative mapping cylinder has explicit rows preserving both old maps. Pullback to the enlarged current carrier requires an actual continuous graded retraction or a separate descent argument. Let \(e:F\twoheadrightarrow D_{\mathrm{cur}}\) be the cochain evaluation, assume \(q\Lambda_F\) already factors through \(e\), and require \(U_F=q\Lambda_F-\partial W_F\). Then simultaneous descent is exactly \(W_F(\ker e)=0\) in the original full-intersection quotient, with the actual quotient-topology bounds. For an independently supplied endpoint \(u_*:D\to O_Z[-1]\) satisfying \(\partial u_*=qc\) and \(u_*i=u_L\), and an actual graded extension \(\widetilde W_L\) of \(w_L\) on this same enlarged carrier with the required finite bounds, the remaining extension class is \([q\Lambda-u_*-\partial\widetilde W_L]\in H^{-1}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(D/L,O_Z)\). These premises do not supply the original maps' enlarged-domain identification or evaluate that class. For prescribed old maps that commute with restriction and are graded-linear over smooth base Dolbeault forms on the same retained tuple, the explicit extension \(E_rz=(-1)^rM_Uz_V-(-1)^rM_Vz_U-M_UM_Vz_0\) descends to the original quotient \(O_Z\), preserves old restrictions and commutes with the full Hom differential. It retains both proper-root defects and finite normal moments. An actual smooth-current overlap disproves a proposed rule that would kill the new exterior-pattern presentation while fixing its equal smooth-multiplier presentation. The original independently prescribed localization maps have not been identified with the required module maps.

known.title: A second contraction isolates the original compact marking
known.text:
Put \(R=Aj_q-E\) for the closed difference of the two maps to the common recipient. First contract the \(q\) coordinate, then the root and central coordinates. The two contraction identities give
\[
A\delta_u-E\delta_c=\partial\mathcal L+\gamma g_r\delta_c,\qquad
\mathcal L=AH_q\delta_u+Rh_r\delta_c,\qquad \gamma=Rj_r.
\]
Indeed \(\partial(Rh_r\delta_c)=R(1-j_rg_r)\delta_c\) by the graded product rule. The differential is the full Hom differential, including precomposition with the source differential. On the unit the primitive retains both root and central homotopy terms, the external \(q\) factor and the full \(q\) primitive. The displayed primitive has boundary \(A\delta_u-E\delta_c\) precisely when \(\gamma g_r\delta_c=0\). Its value for the original compact output remains open.
hypotheses: On the actual common domain use degree-zero cochain maps \(A:N\to\mathcal Y\) and \(E:J_q\to\mathcal Y\). If the recipients differ, include their specified forward maps into \(\mathcal Y\). The odd contact maps \(\delta_u,\delta_c=g_q\delta_u\) are closed of degree one. The closed sections and projections and their degree-minus-one homotopies satisfy \(\partial H_q=1-j_qg_q\), \(g_qj_q=1\) and \(\partial h_r=1-j_rg_r\), with the required coherences on the actual diagram. The [compact comparison](#ch09-compact-comparison-and-prescribed-lower-homotopies) computes the two Hom boundaries on this domain.
Root and central support do not identify the polynomial scalar q section with the supported-current section. The original gamma value, compact exit and original graph binding remain unevaluated.

known.title: Genuine unit and s inputs and all stated finite jets enter the normal words
known.text: The original protected coefficients and finite old-U, selected-field and root jets have explicit genuine unit/s seed rows and full coefficient differential. Finite moment transfer and the original jet maps bind those seeds continuously to the unchanged normal/prism words on actual-current presentation quotients.
hypotheses: Scalar unit/s rows are not manufactured by differentiating eta, and input derivatives are not commuted through later projections.
This supplies input domains and bounds, not new projected values, a stronger horizontal identity, the old cylinder or compact exit.

known.title: All finite own-normal jets have full paired-prefix moment polynomials
known.text: For the original four-supported family with widths \((r,r;s,s)\), every finite own-normal jet has a physical moment polynomial of order at most \(J+2\), with bounded continuous coefficients on the compactified ratio interval. The full current remainder is \(O_{\mathcal D'}(m(1+|\log m|))\), uniformly in the ratio at fixed jet stage, and endpoint coefficients are actual regulated-moment limits.
hypotheses: Narrow-pair derivatives move by exact inverse Leibniz identities before reduced Green estimates. Keep full physical forms, central shear and both output colours.
The theorem controls two paired widths, not four independent widths. A limit uses a convergent ratio; otherwise the asymptotic retains the ratio parameter.
The bare trace is zero, but common normal-dependent multipliers use the full Taylor rule and may change it.

known.title: The paired prefix and weighted last collar compose in their prescribed order
known.text: The displayed six-input word first forms the paired-width prefix and then takes the original common-width last collar. The full angular matrix gives point order at most \(4+J_4+|b|+|e|+|q|-d\), with negative order zero. Positive old-root Taylor signs, protected reflection, physical central shear and every original native factor remain.
hypotheses: Finite source/state jets and degrees are fixed, with bounded required smooth spectator seminorms.
Uniform collar convergence concerns the already formed prefix family; the approximation error is not uniform while the collar shrinks.
No independent-width family, new original source arrow, old-cylinder or compact-exit identification is supplied.

known.title: The actual graph-source image has zero projected polynomial-homotopy term
known.text: Unique finite normal moments taken before the original polynomial section identify the actual graph-source image and preserve the remaining-field section. On that image, the all-jet field map is \(g_{N,*}\iota i_{\rm rem}=1_{G_{34}}\otimes p_*\). With the identical retained contraction and order, \(p_*k_*=0\) therefore gives \(g_{N,*}\iota h_P\delta_Pf_P=0\).
hypotheses: The \(C^2\) normalization ratio and fresh unreduced \(I_q\) remain separate; finite-current domains are established before applying the side condition.
The unprojected term is not declared zero and the larger presentation envelope is not the original polynomial-source image.

The local prism between the two specified retractions and one old incidence are determined at zero old jet and fixed new anchor. The other source term, unsupported old cylinder, eight-term compact evaluation and full fixed-lower attachment remain open. [The lifted root-first prism and its old incidence edge](#s-elliptic-root-first-prism).

questions.title: Comparing the critical Hall product with the field product

question.title: Comparing the critical Hall product with the field product
question.text:
The completed critical Hall endpoint has a formal recipient with its actual markings, and all-charge ambient maps, charged collisions and ordered-to-divisor descent are constructed. The full charge-two normalization square and typed operation comparison remain.

Construct the incoming tensor comparison and a supported homotopy
\[\Theta_{n+1}m^{\mathrm{crit}}_{1,n}-m^{\mathrm{field}}_{1,n}(\theta_1\otimes\Theta_n)=dH_{1,n}+H_{1,n}d\]
for the actual framed/unframed endpoints, moment-graph Gysin map and proper flag forgetting. Extend it through charge composition and the \(13|2\), \(13|24\) incidence complexes. The first test is the full charge-two normalization square on \(Z=\{uD=0\}\): retain both branches with coefficient \(+1\), the collapsed-branch compact trace and Thom class, and the intersection attachment. Identify the geometric input for the [resolved fourth-jet lift](#atlas-c-co-05), or construct its cubic representative directly on the flag. Recover the marked geometric cubic chain, its degree-minus-one endpoint and the field coefficient \(2c q^3\beta^{-3}u^{-3}e_1\,du\), where \(c=t_1t_2(t_1+t_2)\); no level or \(c\) is inverted.

questions.why: This would turn the geometric Hall construction into a comparison of actual singular field operations. All-charge proper descent and module fusion could then be tested against that map. Spectral shuffle formulas and costalk ranks alone do not identify the critical flag operation.

known.title: The completed endpoint has a precise admissible recipient
known.text: A normalized coefficient-linear projection from the full tangent completion to the localized polynomial recipient is impossible. A formal recipient exists, and the exceptional graph after completed point realization retains both odd actions and both branches. Independent supported fields exist with only the final tangent coefficient made formal. The ambient all-charge \(\Theta_n\), charged collisions, zero-charge insertions and normalized ordered-to-divisor descent are separate existing constructions. The first original interface is over \(B[q]/(q^4)\), \(B=\mathbb C[t_1,t_2,\beta,\beta^{-1},\kappa]\), with moment differential \(d\eta=(x_1-x_2)D_0\), \(d\chi=0\). The nonzero cubic field representative lifts from a resolution of the auxiliary fourth jet over this moment algebra. The two equations of the jet are null-homotopic there and the closed odd direction acts by exterior multiplication. [The local lift](#atlas-c-co-05). Its nonlocal affine creation marking is not silently replaced by the cyclic completed formulation.

questions.title: An independent field dual and module tensor on a surface

question.title: An independent field dual and module tensor on a surface
question.text:
The paired cut coalgebra and its pro-perfect transposed dual have an algebraic comparison. An independent singular-field or internal-line realization with the same cuts and unit data remains required.

For the paired coalgebra \(C\) on \(\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}\) and \(A=\Omega_{\mathrm{cut}}C\), independently define the singular-field or internal-line dual, its coefficient extraction, evaluation and module tensor. Compare it with \(A_\sharp^!=(B_{\mathrm{cut}}A)^\sharp\simeq C^\sharp\), preserving both colours, translations, grades, level, every cut, both binary orders and the distinct empty unit and occupied vacuum. First compare the unary dual shifts and occupied-vacuum projection, then binary evaluation in both orders and the \(13|2\) contact. Retain the whole pro-perfect diagram and its transposed cut tensor; an ordinary inverse limit is not the proved dual.

questions.why: This would give an independent associative chiral Koszul-duality bridge in complex dimension two, including a native tensor on modules. It would provide a higher-dimensional line input beyond a tensor defined by transport from coefficient duality.

known.title: The independent dual remains beyond the free realization
known.text: For finite-dimensional degree-zero \(V\), fixed volume on \(\mathbb A^2\), \(R=\mathbb C[\hbar,\kappa]\) and \(\lambda=\hbar\kappa\), the compact smooth realization of the paired coalgebra is factorization-equivalent to the independently defined free theory, with all finite marked insertion diagrams and quantum operation cells. The coefficient dual and its inverse also exist. The five-position comparison is already \(1+H_5\), with inverse \(1-H_5\) and \(H_5^2=0\). The nonzero fixed-binary ternary contact \(-\lambda^3(8\pi^2)^{-1}D_{uv}\delta_4\) is carried by that realization; it is a test for the new independent dual, not an obstruction to the existing equivalence. The independent dual and its module tensor are still separate constructions.

questions.title: An interacting bulk for cubic surface currents

question.title: An interacting bulk for cubic surface currents
question.text:
Polynomial higher currents and regular paired Gaussian or abelian pushforwards are available. The interacting bulk must carry the nonzero ternary central operation through its actual supported boundary action.

Construct an independent mixed theory on \(\mathbb R_{\ge0}\times\mathbb C^2\), with bulk fields, interaction and boundary condition, whose boundary operations identify with the cubic-current factorization algebra
\[(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathrm{sm}}(\Omega_c^{0,*}\otimes\mathfrak g[1]),\bar\partial+d_{\mathrm{CE}}+\ell J_X(\theta)),\quad J_X(\theta)(a,b,c)=\int_X\theta(a,\partial b,\partial c).\]
Carry the ternary central operation through the actual supported boundary/trace map, retaining vacuum, compact-support tensors and incidence faces. For the rank-one abelian current with unit cubic form, the ordered residue of \(z_1^{-1}z_2^{-1}dz_1\wedge dz_2\) is \(+1\). Thus the universal bracket \(\ell_3(e_{-1,-1},z_1,z_2)\) equals the central generator \(K_{\mathrm{cen}}\). After specialization \(K_{\mathrm{cen}}\mapsto\ell\,\mathbf1\), the boundary trace must carry the vacuum coefficient \(+\ell\), which is zero at level zero and two at level two. Then construct the quantum group acting on this bulk's lines.

questions.why: This would supply a non-Gaussian higher-dimensional bulk–boundary example with an operation invisible to binary central tests. Its line theory could be compared with the cubic coefficient and field constructions; general fusion and quantum states would still require their own maps.

known.title: The internal native cubic comparison is known
known.text: For the stated retained-point algebraic presentation over a commutative complex algebra, a full filtered vacuum-preserving native morphism over unary \(A\) exists exactly when \(A\) is a Lie map and \(\ell\theta=\ell' A^*\theta\); \(\operatorname{Sym}(A)\) gives sufficiency. This includes the specified collisions, vacancies, partitions and mixed coherences. The proof uses finite total particle, central and Koszul-weight stages, followed by their polynomial colimit. Its nonzero ternary central symbol, and the separate mode detector, do not construct the independent physical bulk or its boundary/trace composite.

questions.title: A continuous Hamiltonian comparison preserving product and bracket

question.title: A continuous Hamiltonian comparison preserving product and bracket
question.text:
The strict Schouten-source arity-four comparison fails in the stated continuous class. Finite primitives and sources with essential higher Lie operations remain possible; full product, bracket and mixed compatibility is the target.

On the original continuous Hamiltonian carrier, choose an admitted unary comparison and construct normalized product, bracket and mixed homotopies \(H,U,V\) solving \(\partial H=M\), \(\partial U=G\), \(\partial V=R_{\mathrm{mix}}\). Retain the independently defined wedge and Schouten bracket, native cup and braces, the same lower homotopies in the mixed equation, and every nonclosed-input value. Extend them to one \(E_2\) model with a coherent inverse and the essential higher source Lie operations. For the identity-wheel branch, the first deciding component is the actual global continuous Chevalley class \([\zeta\wedge\omega_3]\); finite-weight primitives must extend with the required bounds at every quotient.

questions.why: This would promote a cochain equivalence to an equivalence of the independently prescribed quantum operations. A full admitted-change obstruction would instead determine which source structure must change. One finite primitive cannot decide that alternative.

known.title: A strict Lie source fails, while essential higher operations survive
known.text: For \(\mathfrak h=\prod_{j\ge2}\operatorname{Sym}^j(\mathbb Cu+\mathbb Cv)\), the stated inverse-limit/finite-output continuous cochains over \(\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\) admit no normalized jointly continuous Taylor maps through arity four from the strict Schouten source with first term HKR. The detecting coefficient is \(1/3\); reflected transfer has odd brackets zero and a forced nonzero quartic class with coefficient \(2/3\). This does not exclude an \(E_2\) source with the same binary wedge and Schouten operations and higher Lie data. Existing finite quotient and weight-fifteen product primitives remain valid. No PBW-degree completion or \(\hbar\)-inversion is part of this carrier.

questions.title: Chiral operations on integral arithmetic coefficients

question.title: Chiral operations on integral arithmetic coefficients
question.text:
Integral normal coefficients, height-raising Frobenius, congruence tubes and their typed evaluations are established. A common full chiral/arithmetic operation diagram and independently defined trace comparison remain to be constructed.

For independently specified integral chiral and arithmetic sheaf data, construct \(\Phi:B_{\mathrm{ord}}(A_{\mathrm{ch}})\to C(\mathcal F)\) on a common full ordered coefficient diagram. Intertwine normal operations, mixed and nonconsecutive collisions, Frobenius with its actual variance and height change, exchange, local vacuum, both empty cut placements and higher coherences. Independently define the integrable trace domains and prove \(t_{\mathrm{ch}}=t_{\mathrm{ar}}\Phi\). The first collision/Frobenius square must retain the height-two normal coefficient of \(x_0^p+px_1-x_0\), the punctured residue of \((z+pt)^{-1}\), and the \(13|2\) branch. Scalar arithmetic evaluation loses these tests.

questions.why: This would make arithmetic operations a native instance of the chiral coefficient and fusion programme, with a typed trace comparison. It goes beyond an equality of counts or determinants. Positive states and general descent would still require additional theorems.

known.title: Normal coefficients and Frobenius already have integral comparisons
known.text: For every prime, finite height and finite ordered position set, the integral comparison \(J:C_R(f;g)\to C_B(f;g)\) preserves the declared divided-normal coactions and height-raising Frobenius; its finite weighted evaluations satisfy \(T_BJ=T_R\). Forest-supported residue conclusions require \(g=1\). Separately, arithmetic-point-labelled congruence tubes have a complete groupoid nerve, balanced completed tensors, faithful normal-distribution action and correctly twisted Frobenius squares over the stated \(p\)-complete, \(p\)-torsionfree delta algebras, including \(p=2\). These are substantial coefficient constructions with distinct recipients. Their supported evaluations are not an unrestricted cyclic trace on the normal-operator algebra.

questions.title: A positive geometric realization of the full Weil functional

question.title: A positive geometric realization of the full Weil functional
question.text:
The full functional has a trace representative, while the positive critical multiplicity layers have an explicit nonreal remainder. A cyclic vector state is distinct from the counting trace.

Construct an independently defined positive arithmetic trace representation on the full common test domain, satisfying \(\pi(f^**f)=\pi(f)^*\pi(f)\) and \(\operatorname{Tr}\pi(g)=L(g)\) for the complete Weil functional. Retain both polar terms, the archimedean term and every prime power in both orientations. Compare its supported products and local field operations, and distinguish the counting trace from a prepared vector state. The first tests are the actual involution and counting weight on the same trace ideal, followed by the full remainder identity for any proposed critical-spectrum replacement. Finite positive moment matrices do not establish this equality.

questions.why: This would identify the full arithmetic functional with an ordinary positive trace representation and compatible operations. Its counting trace must still be distinguished from a normalized finite functional or a prepared vector state; omitting part of the divisor changes the question.

known.title: The full trace and a positive critical part are separately constructed
known.text: A trace-class chain representative homotopic to native convolution has quotient trace and supertrace equal to the complete Weil functional on the specified exponentially weighted test steps. Separately, ordinary-positive critical multiplicity layers have a self-adjoint generator and inverse moments of every order \(m\ge2\). Their exact deficit is \(L(g)-\operatorname{Tr}\pi_{\mathrm{crit}}(g)=\sum_{w\in Z\setminus\mathbb R}m_wh_g(w)\). Vanishing of this remainder for all tests remains unproved. Gaussian creators, an invariant cyclic vector and a formal nonlocal field algebra also exist; their bottom-corner operator shows that the full counting trace differs from the vector state. These facts neither prove full positivity nor exclude every other local positive recipient.

questions.title: The compact reduced Hall source and its primitive algebra

question.title: The compact reduced Hall source and its primitive algebra
question.text:
The spherical source has all-length paired recipients, classical coefficient arrows and common-total flag refinements; local mixed reduced–ordinary flags and a common real positive algebra are also available. The stronger global derived and mixed-orientation comparison remains. The specified compact BPS and minimal Gritsenko–Nikulin sources differ in imaginary parity spaces, so primitive recognition needs an independently constructed map.

For compact mixed-character sheaves on \(X=S\times E\), integrate the trace–Atiyah cosection to a shifted moment map \(\mu_\gamma:\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{cpt}}_\gamma\to\mathfrak e^*[-1]\). Orient its derived zero fibre modulo \(E\), and construct reduced mixed/ordinary extension and flag maps. Then build the actual parity-resolved primitive presentation map from the prescribed Borcherds algebra, with the invariant form, exact relation kernel, generation, PBW and compatible completions. First transport the full one-mixed/two-ordinary flag square beyond its product neighbourhood, retaining repeated-block deformations and the endpoint \(Q_A\times_{BE}Q_B\). Primitive recognition must distinguish the first imaginary \(29|93\) parity space, not just its signed dimension.

questions.why: The compact Hall problem requires an oriented product and parity-resolved primitive brackets on the actual reduced coefficient spaces. A protected state would additionally have to yield the normalized modular section and its insertions.

known.title: Compact source constructions and the remaining global comparison
known.text: Choose a strictly unital comparison of the simultaneous cyclic minimal model for the common-reduced-Hilbert-polynomial K3 triple with its Dolbeault category over \(\mathbb C^3\). The ordinary constructible-function composition algebras generated by the three simple classes are isomorphic by their simple indicators. At each finite nilpotence bound the algebraic families identify the actual reduced flag varieties over reduced bases, their subquotients and their forgetting and regrouping maps. At every positive spherical length, the four derived fibres supply an algebraic paired recipient with closed \((-1)\)-shifted form, global classical coefficient arrows and common-total flag refinements retaining intermediate lifting gerbes. On the volume-preserving Kummer product neighbourhood, both reduced–ordinary orders agree on the full one-mixed/two-ordinary flag, with zero binary index shift, at the declared small charges and fixed slope-zero domain. These constructions are stronger than a numerical integral, which can vanish while the coefficient is nonzero. They leave the global derived ambient comparison, mixed reduction beyond that neighbourhood and the prescribed compact orientation/descent conditions unresolved; opposite intermediate moments cannot be erased by separate binary reductions.

known.title: The specified K3 BPS source has different imaginary roots
known.text: The specified K3 BPS Lie algebra is not the specified minimal Gritsenko–Nikulin algebra under the stated category, charge map and Euler pairing. The first null degree has \(24|0\) versus \(10|0\), and the first timelike degree \(25650|0\) versus \(29|93\). Their specified real positive Kac–Moody algebra is common. This excludes that identification; it leaves a different reduced compact source, a derived modification or a smaller common presentation open.

questions.title: Compact states and the calibrated Igusa section

question.title: Compact states and their map to the geometric Igusa section
question.text: Compare reduced compact coefficients with independently defined protected or chiral state complexes, preserving the unit, charge, cyclic structure, preparation and sewing. At the section class of an elliptic K3, recover the untraced cubic and its values on vectors orthogonal to the section and fibre. Among unital commutative first-order products cyclic for the fixed rational pairing, the fibre-marked row and all first multiplication traces leave a 1,750-dimensional ambiguity. In a different geometry let \(j:\mathcal M_2\to\mathcal A_2\) be the Jacobian map on smooth complex genus-two curves and \(e_5\) the evaluation of fifth powers of holomorphic differentials on the six Weierstrass points. Its determinant satisfies \(\det(e_5)^2=2^{32}\pi^{20}j^*\Xi\) for the product-normalized weight-ten section \(\Xi\). Construct the map from the compact state geometry to this modular geometry, identify the determinant lines and their signs, and recover the vacuum scalar from an actual preparation.

questions.why: The genus-two determinant gives a geometric section with specified scalar and sign conventions. A compact-state comparison must identify its own line and state with this independently defined section and reproduce inserted amplitudes under sewing.

known.title: The state comparison must retain the untraced cubic
known.text: On full rational K3 cohomology, the reduced section cubic is \(\mu(a,b)=\eta(a,C)\eta(b,C)C\). A distinct normalized cyclic deformation has the same fibre-marked operator and all displayed multiplication-correction traces but a different Hochschild class: for \(q(u,v)=1\) in the second hyperbolic plane, its paired cubic on \((v,v,v)\) is one, while the genuine section cubic is zero. Conditional on the full protected-state datum, the normalized trace is \(\Delta_5^{-2}\); the separate Oberdieck–Pandharipande scalar convention is \(-4096\Delta_5^{-2}\). The geometric Pfaffian conclusion additionally needs the actual line/section datum. The Weierstrass determinant on smooth genus-two Jacobians has an explicit normalized section identity. The integral map and line identification from the compact protected state to that geometry are open.

questions.title: The finite-rank mixed-string bulk and brane operations

question.title: The finite-rank mixed-string bulk and brane operations
question.text:
Continuous stable coordinates and the typed deformation equations are available. The permitted comparison uses the actual deformed product; a defect against an undeformed target does not decide it.

Construct the continuous filtered twisted-formality/PBW comparison for the independently defined mixed holomorphic–topological bulk and finite-rank brane theory, with HKR linear term, the actual deformed product, and compatible coordinate, window and Roos transitions. Construct its mixed action, Hochschild centrality and QME counterterms in the same allowed local complex, through all scale, support and scalar-contact arrows. The first test is the explicit two-dimensional affine-Lie chain equation with the actual deformed product, followed by its transition homotopy and first mixed-action curvature. A fixed undeformed-target defect does not exclude the permitted twisted comparison.

questions.why: This would identify the physical mixed bulk with the brane operations at finite rank, beyond a stable scalar trace coordinate. It would give a genuine bulk–brane reconstruction on the declared continuous carrier. Global descent and prepared quantum states would remain additional work.

known.title: From continuous coordinates to the physical action
known.text: The declared continuous coordinate construction retains stable trace and the regraded Chevalley/polyvector comparison. The typed deformation complexes specify the missing mixed-action, centrality, transition and QME equations. Their hypotheses are not already constructed physical maps. Retain the Tate/pro-Matlis or specified weighted completion, continuous bracket and kernel tensor, diagonal Casimir and coordinate projections; Taylor ideals are not generally Poisson ideals. The Rees/PBW and loop parameters differ, and RG acts nonlinearly. Objectwise primitives therefore require compatible transition homotopies before they define the full diagram.

questions.title: Interacting curve holography and its physical source

question.title: Interacting curve holography and its physical source
question.text:
Local open and closed fields, normal disks and relative scalar constructions are available. The unchanged interval and point sources prepare different rotor states, so the actual physical source correction must be realized.

For a planar oper with fixed polar and normalization data, construct the coupled closed-string BV theory and its cyclic brane source as a scalar variational functional on the original normal–polar fields. Represent its full mixed derivatives and Green/boundary terms, and compare BF-gauged singlet observables with independently renormalized sourced closed-string observables, preserving collisions, defects and sewn states. First evaluate the full mixed master residual for the physically selected source plus regular disk, including the two-nullary-output scalar. In the two-site \(SU(2)\) rotor sector, calculate the resulting Hamiltonian insertion \(C_{\mathrm{native}}\): the necessary first-order state test is that \(C_{\mathrm{native}}-Q\) be scalar on the prescribed graph domain. Then test the two-source corner and cap.

questions.why: This would turn the planar geometric and renormalization dictionary into a comparison of local correlations and brane amplitudes, with the same physical source measuring the same observable. The first source correction removes a concrete state mismatch; it does not by itself establish finite-source equivalence or sewing.

known.title: Physical realization of the supported disk data
known.text: Independent local open and closed fields, finite normal descendants, normal-valued ordered disks, scalar relative counterterms, cyclic profile actions and a regular cohomological section are available. The scalar brane calibration is \(\lambda_f=Ng_c^2/(8\pi^3\hbar)\). These constructions do not identify the auxiliary regular momenta with the physical boundary fields or prove the full coupled mixed equation. The free smooth annulus primitive has a nonzero matrix Leibniz defect, so a unary extension alone cannot provide the interacting product comparison. The enriched Wilson tensor must be over \(\mathcal O_\Sigma[[\lambda]]\).

known.title: The unchanged interval and point sources prepare different states
known.text: For the full periodic two-site \(SU(2)\) rotor at zero chemical potential, equal marked intervals of length \(\pi\), fixed reference and any positive heat parameters, the same constant smooth source has interval response \(\rho_I'(0)=0\) and point response \(\rho_P'(0)=-\beta Q\rho_0\ne0\). The bounded observable \(Q/(1+Q^2)\) detects the difference. Among symmetric insertions bounded by the \((K_0+1)^{1/2}\) graph norm, the point response is obtained exactly when \(C=Q+c_0I\). No bounded insertion supplies it, and scalar energy shifts cancel under state normalization. The physical realization of this unbounded correction remains to be constructed.

orientation.title: Couplings, fusion and the state of a filling
explanation: For a line coupled to a chiral field, the positions at which operations act enter their composition. Take two distinct labelled points on a curve. In the word \(12\) the only cut into two nonempty words is \(1|2\). The ordered collision atlas also admits \(2|1\). The consecutive-cut product and the product summing over all ordered decompositions therefore use different input maps. A Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral Lie bracket takes its value on the diagonal and obeys Jacobi. An associative chiral algebra retains the ordered products and their higher associativity relations. [The two configuration products](#ch12-associative-products-on-configurations).

The bar construction records these products and homotopies as a coalgebra. For a connected augmented word algebra a word on \(n\) positions has at most \(n\) nonempty blocks. Bar and cobar therefore stabilise in each arity, even for unbounded coefficient complexes. In the composite, changing the first gap in a flattened word contracts the terms with more than one letter. Recovering a second, independently given boundary algebra requires transposing the coproduct into a product of the correct variance and comparing the resulting operations with those on that boundary. [The finite cut filtration and its contraction](#ch05-ordered-cuts-give-a-finite-geometric-bar-construction).

Fusion joins two lines. In the Ising model each channel has a simple label at each end, drawn from the vacuum, the fermion and the spin. Two channels can be joined only when the labels at their meeting end match. The exact faithful tensor functor to bimodules over \(\mathbb C^3\) remembers those ends. The unit coproduct of the reconstructed weak Hopf algebra projects onto matching pairs. A marked half-turn measures a further datum. The ratio of the two spin exchange phases is \(i\) in the given orientation and \(-i\) after reflection. [Fusion channels and the marked half-turn](#ch12-ising-half-turn).

In a compactly generated sector, fusion preserving colimits in each input can be recovered from its value on generating probes together with the actions of their endomorphisms. Two one-dimensional kernels illustrate why the actions matter. The same projection on the second input acts as the identity on one kernel and as zero on the other. Substitution of operations then uses derived tensor product of the kernels over the intermediate algebra. A comparison across a defect must identify these actions as well as the supports and domains of the products it transports. [The calculation with two idempotents](#essay-operation-kernels) and [the operation-kernel proposition](#ch17-proposition-operation-kernels).

A filling assigns a functional or a vector to the boundary. On the harmonic disk its action, sources and integration measure determine the mixed moments of distinct modes. Normalising those moments discards a scalar. To compare absolute amplitudes, compute the empty-insertion amplitude in the independent filling and identify its line across the cut. A gravity reconstruction must in addition exhibit its own spatial cut, fields, probes and sewing operation. [Comparison at a filling](#states-lines-and-caps).

programmeFamilies.title: Fields and their representations
programmeFamilies.text: Free currents, affine and Virasoro systems, \(W\)-algebras and quantum vertex algebras test duality, module localization, exchange and fusion on concrete algebraic or completed carriers.

programmeFamilies.title: Geometry, Hall algebras and branes
programmeFamilies.text: Hall correspondences, Hilbert schemes, matrix complexes, Miura algebras, compact K3 coefficients and symplectic examples have substantial algebraic and geometric theories. Their further comparisons must preserve proper operations, parity, orientation and untraced states.

programmeFamilies.title: Bulk observables, defects and gravity
programmeFamilies.text: Celestial currents, higher-dimensional gauge theories and gravity require independently constructed bulk actions, line or surface operations, analytic sewing and source-dependent state preparation.

programmeFamilies.title: Arithmetic traces and integral coefficients
programmeFamilies.text: The arithmetic branch has continuous spectral duality, integral normal/Frobenius operations and a geometric representative of the complete Weil trace. It asks for a common proper trace domain, further native field comparisons and signed positivity on every whole test window.

readerGuidance.title: Choose a physical operation
readerGuidance.text: Compare the same operation on one probe and on a pair. A [charged line](#row-heisenberg) gives a primary coefficient whose continuation detects winding. A [finite-base tensor product](#ch12-ising-half-turn) keeps the intermediate label, while [Hall composition](#ch15-extensions-and-the-reason-for-associativity) sums over flags of subobjects.

readerGuidance.title: Identify the coefficient space
readerGuidance.text: An algebraic direct sum, a fixed-precision quotient and an inverse limit admit different elements. Write down the first product and apply the next kernel to that actual output. Two radial expansions can agree on a common domain while a substitution on the larger completion is undefined. [Two expansions of the same current](#ch08-factorized-common-domain).

readerGuidance.title: Follow a collision
readerGuidance.text: A full twist measures transport around the diagonal. To extend a coefficient across the collision, specify its attachment to the link. Distinct images of this map give inequivalent four-ray extensions with the same stalk and costalk dimensions. [The projective line of attachments](#atlas-c-cl-05).

readerGuidance.title: Identify the state
readerGuidance.text: A vacuum in the field algebra supplies a local insertion. A cap evaluates a specified filling. On the disk the ray contraction cancels from the normalised law, but it remains in the unnormalised collar pairing. [The scalar disk and its collar](#ch11-harmonic-disk-and-collar) and [the ray norm](#ch11-neutral-ray-pair).
